Everything in the world had its destined course.
To the Demon Bird, Wipeng’s death was just as certain.
A Peak master who had reached an impressive realm for his age.
An outstanding swordsman whose practical sword technique justified the title Ghost Sword.
But that was all Wipeng was.
With enough effort and luck, he might reach Supreme Peak in ten or fifteen years.
That day would never come.
Meeting the Demon Bird in this gorge was proof that Heaven had already abandoned him.
Those who had yet to cross the wall, and those who had.
That was the difference between Peak and Supreme Peak.
*Become a ghost.
Live up to your title.*
Blood-red light flashed as the Demon Bird swung both swords.
The short sword in his left hand went for Cheol Mubaek, who was rushing to save his comrade.
The long sword in his right went for Wipeng, who met it with all his strength.
But the clash unfolded in a way the Demon Bird hadn’t expected.
*CRUNCH—KRRRRANG!*
A substantial recoil traveled up both sword blades.
The Demon Bird’s eyes widened at the dazzling sparks blooming where three different streams of energy met.
*What?*
He was more shaken than he could have imagined.
Cheol Mubaek and Wipeng—those young pups who hadn’t crossed the wall, prey who should have been no more than a meal—had stopped his strike.
With nothing more than their paltry Fist Energy and Sword Energy, they were holding out against Sword Force he had unleashed with all his strength.
*How?*
The Demon Bird was a born killer and hunter.
He knew better than anyone how far beneath him his prey stood, both in their enlightenment in martial arts and in the internal energy they held.
Yet the impossible was happening before his eyes.
A mere Peak master had met head-on the Force he’d swung with several *jiazi* of internal energy.
It was something that couldn’t happen—and shouldn’t.
*Cough.
Spurt.*
Blood mixed with bits of their innards poured from Cheol Mubaek’s and Wipeng’s split lips.
The Demon Bird stared, frozen in shock.
The two men bared their bloodied teeth and smiled.
They could barely hold out against the blood-red Force.
Cheol Mubaek’s snow-white gauntlet and Wipeng’s sword blade trembled beneath its overwhelming power.
Then the Demon Bird noticed the faint glow of their prized weapons, visible even through the thick blood, and remembered something he had briefly forgotten.
A Supreme Peak master’s Force could be resisted by something other than Force of the same kind.
*Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron...!*
The Demon Bird caught his breath.
How could he have known?
In all his long life, even he had never obtained a divine weapon like these.
Yet two Peak masters from remote Shanxi Province each held one.
Nor could he have guessed that the weapons he mistook for Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron were made from the bones of a spiritual creature that had guarded a river unseen for hundreds of years.
His moment of surprise gave someone who was still standing an opening.
*Hup!*
Wipeng wrung out every last bit of his strength and twisted his sword.
His wrist was already broken and his hand mangled, but he swallowed the blood rising from his severe Internal Injury and turned aside the energy bearing down on him.
*KRRRRUNCH!*
The long sword slid along the snow-white blade and drove into the ground.
Deep—driven by all the force behind it.
*Thud!*
Anger flared in the Demon Bird’s eyes as he recovered from his shock.
At that very instant—
*CRUNCH!*
Cheol Mubaek grabbed the short sword that had been slowly forcing his gauntlet back.
His hand closed around the Force shrouding its blade.
*Crack.
Krrrunch.*
Something broke with a sickening sound, and unbearable pain followed.
The irresistible power crushed the flesh inside his gauntlet and splintered his bones.
Without a divine weapon made from the Water God Dragon’s bones, both his hands would have vanished without a trace the moment they touched the Force.
But Cheol Mubaek did not let go.
The pain was too great even to groan.
His organs twisted under the immense energy, yet he held on to the blade with all his strength.
He remembered the great master who had taught him long ago, even without his arms.
And he waited for someone to kill the bastard in his stead, to do what he, an unworthy Disciple, could not.
At last, that wish reached someone’s sword.
*Shwaash.*
A sound so faint it raised goose bumps.
A flash shot forward like a bolt of lightning and descended toward the Demon Bird.

chapters.title: Chapter 962
paragraphs: In an instant split into ever smaller fragments, the Demon Bird realized he had only one choice left.
*Shwaa.*
A faint whistle of displaced air approached like a ghost and brushed his ear.
At the same time, the world slowed.
Everything was clear.
The shallow breaths of Wipeng and Cheol Mubaek, both suffering severe Internal Injuries. The drops of blood spilling from between their lips.
And then the Demon Bird finally released the two beloved swords he had been gripping tightly and turned around.
He kicked off the ground with all his strength and thrust both palms forward like a bolt of lightning.
*Fwoosh!*
Blood-red Force flashed around his hands.
The tremendous energy, enough to reduce even a boulder weighing ten thousand *geun* to dust in an instant, surged forward without resistance.
Toward the sea-blue Sword Energy falling over the Demon Bird’s head.
Toward the man who had brought that blade-sharp wave of Sword Energy crashing down.
Jin Mukyung.
The eyes of the young Sword Demon of the Jin Family of Taiyuan met those of an old fiend who had spent his life killing.
The two men could hardly have been less alike.
Not in the lives they had led, the eras they had been born into, or what they held in their hearts.
The young man had learned martial arts simply because he loved the sword. The old man had wielded one to kill.
The young man had wanted strength to restore his declining family.
The old man had craved strength because the stronger he became, the more people he could trample underfoot.

The young man was one of countless people who wanted no part of an age of chaos. The old man longed more than anyone for those bygone days when blood ran in rivers and corpses piled up like mountains.
The paths they had walked were different, as were the directions they would go from here.
Even now, the Sword Energy and palm force they hurled at each other sounded different.
*Shhk.*
The Sword Energy descended like a blue wave, or a single bolt of lightning, yet its sound was as faint as a child’s breath.
*RROOOAR!*
The enormous blood-red palm force roared like thunder.
And between those small differences lay a gulf as deep and wide as all the differences that had come before.
One crushed the wind. The other cut through it.
*Gooooom.*
A distant flash. Air seething with heat.
As the red and blue lights raced toward each other, a thought struck the Demon Bird.
Supreme Peak and Peak.
Perhaps the wall of enlightenment between Sword Energy Becoming Force and the level of injuring others with Sword Energy was not as high or imposing as he had thought.
*This is...*
Even amid the raging gale, the Demon Bird could see the blue light shining clearly.
That unwavering strike, descending at an angle along its destined path, was proof of all the enlightenment the young man had gained so far—and of his progress toward a new realm.
*Rumble.*
At last, the two immense forces met. They erased the wind.
They warped space.
And under pressure great enough to tear his body apart, Jin Mukyung closed his eyes.
It was a deep night, with even the moonlight dim. Once his sight was cut off, pitch-black darkness settled over him.
It was so familiar. Every bit of energy and sensation in his body surged and flowed into the sword in his hand.
He could see nothing, but he could feel it.
His opponent’s overwhelming power, ready to sweep everything away.
The openings in that ferocious, and therefore unstable, palm force.
*Yes.*
*There.*
As if entranced, Jin Mukyung brought his sword down. Blue light slipped between his closed eyelids, clearer than ever before.
A thousand times, ten thousand times—or dozens, hundreds of times more.
Hammer and cool it beyond counting, and even worthless scrap iron will one day become a fine sword.
A single drop of water can crack solid rock. A single thorn lodged in an elephant’s foot can bring it down.
Just as it did now.
*Shwaaaash.*
The Demon Bird saw it clearly.
A blue flash, so sharp it looked like a single thread, split his palm force from side to side. It was unbelievable.
And he marveled.
*Ah.*
Speed, power, trajectory.
All of it was dazzling. So perfect it sent a shiver through him.
That sharpness could no longer be called Sword Energy. The flash of a divine weapon cut through the blood-red Force and pressed on.
*Truly beautiful.*
The words never left his lips. The Demon Bird smiled brightly and reached both trembling hands toward the blue streak falling over his head.
*Shhk.*
That beautiful, dazzling wave was cold enough to make him shudder.
The world stopped.
No—everyone in it stopped moving.

The nomads who had kept fighting, not daring to interfere in the battle of a superior who was practically a tyrant. The Shanxi defenders who had been slowly tiring against the endless waves of troops.
Even Cheol Mubaek and Wipeng, who had watched everything from closer than anyone else on the battlefield, could do no more than cling to their fading consciousness.
*Shhk.*
The single, startlingly clear slicing sound from moments ago still rang in their ears.
Along with a question they couldn’t understand.
*What on earth...?*
*What just happened?*
The same thought crossed everyone’s mind.
Red and blue had flashed within a distant, swelling blaze of light. That was all.
Everyone on the battlefield had seen that dazzling light clearly, and at the same time, no one had seen a thing.
Now, only the two men standing a *jang* apart with their backs to each other could break the silence that had settled over the narrow gorge, thick with blood and corpses.
Jin Mukyung and the Demon Bird.
The Demon Bird and Jin Mukyung.

The old fiend, who had spent long years killing countless people, and the young Sword Demon, who had spent the past two years swinging a sword in pitch-black darkness, slowly turned to face each other.
*Splash.*
A heavy step sent blood spilling from a puddle. No one knew whose it was.
Soon, someone’s fresh blood filled the space it had left.
*Cough.*
Lips pressed tightly together parted. Like a cracked dam giving way, blood mixed with fragments of innards burst through the tiny gap.
*Splaaash!*
Dark red blood sprayed through the air and soaked the ground. Reflected in the refilled puddle was the young Sword Demon’s pallid face.
“No! Mukyung!”
*CLANG!*
At the desperate cry from somewhere far away, the clamor of steel began again.
Thinking of the familiar voice behind that cry, Jin Mukyung smiled faintly. The Demon Bird suddenly spoke to him.
“What was that strike?”
The question was far too short to contain everything he felt and wanted to know.
Jin Mukyung swallowed another surge of blood before answering.
“I don’t know either. I’ve never done it before.”
The Demon Bird gave a wry laugh.
He wasn’t mocking him. Those who stepped into a new realm in a moment of No-self, forgetting even themselves, always gave the same answer.
He had too, when he was young.
“Honest, at least.”
“Can’t help it. It’s true.”
“If only I could see that strike of yours one more time. Just once, before the end.”
“I’ll pass. I’ve seen enough of your face.”
The Demon Bird’s smile widened.
“Have you named that form?”
Jin Mukyung quietly shook his head.
What he had trained was a martial art. In a sense, it wasn’t one at all.
Only One Strike.
He had spent two years searching for a single path for his sword, and today, in this place, he had glimpsed its very edge.
He had never thought to give the form a name.
Not until the old monster in front of him brought it up.
“Blue Wave, Falling Bird.”
A blue wave surges, and a bird falls.
The Demon Bird murmured it like a line of poetry, then asked Jin Mukyung with unmistakable pride, “Well? Pretty good, isn’t it?”
“Hard to say. It’s kind of cheesy.”
“Oh.”
Disappointment spread across the Demon Bird’s face. Then Jin Mukyung went on, his voice calm.
“But I suppose I could get used to it.”
“Really? I knew you’d see it my way.”
The Demon Bird grinned from ear to ear.
He had no idea faint red lines were beginning to appear all over his body.
No—he was doing his best to pretend he hadn’t noticed.
“Heaven Shaking Sword, Jin Mukyung. Of the Jin Family of Taiyuan... Cough, you young Sword Demon.”
*Drip. Drip.*
Blood fell in scattered drops.
The Shanxi defenders rushing to save Jin Mukyung and the steppe fighters who had held them back, certain of their superior’s victory, stared wide-eyed at the Demon Bird.
The old fiend steadied himself as he swayed, his gaze fixed on Jin Mukyung alone.
“Kill. Kill, and kill again.”
His eyes and voice burned with the obsession he had kept all his life: murder.
“With the strike that cut me down. Everything that stands in your way. Every last thing. Guh. Every last...!”
*Slith.*
The Demon Bird never finished.
The red lines crossing his body, and the beads of blood swelling along them, finally burst in a magnificent explosion.
*FWOOSH!*
A fountain of blood surged upward, staining the air.
Everyone stared in shock as the Demon Bird collapsed like a rotten tree.
One man had fallen. One still stood.
There was no mistaking the victor.

Jin Mukyung looked down at the corpse lying face-first in the pool of blood it had made, its upper body and both arms severed. Then he spoke quietly, returning the words the Demon Bird had said before the battle began.
“When you get to the afterlife, tell them a man from Shanxi killed you.”
He gripped the sword hilt, which felt heavier than ever, and without hesitation cut off his enemy’s head. He raised it for all to see.
*Shhk.*
“I, Jin Mukyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan, have slain the Blood Soul Fat Demon!”
The force of his shout, carrying what little internal energy he had left, froze the air in the gorge.

Jamukha’s personal guard, already well aware of the Demon Bird’s identity, was stunned by his end. The Shanxi defenders stared wide-eyed at the title of the fiend who had stained the world with blood long ago.
The Demon Bird was dead.
And in that same moment, another Supreme Peak master had been born.
“Waaaaah!”
A tremendous roar shook the gorge. Their blood boiling like erupting lava, the Shanxi defenders charged without regard for their lives.

They looked ready to swallow the personal guard, still frozen by the unexpected turn of events, and the nomads in the rear, bewildered by the connection between their Great Chieftain Chinggen and the Blood Soul Fat Demon.
“Attack!”
“We are Shanxi! We will not fall!”
“Wipe out every barbarian who dared invade this land!”
“Loose!”
*Shh-shh-shh-shshsh!*
Beneath a downpour of arrows, thousands of martial artists and government troops drove like a wedge into the broken enemy line. Jin Wikyung led them, his eyes bloodshot.
“They’re coming!”
“Shields! Sh—!”
*Puhpuhpuk! KRRUNCH!*
The blood mist that had briefly settled rose thick again.
With the tide turned and their morale at its peak, the Shanxi defenders charged into the jaws of death.
They swung their weapons with every last ounce of strength, and endured the pain, biting at their enemies until their final breath.
*Shhk! CRUNCH!*
Cut one down, and two took his place. Cut two down, and three came on.
After that, there was nothing. Only death.
*CRUNCH!*
Seven in ten Keshik were First Rate warriors. They were unquestionably the finest troops on the grasslands. Yet the roughly three hundred deployed in the gorge were cut in half in no time.
“What do we do? What are we supposed to do now?”
The Keshik squad leader gave no answer to his subordinate’s desperate shout.
He couldn’t.
The three commanders of a hundred were dead. So was the Demon Bird, an absolute master alongside Jamukha.
And that was not all.
Even now, his men were dying to blades coming at them from every direction.
And at the center of it all was a ghost, staggering as he drank in blood without end.
*Shhk. Shhk!*
He brought his sword down, slashed, and thrust.
With those simple movements, Jin Mukyung felled twenty Keshik.
Despite his unmistakably severe Internal Injury, the Sword Demon of the Jin Family of Taiyuan stood in the middle of the gorge, protecting his two companions.
*What is this...?*
The Keshik squad leader squeezed his eyes shut.
After a brief hesitation, he ordered a retreat.
Or rather, he was about to.
Then a familiar sound rang out behind him.
*Boooooo!*
The squad leader knew what it meant.
That great call from dozens of horns sounding at once was for one man alone.
Jamukha.
The great Khan, the supreme ruler of the grasslands.

He slipped past a thrusting spear from behind and drove his sword, held in a reverse grip, into his attacker’s side.
“Guh!”
The dying groan reached his ears. Mukyung pulled the sword from the man’s chest and left the collapsing body behind, already rushing toward another enemy.
His eyes, impossibly, were closed.
And yet...
*It’s all so clear.*
He could feel everything without seeing it. No—with his eyes closed, everything around him felt even more vivid.
Darkness.
He had spent two years in darkness so complete that not a single ray of light could enter. He had swung his sword to grow stronger and, at times, to keep from going mad.
As his sight dulled, his other senses sharpened beyond measure. His Qi Sense had grown by leaps and bounds.
“K-kill him!”
“He’s only one man! If we take him down...!”
*Crunch!*
A grisly sound of torn flesh cut the shout short. Mukyung felled yet another enemy amid the endless carnage—he had lost count of how many—and steadied his ragged breathing.
He was dizzy. His body felt as heavy as waterlogged cotton, his mind as hazy as a dream.
The fight against the Demon Bird had given him more than a moment of enlightenment.
A severe Internal Injury.
His organs and acupoints were twisted and torn. He could almost hear them screaming.

Mukyung knew defeating the Demon Bird had taken something close to a miracle. Cheol Mubaek and Wipeng had risked their lives to help him. He had delivered a perfect strike, one he wasn’t sure he could ever repeat. And he had wielded a divine weapon capable of standing up to Force.
If any one of those three things had gone differently, the Demon Bird would be standing here instead of him.
But...
*Damn it.*
Nothing came without a price.

Mukyung swallowed the blood rising in his throat and drew a breath. He closed his fingers tight once more around the hilt that kept slipping from his grasp and felt, with every sense, the enemies surrounding him. Their breathing was thick with fear and rage.
Beyond the ceaseless shouts and screams, he heard a faint voice.
“Hurry. Go on.”
Jin Mukyung already knew who owned that hoarse, elderly voice.
“I’m not going. No—I can’t go.”
Mukyung opened his eyes. Blood running down his forehead stained his vision red, but he could see Cheol Mubaek and Wipeng, each on one knee and gasping for breath.
“We’re going back. All of us.”
Wipeng laughed at the resolve in his voice.
“See? What did I tell you? Those Jin Family people are stubborn as hell, h—”
*Hack. Drip, drip.*
He broke off and coughed up blood. Mukyung’s gaze darkened.
The color of coughed-up blood, and what came with it, could tell you how bad an injury was. By that measure, it was a miracle Wipeng was still conscious.
“Damn it. After coughing up bucketfuls, now all I’ve got left is a handful.”
He said it as though it were nothing, but Wipeng knew how dire things were. He fought to keep his eyes open and looked at Mukyung.
“Second Young Master. May I say one thing?”
“No. Don’t say any more. Save what strength you—”
“Mukyung.”
Mukyung went rigid. Wipeng bared his bloodstained teeth in a smile.
“Go. Stop being so stubborn.”
“I know it, Great Hero Cheol here knows it, and you know it too. You know what’s best.”
Mukyung clenched his teeth.
“It’s not too late. We can still go back.”
“Yes. We can go back,” Wipeng added gently.
“If you go alone.”
“What are you—!”
“Leave before it’s too late. You can still break through.”

Pushing deep into the enemy ranks to spare their allies as many casualties as possible had been the right choice. It had also been a costly mistake. Even now, hundreds of enemies surrounded them, watching for their chance to strike.
Wipeng and Cheol Mubaek saw that cruel reality clearly.
The old tiger who had once commanded Mount Heng was no more. Neither was the Peak swordsman with his ghostly swordplay.
The tiger’s claws were broken. The Ghost Sword’s swordplay was gone with his shattered arm.
That was the price they had accepted to tie down, for just one moment, the hand of a fiend who had once shaken an entire age.
But...
“You, Mukyung—you, of all people, have to live.”
“Not because you’re the Second Young Master of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”
Wipeng and Cheol Mubaek looked at Jin Mukyung through eyes that seemed ready to go dark at any moment.

The young man reflected in those eyes was no longer simply Jin Mukyung. He was the hope they had to save, even at the cost of their lives. He was the revenge that would one day return upon their enemies tens, hundreds of times over.
“Live. Survive, whatever it takes.”
“And come back. To us, and to them.”
Spring. Summer. Fall. Winter.
The four seasons returned without fail. Only people vanished as they passed.

That was why Wipeng believed, and Cheol Mubaek was certain: the winter that had come early for them today would one day reach their enemies too. The young Sword Demon of the Jin Family of Taiyuan, who would protect countless people in the years ahead, would bring them down.
Wipeng gave Mukyung a faint smile. He remembered the young man as a boy, coming to ask him to teach him the sword.
“Leave this place at once. Jin Mukyung—no, Commander of the Heaven Shaking Squad.”
“This is an order from your superior in the family.”
Mukyung was struck speechless. He squeezed his eyes shut.
He knew. What the best choice was. What he had to do to save more people.
But his feet would not move.
He still remembered the lesson he had learned alongside martial arts when he first picked up a sword.
*Chivalry.*
Stand against the strong and help the weak. Never turn away from injustice. Keep faith as dearly as life itself.
That was what it meant to be a chivalrous hero. It was the way of life a martial artist of the orthodox faction, one who stood for what was right, was supposed to follow.
He had learned martial arts because he loved the sword, because he wanted to grow stronger. But he had never forgotten the weight and meaning behind those two words.
*What’s best?*
Wipeng and Cheol Mubaek had said it, and Jin Mukyung had endlessly repeated it in his heart even as he cut down his enemies.
And suddenly, he understood.
“You’re both wrong.”
*Shhk.*
He opened his eyes and pressed his foot into the blood-soaked earth.
His sword tip, trembling a moment ago with fatigue and doubt, pointed toward the enemy without the slightest wavering.
“Before we ask what’s best or worst, there’s something we mustn’t forget.”
*Shhk, shhk!*
A nomad creeping closer was split diagonally through the torso. Blood ran down the snow-white blade that had cut through both the man and his spear.
“What’s right?”
Mukyung moved like flowing water. The blue Sword Energy that had been fading now surged along his blade, the insight of that fleeting moment slowly finding its way into his sword.
*Shwaaash!*
A thick mist of blood bloomed. Mukyung cut down three Keshik with a single stroke, snatched a crescent saber from a dead man’s hand, and sent it flying.
“What choice won’t I regret?”
*Whoosh! Thud!*
A single streak of light cut through the air. At its end, death came without even a scream.
A man stringing his composite bow fell. At that signal, the enemies packed around Mukyung gave vent to their pent-up fear and rage and charged as one.
*Shhk-shhk-shhk!*
*Fwoosh! CLANG!*
Flashes gleamed in the darkness.
Jin Mukyung knocked away the throwing blades, but a dozen thrusting spears and crescent sabers came down on him.
*Pit, pit!*
Heat. Drops of blood mingled with the wind whipping past.
He knew he could avoid them, but his body refused. The places all over his body where blades had grazed him burned with pain.
Or perhaps what burned was his disappointment and anger at himself. For even a moment, he had thought about what was best instead of what was right.
*This is the only right choice.*
The turmoil in his head cleared. Mukyung clenched his teeth with all his strength.
*Crack.*
The stench of blood filled his mouth.
One pain drowned out another. His fading awareness returned.
And at the same time—
*Tsutsutsu.*
The blue Sword Energy, rippling like small waves, gathered into one. Guided by the will of the man holding the sword, its currents joined and merged, then traced a single beautiful arc.
An arc so perfect that the dead old fiend would have laughed aloud to see it.
*Shwaaaash.*
The wind disappeared. A chill cleaved through the darkness.
The ten Keshik squad leaders charging at Mukyung widened their eyes as one.
At last, they understood what the Demon Bird had seen in his final moments. What that monster of a martial artist had felt.
*Shing.*
Their spears, shining with tangible energy, groaned. So did their crescent sabers.
As the energy around each weapon faded, the ten Peak masters watched their prized weapons break into pieces. Their vision tilted.
“S-Sword Demon...”
*Fwoosh!*
A dense fountain of blood stained the air.
Beneath the sticky blood pouring down like a shower, Jin Mukyung had felled ten birds with a single strike, like a blue wave. He murmured softly.
“I’ll keep that promise.”
*Blue Wave, Falling Bird.*
Thinking of the old fiend who had become the first prey of that once-nameless strike, Mukyung stepped toward the enemies frozen before him.
At that very moment—
“May I hear who you made that promise to, and what you promised?”
Mukyung’s whole body went rigid.
The unfamiliar voice had come from a man standing barely ten feet away, looking at him.
“Jamukha Khan!”
One shout—no, the same cry erupted from every direction, drowning out Mukyung’s voice.
*Jamukha.*
The voice was unfamiliar. The name was not.

The words spoken by the strongest nomad warrior as he died—the day Jin Mukyung annihilated the thousand-man vanguard that had invaded Shanxi Province ahead of the main force—were still vivid in his mind.
*He will punish you. Jamukha Khan will. He’ll take everything from you and burn it—your family, your friends, your home.*
Now, facing Jamukha at last, Mukyung understood. There had not been the slightest exaggeration in that curse.
“So it’s you. The Sword Demon.”
Jamukha.
The supreme ruler of the grasslands took a step toward Mukyung.
*Rrrumble.*
A faint but unmistakable tremor traveled up through everyone’s feet.

chapters.title: Chapter 964
paragraphs: *Rrrumble.*
Ripples spread across the pool of blood that had lain still.
Tiny fragments of stone trembled. So did the countless corpses, their eyes wide open in death.
*This is...*
Everyone felt the tremor, small but unmistakable.
And at the same time, they knew instinctively what it meant.
An earthquake?
Ridiculous.
This tremor was undeniable proof that at least several thousand men and horses were closing in.
The cruel omen was enough to give some people hope, and others deep despair.
“Waaaaah!”
*Wheeeee!*
The gorge filled with shouts.
The nomads, whose morale had plummeted at the Demon Bird’s death, let out shrill cries and charged.
“Reinforcements!”
“Jamukha Khan has arrived!”
If Jin Mukyung’s defeat of the Demon Bird had turned the tide of battle, now the reverse was happening.
Jamukha.

A name unfamiliar to the people of Shanxi. The ruler of the western grasslands, the absolute master of the vast Great Steppe. As if his arrival weren’t enough, at least several thousand reinforcements had joined him.

The nomads had been pushed back, their morale dwindling like a dying ember. Now it soared. The Shanxi defenders, who had been driving back the invaders moments ago, felt their forgotten fatigue and fear return.
Even the man leading them felt it.
*What do I do now? What am I supposed to do?*
Jin Wikyung swallowed a groan.
Blood from his enemies ran down the commander in chief’s sword, proof of how fiercely he had fought.
He had given the battle everything he had.

He had joined the fighting himself to raise his men’s spirits. Whenever a crisis arose, he had given flawless orders, sealing the gorge entrance so thoroughly that not even a drop of water could pass.
Fifteen thousand troops, scraped together from across Shanxi Province.
But reality was cold.
Less than half of those fifteen thousand could be called the main force, and even they had suffered heavy losses against the enemies who kept pouring in.
For every enemy they felled, there were two. For every two, five.
For every five, ten.
And behind them, tens of thousands more still waited.
In this long, dreadful war of attrition around the narrow gorge, it was not the rocks that would break first, but the pebbles.
*Was this how it had to end?*
Jin Wikyung breathed hard and looked around.
Everything was hazy, muffled.

Enemies and allies charged over heaps of corpses and tangled together. He stood rooted to the spot while a retainer called to him, but the enemy’s shouts drowned out the words. They reached him only in broken snatches, like stepping-stones across a stream.
“...urry, hurry!”
He couldn’t make out the words, but Jin Wikyung understood exactly what his retainer meant.
A hand tugged hard at his sleeve.
The retainer’s face was full of despair and urgency.

And it wasn’t just the retainer in front of him. Everyone around him—the martial artists of the Jin Family of Taiyuan, the Sect Leaders of their vassal sects, and the government troops—was speaking to him with their eyes.
*You have to get out of here.*
*You have to live.*
*Yes. I suppose so.*
Jin Wikyung understood how they felt.
The scales of victory and defeat had already tipped, and the invaders from the steppe were stronger than anyone had expected.
No—the strength of Dark Heaven, planted deep in the steppe, was far more terrifying than he had imagined.
Even now, the best course was to order a retreat.
While the troops at the front held out to buy time, he—the commander in chief—could gather the remaining forces and withdraw. That was the best strategy.
But...
*There’s no reason the commander in chief has to be me.*
Jin Wikyung smiled faintly and tightened his grip on his sword hilt.
He had spent the past few years more accustomed to a brush than a sword, but the Sword Energy of a Peak master had not dulled in the slightest.
*Shhk!*
A Keshik trying to break through his guards crumpled without a fight.
Jin Wikyung advanced, cutting down the enemy with clean, precise movements. His retainer hurried after him again.
“Lesser Family Head, why—”
*Thuk!*
Jin Wikyung took another life and spoke.
“Tell Lee Seowol, the Sect Leader of the Mount Heng Sword Sect, that from this moment on, I’m leaving everything that follows to her.”
“Go. Now!”
With that shout, Jin Wikyung swept his sword through the air.
A defeated commander had nowhere to return to. After sacrificing the lives of so many of his people, this was where he belonged.
*She’s clever. She’ll manage.*
With the weight on his heart lifted, his sword felt lighter. Pain flared from the wounds where lances and arrows had grazed him, setting his blood ablaze.
*I promised everyone I would protect this land—Shanxi Province.*
He had made another vow, too.
Even if everyone else fled in terror, he would remain here.
He would live and die with them.
“Come on, then! I am Jin Wikyung, Lesser Family Head of the Jin Family of Taiyuan! I’m right here!”
*Crack!*
At the sight of Jin Wikyung advancing with a beast’s roar, a flame sprang up deep in the eyes of the Shanxi defenders who had been wavering.
A shiver, its origin unknown, raced from the crowns of their heads through their bodies.
*There he is.*
The man they had been searching for all this time was right there.
The man who cherished and loved this barren land and the people living on it more than anyone.
The true Alliance Leader of Shanxi Province.
“Yaaaaah!”
“Protect the Lesser Family Head! Protect Shanxi Province!”
With a tremendous roar that shook the gorge, the people of Shanxi charged with all their strength.
They did not retreat.
Not one of them.
Jin Mukyung suddenly felt fatigue seep through his whole body.
It was the pain of his flesh, which he had momentarily forgotten, and the vague helplessness of facing an insurmountable wall.
*Was this how it had to end?*
Jin Mukyung looked up at the sky and muttered inwardly.
Even the faint moonlight had been swallowed by the clouds. As always, the sky offered no answer.
It simply hung over everyone in silence, watching, as though this too were fate.
The countless enemies and allies.
The corpses that had left this world and could no longer move.
And the two men standing tall at the center of it all.
Jin Mukyung and Jamukha.
“That’s a fine sword. More than worthy of being called a divine weapon.”
Jamukha’s gaze moved slowly.
To the blade, shining white even in the darkness. To Jin Mukyung. And, finally, to the Demon Bird’s corpse, sprawled in a pool of blood without so much as a twitch.
“He always called himself a hunter. Arrogant and stupid, considering how long he’d lived.”
His eyes and tone were calm.
Jamukha showed not the slightest regret at the Demon Bird’s death. Jin Mukyung tightened his grip on the hilt and spoke.
“If he’d heard that, he’d have been sad. You’re saying he was a hunting dog his master didn’t even acknowledge.”
“Master?”
“He was a subordinate you cared for, wasn’t he? Or was I wrong?”
Jin Mukyung had tossed out the remark to create even the smallest opening. But Jamukha’s gaze did not waver in the slightest.
“I’m disappointed.”
“What?”
“Speak with your sword, not that tongue of yours. A provocation like that doesn’t suit someone like you.”
“You’re still far too clumsy at it. Though choosing the wrong opponent was a big part of it. Like that pathetic fool lying over there.”
At Jamukha’s scornful glance toward the Demon Bird’s corpse, Jin Mukyung bit his lip.
Jamukha was right.
Trying to provoke an opening by using the Demon Bird’s death had been the wrong move from the start.
Jin Mukyung didn’t know why, but even after losing his sharpest-toothed hunting dog, Jamukha seemed entirely unmoved.
No—somehow, he even seemed pleased.
*What is it? Why?*
As Jin Mukyung wrestled with the question, Jamukha, who had been studying the Sword Demon with interest, suddenly spoke.
“If you’re not going to swing that sword, why not put it down?”
For a moment, Jin Mukyung understood what he meant and let out a quiet laugh.
“You want me to surrender? To you, of all people?”
“Surrender?”
Jamukha frowned and shook his head.
“No. I mean submit. Roll over and show your belly to your master, wag your tail, and lick the tops of his feet like a dog.”
“You’ll have to become my new hunting dog. Fortunately, I happen to have a spare collar.”
Jin Mukyung stared silently at Jamukha.
Then he spoke without warning.
“The Blood Soul Fat Demon—the Demon Bird—said something similar to me.”
“Did he offer to take you as his disciple?”
“I didn’t listen closely. It sounded like a pig squealing. But something like that.”
“That’s no surprise. He would’ve trained you and eventually tried to kill you himself. Though, looking at how he ended up, he’d have been the one to die.”
Jamukha spoke calmly, then continued.
“But don’t misunderstand me. I’m not like the Demon Bird.”
“You don’t look any better than him. If anything, you look worse.”
“I only intend to raise you as a hunting dog instead of prey. I might even let you off the leash when the time is right.”
“Sure. I bet you would.”
*Shing.*
A cold, sharp edge filled the air.
Jin Mukyung slowly raised his sword upright and spoke across its white blade.
“By the time that ‘right time’ you’re talking about comes, everything I want to protect will be gone.”
Their conversation was over. He had no regrets.
Better to die as a human being, the Second Young Master of the Jin Family of Taiyuan, than survive as a hunting dog.
To Jin Mukyung, who had already resolved to die, everything Jamukha had said was bullshit from beginning to end.
At least, until he heard Jamukha’s next words.
“I’ll spare your life. Yours, and all of theirs.”
“...What?”
“If you refuse to become a hunting dog because you have something to protect, then I mean to give you enough food.”
Jamukha looked at Jin Mukyung, whose eyes had widened, and gestured toward the battlefield, filled with screams and shouts.
“Do you know how to tame a hunting dog? It’s surprisingly simple.”
A leash alone was not enough.
A hunting dog that hadn’t been fully tamed would become a beast the moment its leash came off, and bite its master.
“But what if it’s starving?”

A hunting dog kept on a tight leash and starved for days on end would grow docile. It would have no strength left to bite anyone, and in the helplessness it had never experienced before, it would realize it was nothing but an animal.
“That’s when the master appears and tosses it some food.”
*Shk.*
Jamukha held out his hand toward Jin Mukyung.
There was nothing in his empty palm. Yet Jin Mukyung could see it clearly.
Not meat dripping with blood, but the countless people of Shanxi fighting to the death inside the gorge.
Everyone’s lives—including his own.
Jin Mukyung gritted his teeth without realizing it.
Was it fear of the man in front of him?
Wrong.
It was hope.
Just for a little while.
The hope that if he betrayed righteousness and turned his back on chivalry for only a short time, everyone could survive.
That he could save the people continuing a blood-soaked battle whose ending was already decided, his one and only older brother, and the two Peak masters waiting to die behind him.
“Mukyung!”
“No! Absolutely not!”
Wipeng and Cheol Mubaek.
Jin Mukyung looked at the two men shouting with what little strength they had left, his gaze sunk deep.
“I’m sorry. Both of you.”
Wipeng and Cheol Mubaek’s eyes widened. Jamukha smiled.
Jin Mukyung looked at Jamukha and parted his lips.
“Did I ever tell you?”
“Tell me what?”
“What I said to a certain pig bastard who wanted to take me as his disciple.”
Jamukha’s smile faded a little as Jin Mukyung stepped toward him.

“Go suck a dick.”

*Boooooo!*

Jamukha knew better than anyone what that urgent blast meant.
*An enemy attack!*

The tremor everyone in the gorge had felt moments ago hadn’t come from the nomads alone.

sentences.text: *Rrrumble.*
Ripples spread across the pool of blood that had lain still.
Tiny fragments of stone trembled.
So did the countless corpses, their eyes wide open in death.
*This is...*
Everyone felt the tremor, small but unmistakable.
And at the same time, they knew instinctively what it meant.
An earthquake?
Ridiculous.
This tremor was undeniable proof that at least several thousand men and horses were closing in.
The cruel omen was enough to give some people hope, and others deep despair.
“Waaaaah!”
*Wheeeee!*
The gorge filled with shouts.
The nomads, whose morale had plummeted at the Demon Bird’s death, let out shrill cries and charged.
“Reinforcements!”
“Jamukha Khan has arrived!”
If Jin Mukyung’s defeat of the Demon Bird had turned the tide of battle, now the reverse was happening.
Jamukha.
A name unfamiliar to the people of Shanxi.
The ruler of the western grasslands, the absolute master of the vast Great Steppe.
As if his arrival weren’t enough, at least several thousand reinforcements had joined him.
The nomads had been pushed back, their morale dwindling like a dying ember.
Now it soared.
The Shanxi defenders, who had been driving back the invaders moments ago, felt their forgotten fatigue and fear return.
Even the man leading them felt it.
*What do I do now?
What am I supposed to do?*
Jin Wikyung swallowed a groan.
Blood from his enemies ran down the commander in chief’s sword, proof of how fiercely he had fought.
He had given the battle everything he had.
He had joined the fighting himself to raise his men’s spirits.
Whenever a crisis arose, he had given flawless orders, sealing the gorge entrance so thoroughly that not even a drop of water could pass.
Fifteen thousand troops, scraped together from across Shanxi Province.
But reality was cold.
Less than half of those fifteen thousand could be called the main force, and even they had suffered heavy losses against the enemies who kept pouring in.
For every enemy they felled, there were two.
For every two, five.
For every five, ten.
And behind them, tens of thousands more still waited.
In this long, dreadful war of attrition around the narrow gorge, it was not the rocks that would break first, but the pebbles.
*Was this how it had to end?*
Jin Wikyung breathed hard and looked around.
Everything was hazy, muffled.
Enemies and allies charged over heaps of corpses and tangled together.
He stood rooted to the spot while a retainer called to him, but the enemy’s shouts drowned out the words.
They reached him only in broken snatches, like stepping-stones across a stream.
“...urry, hurry!”
He couldn’t make out the words, but Jin Wikyung understood exactly what his retainer meant.
A hand tugged hard at his sleeve.
The retainer’s face was full of despair and urgency.
And it wasn’t just the retainer in front of him.
Everyone around him—the martial artists of the Jin Family of Taiyuan, the Sect Leaders of their vassal sects, and the government troops—was speaking to him with their eyes.
*You have to get out of here.*
*You have to live.*
*Yes.
I suppose so.*
Jin Wikyung understood how they felt.
The scales of victory and defeat had already tipped, and the invaders from the steppe were stronger than anyone had expected.
No—the strength of Dark Heaven, planted deep in the steppe, was far more terrifying than he had imagined.
Even now, the best course was to order a retreat.
While the troops at the front held out to buy time, he—the commander in chief—could gather the remaining forces and withdraw.
That was the best strategy.
But...
*There’s no reason the commander in chief has to be me.*
Jin Wikyung smiled faintly and tightened his grip on his sword hilt.
He had spent the past few years more accustomed to a brush than a sword, but the Sword Energy of a Peak master had not dulled in the slightest.
*Shhk!*
A Keshik trying to break through his guards crumpled without a fight.
Jin Wikyung advanced, cutting down the enemy with clean, precise movements.
His retainer hurried after him again.
“Lesser Family Head, why—”
*Thuk!*
Jin Wikyung took another life and spoke.
“Tell Lee Seowol, the Sect Leader of the Mount Heng Sword Sect, that from this moment on, I’m leaving everything that follows to her.”
“Go.
Now!”
With that shout, Jin Wikyung swept his sword through the air.
A defeated commander had nowhere to return to.
After sacrificing the lives of so many of his people, this was where he belonged.
*She’s clever.
She’ll manage.*
With the weight on his heart lifted, his sword felt lighter.
Pain flared from the wounds where lances and arrows had grazed him, setting his blood ablaze.
*I promised everyone I would protect this land—Shanxi Province.*
He had made another vow, too.
Even if everyone else fled in terror, he would remain here.
He would live and die with them.
“Come on, then!
I am Jin Wikyung, Lesser Family Head of the Jin Family of Taiyuan!
I’m right here!”
*Crack!*
At the sight of Jin Wikyung advancing with a beast’s roar, a flame sprang up deep in the eyes of the Shanxi defenders who had been wavering.
A shiver, its origin unknown, raced from the crowns of their heads through their bodies.
*There he is.*
The man they had been searching for all this time was right there.
The man who cherished and loved this barren land and the people living on it more than anyone.
The true Alliance Leader of Shanxi Province.
“Yaaaaah!”
“Protect the Lesser Family Head!
Protect Shanxi Province!”
With a tremendous roar that shook the gorge, the people of Shanxi charged with all their strength.
They did not retreat.
Not one of them.
Jin Mukyung suddenly felt fatigue seep through his whole body.
It was the pain of his flesh, which he had momentarily forgotten, and the vague helplessness of facing an insurmountable wall.
*Was this how it had to end?*
Jin Mukyung looked up at the sky and muttered inwardly.
Even the faint moonlight had been swallowed by the clouds.
As always, the sky offered no answer.
It simply hung over everyone in silence, watching, as though this too were fate.
The countless enemies and allies.
The corpses that had left this world and could no longer move.
And the two men standing tall at the center of it all.
Jin Mukyung and Jamukha.
“That’s a fine sword.
More than worthy of being called a divine weapon.”
Jamukha’s gaze moved slowly.
To the blade, shining white even in the darkness.
To Jin Mukyung.
And, finally, to the Demon Bird’s corpse, sprawled in a pool of blood without so much as a twitch.
“He always called himself a hunter.
Arrogant and stupid, considering how long he’d lived.”
His eyes and tone were calm.
Jamukha showed not the slightest regret at the Demon Bird’s death.
Jin Mukyung tightened his grip on the hilt and spoke.
“If he’d heard that, he’d have been sad.
You’re saying he was a hunting dog his master didn’t even acknowledge.”
“Master?”
“He was a subordinate you cared for, wasn’t he?
Or was I wrong?”
Jin Mukyung had tossed out the remark to create even the smallest opening.
But Jamukha’s gaze did not waver in the slightest.
“I’m disappointed.”
“What?”

“You’re still far too clumsy at it.

Jamukha was right.

Jin Mukyung didn’t know why, but even after losing his sharpest-toothed hunting dog, Jamukha seemed entirely unmoved.

chapters.title: Chapter 965
paragraphs: *Boooo! Boooooo!*
The horns sounded in wave after wave, but this was nothing like their earlier call.
Instead of joining in one great roar, the blasts broke off in fits and starts. There was urgency in them, too.

Even the people of Shanxi, who did not know exactly what the horns meant, could tell that something unexpected had happened to the enemy before them. And that this sudden turn would bring them a stroke of luck they had never imagined.
“Now! Now’s our chance!”
“Don’t fall back! Keep pressing them!”
Not one of the Shanxi defenders stopped to wonder what had happened.
Not a single one.
They had already made peace with dying. They had stayed to protect their homes, their families, and their friends, and now they faced the invaders head-on.
Those who came to take, and those who stayed to protect.
They did not share the same desperation, or the same weight of resolve.
The people of Shanxi wrung out every last bit of strength. They stumbled forward and swung weapons that felt heavier than ever.
At the enemies faltering as they grasped what the horns meant.
At the cruel invaders from the steppe.
*Klang!*
*Thud, thud!*
Sparks flew where sharp blades met.
The Keshik, frozen for a moment in confusion, scrambled to fight back. But that moment of distraction was all the furious Shanxi defenders needed.
*Shhk!*

Saber Force surged along a crescent saber, sending the limbs of three or four men flying. Yet even in their agony, those who had not died threw themselves at a Keshik squad leader with all the strength they had left.
“Y-you crazy bastards...!”
*Crack!*
Flesh split with a sickening sound. The shout stopped short.
Not many people could survive an axe buried in the crown of their head.
No. None could.
“That’s what you get for setting your sights on Shanxi Province, you damned barbarian.”
*Ptooey.*

An unknown martial artist spat phlegm onto the squad leader’s corpse, its eyes still wide open in death. Then he carefully took the sword from the hand of a comrade who had fulfilled his final duty and closed his eyes in peace.
His voice was thick as he said goodbye.
“Rest here a little while. I’ll kill just ten more and be right back.”
He knew the truth.
No—all the people of Shanxi knew.
They might never come back. They might never meet again in this life.
But knowing that changed nothing.
Nothing except the resolve with which they faced certain death.
“Yaaaaah!”
A cry like a scream shook the gorge.
It broke the stillness of the deep night, pierced the blare of dozens of horns, and traveled farther and farther on.
Past grass darkened by night and ground packed hard by countless hooves, until it reached a band of horsemen cresting a high hill and racing toward the battlefield.
The towering old man at their head smiled when he heard the fierce cry rising from the people of Shanxi.
“Yes. I hear you loud and clear. This old man does—and so do we all.”
*Thud, thud, thud!*
Pounding hooves shook the earth.
The wind drove the stench of blood deep into their nostrils. The ceaseless clangor of steel set blood that had gone cold boiling again.
“Thank you. You’ve held out well.”
His murmur faded into the wind rushing over him.
The towering old man spoke from the heart to those who had fought without giving an inch in the worst of circumstances. To those still desperately facing an overwhelming enemy.
He offered them his respect, his gratitude, and his apology.
“We swore to stand together beneath one banner. Yet some turned away when our neighbors were in danger, afraid their own fences would come down.”
His voice rang clear over the pounding hooves.
The words were a reminder of his own shame, and a rebuke to everyone riding behind him.
“Spilled water cannot be gathered again, nor can an arrow be called back once it leaves the bow. But...”
The Jin Family of Taiyuan and the people of Shanxi had not been easily broken.
They were still here, burning with countless lives as fuel.
Their cup had not yet shattered. Their enemies’ arrows might still be on the string.
“Look at them. And remember this well!”
His shout rose like wildfire, tearing through the night air.
The old man pointed toward the gorge, where a fierce battle was raging.
Below the hill, the steppe army was rapidly closing in, moving toward them to the sound of horns. He paid it no heed and continued to shout.
“They are our neighbors, our friends, our comrades-in-arms! They swore beneath the same banner as we did. And they are the very people our family tried to turn its back on!”
The old man was ashamed.
Ashamed of the family that had tried to abandon the people of Shanxi. Ashamed that he himself had wavered, if only for a moment, at that pathetic proposal.
But he had not forgotten the vow they had made long ago: to rise together against the injustice of Dark Heaven and save a world sunk in misery.
That was why he had ridden here with all his strength, repeating the same hopes to himself again and again.
*Hold out until the end. Let us not be too late.*
The people of Shanxi had not let him down.
They had given him another chance to unfurl the banner he had been too ashamed to raise.
“What are you?”
At the old man’s roar, like the bellow of a beast, two thousand tightly shut mouths opened as one.
“Fighters!”
Fighters.
For a very long time, they had called themselves fighters, not martial artists.
To them, martial arts were not something to hone for their own sake. They were tools for battle.
“And what is an enemy to you?”
At the old man’s next shouted question, the eyes of those riding through the darkness flashed.
“Weak losers who will kneel before a fighter’s spear and blade!”
*Thud, thud, thud!*
*Boooooo!*
Thunderous hooves and blaring horns rang out one after the other.
The sight of countless horsemen charging toward them through a hazy cloud of dust, just over thirty meters away, did not shake a single one of them.
They were valiant fighters. Those men were losers who would soon be broken and crushed.
“I’ll ask you one last time!”
The old man roared. The enormous saber in his hand now scattered dazzling flashes of light.
“Who are we!”
The gap closed. Watching a wave of lances glint in the darkness, the two thousand fighters shouted with one voice.
“The masters of Hebei!”
At that very moment—
*Flap.*
The twenty or so standard-bearers, who had waited through the past several days for this moment alone, raised their flags high.
A blue tiger that looked ready to leap to life, and four characters stitched in a rough hand, billowed fiercely in the rushing wind.
At last, they revealed themselves to everyone on the battlefield.
The Hebei Peng Family.
The Tiger of the North. One of the Five Great Families.
And the towering old man leading them was a great tiger, grown stronger still through the long years.
“Charge!”
With a roar that shook earth and sky, the old man kicked off his saddle and shot toward the enemies closing in on him.
*Rrrumble.*
Thunder that chilled body and mind.
The old man—no, the Thunderbolt Saber King—swept his great saber through the dense forest of spears and blades like a massive bolt of lightning.
*Kaboom!*
A blinding flash and a deafening boom swallowed everything around them.
Behind the old tiger, who rampaged through the enemy formation and shattered it, two thousand fighters burst through the thick haze of blood. Together they pierced the enemy ranks like a single awl.
*Crack!*
In the deep of night, when even the birds slept—
The battle, and the Double Ninth Festival, were not over yet.
Everyone heard it.
And everyone saw it.
The strange thunder that had come from the ground, not the sky.
Beyond the flash and the boom, dozens of blood-soaked flags snapped in the wind as the enemy shrieked.
“The Hebei Peng Family! It’s the Hebei Peng Family!”
“T-The Thunderbolt Saber King...!”
The first was the Shanxi defenders’ cry of joy. The second was the nomads’ lament.
Peng Cheolhu, the Thunderbolt Saber King.
His name and title were no relics of a bygone age.
An old tiger might lose its strength and standing among its own, but the teeth and claws of the great tiger called the Thunderbolt Saber King had only grown sharper.
What’s more, the Hebei Peng Family was a renowned great family that ruled the north alongside the Murong Family.
In that sense, the Thunderbolt Saber King and the martial artists of Hebei following him were showing exactly how they had earned the titles of Ten Kings and one of the Five Great Families.
*Boooo! Boooooo!*
As the horns blared without pause, Jamukha had a sudden thought.
*This is going to be a long night.*
But he was not flustered.
The Shanxi defenders, united around the Jin Family of Taiyuan, had fought harder than he expected. The arrival of the Hebei Peng Family, though, was within the range of what he had anticipated.
So was the Thunderbolt Saber King himself.
“Just as that person said.”
At Jamukha’s muttered words, Jin Mukyung’s face stiffened. He had been trying to steady himself, to keep his emotions from taking hold.
“What did you just say?”
“The Thunderbolt Saber King’s temper is so fiery that he’ll act without thinking of the consequences. So even if he leads the Hebei Peng Family to Shanxi’s aid, it will be no surprise.”
Jamukha spoke without hesitation, then added quietly:
“That is what that person said. I remember it clearly.”
“Don’t look at me like that. If you thought we couldn’t anticipate even this much, I’d be very disappointed in you.”
“Yes. We.”
Jamukha nodded slightly and clicked his tongue as he looked at Jin Mukyung.
“A pity. If you’d taken my hand, you could have been one of us.”
*Step.*
Jamukha took a step as casually as if he were out for a stroll.
*Shwack!*
The crescent saber in his hand sliced through the air.
The strike was so precise and swift it made Jin Mukyung’s skin crawl. His eyes widened as he twisted aside.
*Shhk!*
His hair fluttered. Blood sprayed from the gash cut into his forehead by the pressure alone, blinding him.
*Damn it.*
Jin Mukyung’s body jerked to a halt for an instant. His two years of training had made losing his sight no problem—but the blood in his eyes was enough to shake his composure.
For Jamukha, it was the perfect opening.
A chance to uproot the young Sword Demon, still unfinished but full of potential.
“If you’d put that collar on yourself, this wouldn’t have happened.”
Jamukha raised his crescent saber, his voice low.
He surpassed the Demon Bird in every respect. Even facing Jin Mukyung, exhausted to the limit, he did not let his guard down.
Calmly and without a word, he found the fastest, most precise path and brought his saber down.
*Farewell, young Sword Demon.*
Blue-green Force flowed along the smooth blade, about to cut through the air—
*Whoosh! Whoom!*
With a fearsome whistle, a great saber shot in like a bolt of lightning and plunged squarely between Jamukha and Jin Mukyung.
*Kaboom!*
Beyond the boom that sounded as though the sky had split and the cloud of dust rising pale in its wake, the towering old man appeared. He bared his teeth in a grin at Jamukha.
“Ready to die?”
At the sight of the Thunderbolt Saber King drenched in blood from head to toe, Jamukha replied in fluent Chinese.
“Thanks for saying what I was about to.”
For Jamukha, nothing had changed.
Nothing at all.

Past grass darkened by night and ground packed hard by countless hooves, until it reached a band of horsemen cresting a high hill and racing toward the battlefield.
The towering old man at their head smiled when he heard the fierce cry rising from the people of Shanxi.
“Yes.
I hear you loud and clear.
This old man does—and so do we all.”
*Thud, thud, thud!*
Pounding hooves shook the earth.
The wind drove the stench of blood deep into their nostrils.
The ceaseless clangor of steel set blood that had gone cold boiling again.
“Thank you.
You’ve held out well.”
His murmur faded into the wind rushing over him.
The towering old man spoke from the heart to those who had fought without giving an inch in the worst of circumstances.
To those still desperately facing an overwhelming enemy.
He offered them his respect, his gratitude, and his apology.
“We swore to stand together beneath one banner.
Yet some turned away when our neighbors were in danger, afraid their own fences would come down.”
His voice rang clear over the pounding hooves.
The words were a reminder of his own shame, and a rebuke to everyone riding behind him.
“Spilled water cannot be gathered again, nor can an arrow be called back once it leaves the bow.
But...”
The Jin Family of Taiyuan and the people of Shanxi had not been easily broken.
They were still here, burning with countless lives as fuel.
Their cup had not yet shattered.
Their enemies’ arrows might still be on the string.
“Look at them.
And remember this well!”
His shout rose like wildfire, tearing through the night air.
The old man pointed toward the gorge, where a fierce battle was raging.
Below the hill, the steppe army was rapidly closing in, moving toward them to the sound of horns.
He paid it no heed and continued to shout.
“They are our neighbors, our friends, our comrades-in-arms!
They swore beneath the same banner as we did.
And they are the very people our family tried to turn its back on!”
The old man was ashamed.
Ashamed of the family that had tried to abandon the people of Shanxi.
Ashamed that he himself had wavered, if only for a moment, at that pathetic proposal.
But he had not forgotten the vow they had made long ago: to rise together against the injustice of Dark Heaven and save a world sunk in misery.
That was why he had ridden here with all his strength, repeating the same hopes to himself again and again.
*Hold out until the end.
Let us not be too late.*
The people of Shanxi had not let him down.
They had given him another chance to unfurl the banner he had been too ashamed to raise.
“What are you?”
At the old man’s roar, like the bellow of a beast, two thousand tightly shut mouths opened as one.
“Fighters!”
Fighters.
For a very long time, they had called themselves fighters, not martial artists.
To them, martial arts were not something to hone for their own sake.
They were tools for battle.
“And what is an enemy to you?”
At the old man’s next shouted question, the eyes of those riding through the darkness flashed.
“Weak losers who will kneel before a fighter’s spear and blade!”
*Thud, thud, thud!*
*Boooooo!*
Thunderous hooves and blaring horns rang out one after the other.
The sight of countless horsemen charging toward them through a hazy cloud of dust, just over thirty meters away, did not shake a single one of them.
They were valiant fighters.
Those men were losers who would soon be broken and crushed.
“I’ll ask you one last time!”
The old man roared.
The enormous saber in his hand now scattered dazzling flashes of light.
“Who are we!”
The gap closed.
Watching a wave of lances glint in the darkness, the two thousand fighters shouted with one voice.
“The masters of Hebei!”
At that very moment—
*Flap.*
The twenty or so standard-bearers, who had waited through the past several days for this moment alone, raised their flags high.
A blue tiger that looked ready to leap to life, and four characters stitched in a rough hand, billowed fiercely in the rushing wind.
At last, they revealed themselves to everyone on the battlefield.
The Hebei Peng Family.
The Tiger of the North.
One of the Five Great Families.
And the towering old man leading them was a great tiger, grown stronger still through the long years.
“Charge!”
With a roar that shook earth and sky, the old man kicked off his saddle and shot toward the enemies closing in on him.
*Rrrumble.*
Thunder that chilled body and mind.
The old man—no, the Thunderbolt Saber King—swept his great saber through the dense forest of spears and blades like a massive bolt of lightning.
*Kaboom!*
A blinding flash and a deafening boom swallowed everything around them.
Behind the old tiger, who rampaged through the enemy formation and shattered it, two thousand fighters burst through the thick haze of blood.
Together they pierced the enemy ranks like a single awl.
*Crack!*
In the deep of night, when even the birds slept—
The battle, and the Double Ninth Festival, were not over yet.
Everyone heard it.
And everyone saw it.
The strange thunder that had come from the ground, not the sky.
Beyond the flash and the boom, dozens of blood-soaked flags snapped in the wind as the enemy shrieked.
“The Hebei Peng Family!
It’s the Hebei Peng Family!”
“T-The Thunderbolt Saber King...!”
The first was the Shanxi defenders’ cry of joy.
The second was the nomads’ lament.
Peng Cheolhu, the Thunderbolt Saber King.
His name and title were no relics of a bygone age.
An old tiger might lose its strength and standing among its own, but the teeth and claws of the great tiger called the Thunderbolt Saber King had only grown sharper.
What’s more, the Hebei Peng Family was a renowned great family that ruled the north alongside the Murong Family.
In that sense, the Thunderbolt Saber King and the martial artists of Hebei following him were showing exactly how they had earned the titles of Ten Kings and one of the Five Great Families.
*Boooo!
Boooooo!*
As the horns blared without pause, Jamukha had a sudden thought.
*This is going to be a long night.*
But he was not flustered.
The Shanxi defenders, united around the Jin Family of Taiyuan, had fought harder than he expected.
The arrival of the Hebei Peng Family, though, was within the range of what he had anticipated.
So was the Thunderbolt Saber King himself.
“Just as that person said.”
At Jamukha’s muttered words, Jin Mukyung’s face stiffened.
He had been trying to steady himself, to keep his emotions from taking hold.
“What did you just say?”
“The Thunderbolt Saber King’s temper is so fiery that he’ll act without thinking of the consequences.
So even if he leads the Hebei Peng Family to Shanxi’s aid, it will be no surprise.”
Jamukha spoke without hesitation, then added quietly:
“That is what that person said.
I remember it clearly.”
“Don’t look at me like that.
If you thought we couldn’t anticipate even this much, I’d be very disappointed in you.”
“Yes.
We.”
Jamukha nodded slightly and clicked his tongue as he looked at Jin Mukyung.
“A pity.
If you’d taken my hand, you could have been one of us.”
*Step.*
Jamukha took a step as casually as if he were out for a stroll.
*Shwack!*
The crescent saber in his hand sliced through the air.
The strike was so precise and swift it made Jin Mukyung’s skin crawl.
His eyes widened as he twisted aside.
*Shhk!*
His hair fluttered.
Blood sprayed from the gash cut into his forehead by the pressure alone, blinding him.
*Damn it.*
Jin Mukyung’s body jerked to a halt for an instant.
His two years of training had made losing his sight no problem—but the blood in his eyes was enough to shake his composure.
For Jamukha, it was the perfect opening.
A chance to uproot the young Sword Demon, still unfinished but full of potential.
“If you’d put that collar on yourself, this wouldn’t have happened.”
Jamukha raised his crescent saber, his voice low.
He surpassed the Demon Bird in every respect.
Even facing Jin Mukyung, exhausted to the limit, he did not let his guard down.
Calmly and without a word, he found the fastest, most precise path and brought his saber down.
*Farewell, young Sword Demon.*
Blue-green Force flowed along the smooth blade, about to cut through the air—
*Whoosh!
Whoom!*
With a fearsome whistle, a great saber shot in like a bolt of lightning and plunged squarely between Jamukha and Jin Mukyung.
*Kaboom!*
Beyond the boom that sounded as though the sky had split and the cloud of dust rising pale in its wake, the towering old man appeared.
He bared his teeth in a grin at Jamukha.
“Ready to die?”
At the sight of the Thunderbolt Saber King drenched in blood from head to toe, Jamukha replied in fluent Chinese.
“Thanks for saying what I was about to.”
For Jamukha, nothing had changed.
Nothing at all.

paragraphs: If two martial artists were evenly matched, what decided a life-and-death duel? For ages, that question had been a favorite topic among the gossips of the martial world.
Some said it was superior internal energy and peerless martial arts. Others put a divine weapon first. Still others insisted it was an unshakable mind and exceptional physical ability.
Every one of those answers was right. And every one was wrong.
Masters who had reached a certain realm knew. They had felt it firsthand.
In a life-and-death duel, a single difference—however small, however trivial it might seem—could decide the outcome.
That was why they often agreed on one thing:
*What martial art you’ve learned isn’t all that important. What matters most is having the eyes and instincts to see through your opponent’s movements.*
And now, everyone in the gorge understood exactly what those words meant, though they had once seemed so distant.
*Whoosh! Kaboom!*
They couldn’t see the movements. They couldn’t even sense them.
They could only stare, dazed, forgetting for a moment to swing their blades at the enemies before them.
Beyond the endless flashes and thunderous booms, three figures tangled together at speeds too great to see.
*Whoom!*
An absurdly massive saber cleaved through the air. The mighty Force along its edge tore through Jamukha’s body with the wind.
Or seemed to.
*Shhk.*
A single step.
Jamukha’s form blurred for an instant, then reappeared about ten feet away.
He had dodged the attack with a ghostly movement. Just as he surged toward the Thunderbolt Saber King, a faint whistle sounded from beyond his blind spot.
*Shwaa!*
In that instant, Jamukha was reminded of something.
The Thunderbolt Saber King wasn’t the only enemy he had to defeat here today.
*Shk—KABOOM!*
The crescent saber met a gleaming white sword.
Amid the shock wave and deafening boom that reverberated through the gorge, Jamukha took an unexpected step back. A smile formed at the corner of his mouth.
*Impressive. Even better than I expected.*
His gaze fell on Jin Mukyung, who had been driven back, carving a deep furrow through the ground.
The young Sword Demon of the Jin Family of Taiyuan had delivered an unexpected strike despite his battered body.
And at last, Jamukha understood how Jin Mukyung, who had only just broken through to Supreme Peak, had defeated the Demon Bird, a master firmly established in that realm.
The sword Mukyung wielded had neither the prescribed movements nor the shapes considered fundamental to martial arts.
Only One Strike.
He found the fastest, most perfect path to end his opponent’s life, then took it.
And that strike, driven by the will to kill, carried far greater power than Mukyung’s own martial prowess should have allowed.
Enough to defeat the Demon Bird, a superior master, in the realm of Supreme Peak, where a single form could decide the fight.
But...
*This is as far as it goes.*
Without a word anyone could hear, Jamukha shook out both arms.
Green Force, like the vast grasslands where he had been born and raised, surged along his crescent saber and his empty hand.
*Fwoosh!*
Beyond the blinding flash swelling to an immense size, the two streams of Force shot in different directions.
One toward the Thunderbolt Saber King, who was bringing his great saber down as if to cleave the world in two.
The other toward Jin Mukyung, who was staggering and swallowing blood.
The result went far beyond what one man had expected.
*Craaaack!*
The Thunderbolt Saber King’s eyes widened as he stared at the two blades locked together without the slightest give.
*What in the—!*
He was a warrior to the bone. He had made his name in the Great Faction War and become a living legend, yet he had never underestimated an opponent standing before him.
And still, his full-powered strike had been blocked.
With astonishing ease.
As though his opponent had seen through both the form and the flow of the martial art he had used.
“How could you...!”
Confusion and anger mingled in his voice.
The two blades remained locked in midair, their wielders’ bodies still apart. Jamukha looked at the Thunderbolt Saber King with calm eyes.
“I’m disappointed. Shouldn’t you have saved your much younger junior first, Thunderbolt Saber King?”
The Thunderbolt Saber King’s eyes wavered.
Over Jamukha’s shoulder, he belatedly saw Jin Mukyung on his knees, vomiting blood, unable to withstand the force of the palm strike.
*Damn it.*
A mistake.
No—a grievous misjudgment.
Jamukha was stronger than he had thought, and he was a far more formidable master, with deeper secrets.
*BOOM!*
After a fierce contest of strength, their sabers finally tore apart with a deafening boom.
The Thunderbolt Saber King let the force of the impact pass through him, then brought his great saber down at Jamukha again.
*Fwoosh!*
A strike combining his innate divine strength with several jiazi of internal energy.

Born the third son of the Hebei Peng Family, he had become its Family Head and the Thunderbolt Saber King through the family’s peerless martial art, the Primordial Thunderbolt Saber. Now it fell like a bolt of lightning.
As if it would split the world in two along with the enemy before him.
*Shing! KRAAAASH!*
A keen slicing sound rang out as the gorge shook.
Yet even after delivering a strike worthy of one of the Ten Kings, the Thunderbolt Saber King swept his gaze over the area, eyes grave, while a hazy cloud of dust billowed around him.
*Where is he?*
He had swung his saber countless times and cut down more than a thousand people, by his estimate.
So he knew better than anyone:
That strike had cut through wind and earth, not a man’s flesh and bone.
“You bastard!”
The Thunderbolt Saber King roared like a tiger and swung his great saber.
Beyond the dust cloud scattering under the force of his blow, Jamukha was crouched in silence, like a wolf preparing to hunt.
*Hup.*
Neither moved first.
As if on cue, both men shot toward each other.
No one there could see the teeth and claws of the great tiger from the Hebei Peng Family or the wolf of the Great Steppe—so fast and so powerful were they.
*BOOM! BOOM! KRAAA-BOOM!*
Every time their sabers collided, a boom like cannon fire rang out.
The screams of those caught in the tremendous shock waves sweeping across the gorge rose over the noise.
“Gwaaaah!”
Arms and legs tore from bodies. Fountains of blood shot into the air.
Beyond a thick haze of blood, flashes of light kept sparking without pause. The nomads caught at the heart of the calamity fled for their lives.
Some ran toward the relatively safe entrance at the rear.
Others ran toward the exit at the opposite end.
Those with no choice but to take the latter route found themselves face-to-face with a forest of spears and blades, now almost upon them.
*Thud-thud-thud!*

Dozens of nomads, unable to dodge the arrows raining down from the still-standing earthen rampart, fell like pincushions. The blades in the hands of Shanxi fighters flashed as they pressed forward, trampling the crumbling bodies.
*Shhk!*
Jin Wikyung was exhausted, but the keen edge of his sword had lost none of its bite.
Having cut through a crescent saber and its wielder, he steadied his ragged breathing and advanced.
Toward the enemies inside the gorge, who had once seemed endless no matter how many they killed, but were now being swept away like a wave.
Toward the heart of the gorge, where two monsters were locked in a fierce battle.
Danger?
It didn’t matter.
The arrow had already been loosed. If they retreated now, only a defeat they could never undo awaited them all.
*We have to seize the gorge and drive them out as soon as possible. That’s our only chance.*

The arrival of the Hebei Peng Family, led by the Thunderbolt Saber King, had greatly improved the desperate battle situation. But Jin Wikyung’s cool head saw every detail of the position his side was in.
*This momentum is only temporary. If the enemy regains their composure, the tide will turn again.*
The Hebei Peng Family was undoubtedly strong.

Its power reached beyond its home province of Hebei to encompass the entire north alongside the Murong Family. And the Thunderbolt Saber King, a peerless Supreme Peak master, could take on an army by himself.
But the enemy was strong, too.
Jamukha was fighting the Thunderbolt Saber King without giving an inch, and beyond the gorge, tens of thousands of steppe warriors were still fighting the Hebei Peng Family.
Their morale had faltered, but they still outnumbered the Hebei Peng Family ten to one—perhaps more.
Even after thousands of their soldiers had been killed or put out of action in the narrow gorge, the fundamental gap in their forces remained.
There was only one answer.
To win a battle still hanging in the balance, they had to keep advancing with everything they had until the very end.
“Follow me!”
Jin Wikyung shouted at the top of his lungs and charged.
His body now soaked in blood, he plunged into the crumbling enemy line and swung his sword like a madman.
*Craaaack!*
He had too much to protect.
The people who followed him, ready to give their lives.
The land where they had been born and raised.
And, far in the distance, his little brother, staggering back to his feet despite his grievous internal injuries.
Jin Wikyung couldn’t give up any of it.
Not one thing.
Whatever else happened, Jin Wikyung’s judgment was right.
Outside the gorge, the terrain opened into a broad basin beyond its narrow, jar-like entrance. There, the battle raged on without either side giving an inch.
*Thud-thud-thud!*
*Shhk! KRAAA-BOOM!*
The Hebei Peng Family and the nomads.
The nomads and the Hebei Peng Family.
The two forces had shared a border and been at odds for many years. Now they swung their weapons and shouted themselves hoarse as if facing the enemies of a lifetime.
“They’re weak barbarians! Crush them in one blow!”
“Brothers of the Great Steppe! Will you retreat before a mere handful of Han Chinese?”
Those cries, carried on the wind as they rang out against each other, perfectly reflected the situation they were in.
The Hebei Peng Family’s martial artists were individually superior. But the nomads outnumbered them more than ten to one, surrounded them on all sides, and attacked without pause.
“Attack! Don’t fall back—surround them!”
“Break through!”
Sharp spears against enormous shields.

If the Thunderbolt Saber King had stayed, the Hebei Peng Family would have held the advantage. But after throwing the enemy ranks into disarray, he had headed into the gorge with some of his elite fighters. The nomads had quickly closed the gap in their encirclement and counterattacked.
Still, a trace of unease lingered in their hearts.
*If this keeps up...*
*This is bad. Very bad.*
The Keshik centurions Jamukha had left outside the gorge exchanged grim looks.
The Hebei Peng Family’s sudden arrival had sent the morale of the Shanxi fighters soaring, while brutally crushing the nomads’ momentum.
There was the imposing presence of a master like the Thunderbolt Saber King.
And there was the Hebei Peng Family’s reputation, which had kept the nomads from daring to encroach on Hebei.
Some of the centurions were already reaching inside their robes without realizing it.
*If we use that now, we could turn this battle around in an instant.*
But the thought quickly faded.
They remembered Jamukha’s order—the command of the absolute ruler of the Great Steppe, the lord they served.
“No one uses it without my order. This won’t be the last battle we have to fight.”
They had not objected to that firm command or doubted it in the slightest.
Not simply because they were his subjects, but because it was Jamukha who had given it.
Jamukha was always coolheaded and certain. Everything he had said so far had proved right, and this would, too.
That wouldn’t change even if the opponent was the Thunderbolt Saber King.
They had only one small question.
*What made him so certain?*
Before they reached Shanxi Province, Jamukha had already predicted that other enemies would come to the aid of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
And he had declared without a trace of doubt:
“Nothing will change. Nothing at all.”
As the centurions recalled those words from several days ago and watched the battlefield with questioning eyes—
*Rrrrattle.*
Beyond the vast basin, where tens of thousands of enemies and allies were tangled together, a group suddenly emerged from the darkness. All at once, they drew their bows.
*Shwaaaaa!*
Beneath the storm clouds, thousands of arrowheads flashed as they cut through the wind and plunged down.
