Outside the gorge, the terrain opened into a broad basin beyond its narrow, jar-like entrance.
There, the battle raged on without either side giving an inch.
*Thud-thud-thud!*
*Shhk!
KRAAA-BOOM!*
The Hebei Peng Family and the nomads.
The nomads and the Hebei Peng Family.
The two forces had shared a border and been at odds for many years.
Now they swung their weapons and shouted themselves hoarse as if facing the enemies of a lifetime.
“They’re weak barbarians!
Crush them in one blow!”
“Brothers of the Great Steppe!
Will you retreat before a mere handful of Han Chinese?”
Those cries, carried on the wind as they rang out against each other, perfectly reflected the situation they were in.
The Hebei Peng Family’s martial artists were individually superior.
But the nomads outnumbered them more than ten to one, surrounded them on all sides, and attacked without pause.
“Attack!
Don’t fall back—surround them!”
“Break through!”
Sharp spears against enormous shields.
If the Thunderbolt Saber King had stayed, the Hebei Peng Family would have held the advantage.
But after throwing the enemy ranks into disarray, he had headed into the gorge with some of his elite fighters.
The nomads had quickly closed the gap in their encirclement and counterattacked.
Still, a trace of unease lingered in their hearts.
*If this keeps up...*
*This is bad.
Very bad.*
The Keshik centurions Jamukha had left outside the gorge exchanged grim looks.
The Hebei Peng Family’s sudden arrival had sent the morale of the Shanxi fighters soaring, while brutally crushing the nomads’ momentum.
There was the imposing presence of a master like the Thunderbolt Saber King.
And there was the Hebei Peng Family’s reputation, which had kept the nomads from daring to encroach on Hebei.
Some of the centurions were already reaching inside their robes without realizing it.
*If we use that now, we could turn this battle around in an instant.*
But the thought quickly faded.
They remembered Jamukha’s order—the command of the absolute ruler of the Great Steppe, the lord they served.
“No one uses it without my order.
This won’t be the last battle we have to fight.”
They had not objected to that firm command or doubted it in the slightest.
Not simply because they were his subjects, but because it was Jamukha who had given it.
Jamukha was always coolheaded and certain.
Everything he had said so far had proved right, and this would, too.
That wouldn’t change even if the opponent was the Thunderbolt Saber King.
They had only one small question.
*What made him so certain?*
Before they reached Shanxi Province, Jamukha had already predicted that other enemies would come to the aid of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
And he had declared without a trace of doubt:
“Nothing will change.
Nothing at all.”
As the centurions recalled those words from several days ago and watched the battlefield with questioning eyes—
*Rrrrattle.*
Beyond the vast basin, where tens of thousands of enemies and allies were tangled together, a group suddenly emerged from the darkness.
All at once, they drew their bows.
*Shwaaaaa!*
Beneath the storm clouds, thousands of arrowheads flashed as they cut through the wind and plunged down.

chapters.title: Chapter 967
paragraphs: To a martial artist, martial arts were like fingerprints: each person’s took a different shape.
Even disciples who studied under the same master, learned the same martial arts, and followed the same formulas would move differently according to their temperaments and physical traits.
A man who doesn’t fear death might use a sword technique more boldly than prescribed. Someone with short arms and legs might widen their stride when using a footwork technique.
And at that moment, something about Jamukha felt strangely familiar to Peng Cheolhu, the Thunderbolt Saber King.
*BOOM! BOOM! KRAAA-BOOM!*
The two saber blades clashed without pause, accompanied by a barrage of fierce impacts.
Beyond them, Jamukha’s calm face—and every movement he made—grew more familiar the longer the Thunderbolt Saber King watched.
*What is it?*
For a martial artist who had reached a high realm, letting his mind wander during a life-and-death duel was forbidden.
Yet the Thunderbolt Saber King kept watching Jamukha, breaking that rule until he finally recalled a scene buried deep in his memory.
*Could it be?*
His eyes flew wide.
Jamukha seized that instant of distraction and brought his crescent saber down with all his might.
*BOOM! KRRRACK!*
Two sabers worthy of being called treasured blades locked together, scattering sparks.
Neither man gave an inch. The Thunderbolt Saber King studied Jamukha’s face beyond their crossed blades, his gaze growing grave.
“I wondered where a barbarian like you had come from... Now I see we’ve met before.”
Jamukha was silent for a moment. Then he spoke in Chinese so fluent that no nomad from the western steppe, so far from the Central Plains, should have known it so well.
“So you finally remember. Your head’s still as thick as ever, Thunderbolt Saber Peng Cheolhu.”
“Thunderbolt Saber. There was a time when they called me that.”
The Thunderbolt Saber King murmured as if to himself.
Only one character separated that title from his current one, but more than half a lifetime lay between them.
The first time the two had crossed paths was before the unprecedented Great War called the Great Faction War, back when Peng Cheolhu was the Lesser Family Head of the Hebei Peng Family.
*I thought so. He’s that barbarian from back then.*
The Thunderbolt Saber King looked at Jamukha with fresh eyes.

It was a fragment of a memory more than half a century old. And yet he could still dredge it up from his aging mind because the young nomad, who had rampaged like a wolf despite his terrible injuries, had left such a powerful impression on him.
*Right. That’s how it was.*
Nomads crossed the Great Wall and raided the borderlands. Those who lived there fought to protect their homes and possessions.
Such clashes were a fact of life along the frontier near the Great Steppe. Hebei, where the Peng Family stood like a great tree, was no exception.
What made this encounter different was the young chieftain who had risen to power amid the turmoil of the eastern steppe. He had set his sights on Hebei and brought thousands of warriors with him.
Even along a frontier accustomed to raids and resistance, that was rare.
No—it was the first large-scale invasion in over a decade.

Peng Cheolhu had led his family in place of the bedridden Family Head. Recognizing the gravity of the situation, the Murong Family had sent a thousand elite fighters to help, including its own Lesser Family Head.
The Hebei Peng Family and the Murong Family each held a place among the Five Great Families. Their forces were led by two Lesser Family Heads emerging as the finest young masters of their generation.
Before the Great Faction War, the two families had been at odds over supremacy in the north. Their dramatic alliance proved enough to secure a fitting reward.
A flawless victory, without a single misstep.
Or perhaps a glorious triumph.
No one in the world questioned either description.

So complete was their victory that the young chieftain of the eastern steppe, routed by Peng Cheolhu and the Hebei Peng Family, had barely escaped the Murong Family’s pursuit when its fighters arrived.
Leaving behind only the blood of the countless warriors who had followed him.
Then he vanished without a trace, seemingly forever.
Or so everyone, including the Thunderbolt Saber King, had believed.
Until they met again today.
“I never thought you’d still be alive. You’re a hard one to kill.”
They said a needle in a bag would eventually poke through. Someone that sharp was bound to reveal himself—even if he was out on the vast steppe rather than inside a bag.
Yet the young chieftain, with ambition and skill to spare, had not shown himself for more than half a century. The nomads had never invaded Hebei again.
That was why the Thunderbolt Saber King had forgotten Jamukha.

Barbarian or not, a man of his ability would not have failed to rise again without good reason. Peng Cheolhu had assumed that the wounds he’d inflicted that day had killed him, or that he’d fallen victim to another conflict on the steppe.
Whatever had happened, Peng Cheolhu had been certain of the outcome: Jamukha was dead.
“I should’ve done whatever it took to root you out back then. I should’ve torn out the source of this trouble.”
The Thunderbolt Saber King sighed quietly across their locked blades. Jamukha saw him reflected in his own gleaming eyes.
“I couldn’t die. Not before I repaid an old debt.”
Jamukha spat out the words.
How could he forget that bitter past?

He had returned from Hebei in defeat, then left the eastern steppe with the surviving members of his tribe. After marching thousands of li, he had reached its distant western edge and raised a ger of his own.

There, he could no longer see the hated banners of the Hebei Peng Family. There, he could avoid the teeth of the wolves waiting for his downfall. He settled in and waited for his chance to rise again.
Some fifty years flowed by like a river.
So much changed.

The new name he had taken to avoid a possible pursuit—Jamukha—had become a symbol of authority across the western steppe. His ranks teemed with fine steeds and warriors like hunting dogs. The few dozen gers he had started with had grown into tens of thousands of households.
But even when he had become all but king of the steppe, Jamukha had not forgotten Peng Cheolhu’s saber cutting across his body like a bolt of lightning.
Nor had he forgotten the humiliation of that defeat.
*Wooooom.*
The green Force around his crescent saber set the air trembling as it swelled larger and larger.
In Jamukha’s gaze, fixed on the Thunderbolt Saber King, lay a past he had yet to put to rest.
“Thunderbolt Saber. No—Thunderbolt Saber King Peng Cheolhu.”

The young chieftain who had dreamed of restoring his ancestors’ achievements had returned as the absolute ruler of the steppe, leading a vast army. The Lesser Family Head of the Hebei Peng Family, who had taken everything from him, had come through the Great Faction War to become one of the Ten Kings—a great tree supporting the martial world.
One thing, though, had not changed: their old grudge.
“Do you still not understand?”
*Krrrrk.*
The crescent saber, engulfed in radiant green Force, pressed down on the great saber.
The Thunderbolt Saber King groaned as his blade trembled. Jamukha’s lips twisted.
“I waited. I waited for you—for the Hebei Peng Family—to appear here.”
The Thunderbolt Saber King’s eyes widened at the unexpected words.
*KA-BOOM!*
With a thunderclap that seemed to split the sky, the great saber—until then like a colossal wall—was forced back, unable to withstand the crescent saber’s power.
*KRAAAASH!*
A gale swept through. Part of the rocky cliff cracked and burst apart under the terrible pressure.
Yet even amid the dust swirling around them, Jamukha moved with precision and speed.
*Shwaa!*
Space split along his saber’s path. Streams of green Force shot from the crescent-shaped blade toward the retreating Thunderbolt Saber King.
*BOOM! BOOM!*
The roar of the two sabers colliding had already gone beyond the realm of steel.
Jamukha’s gaze, so composed until now, had begun to boil like lava. So had the voice rising from his lips.
Just like—
“I’ll kill you! Every last one of you!”
—the young chieftain who had lost everything in a bitter defeat and been forced to leave.
*FWOOOSH!*
Green Force erupted from his saber with all his strength. The dazzling beam lit the gorge like an early dawn as it slashed diagonally toward the Thunderbolt Saber King.
*Shhk!*
A single, chilling sound of something being cut rang out amid the flash.
“Cough.”
*Thud, thud.*
The Thunderbolt Saber King staggered backward, spat out a mouthful of blood, and looked at Jamukha. Pain from his internal injuries twisted his deeply furrowed brow.
“...Impressive. Truly impressive.”
There was no sarcasm in his voice. He meant it.

As a martial artist and a warrior who carried on the Peng Family’s legacy, the Thunderbolt Saber King admired Jamukha’s patience through all those years spent seeking revenge for his defeat. He admired his astonishing martial prowess.
And he admired Jamukha himself—a man who had kept his wits about him to the very end, even with his revenge almost within reach.
“How did you think to pull back? You had the perfect chance.”
Even an enemy deserved respect when he had shown courage and fighting spirit worthy of praise.
But Jamukha did not answer the Thunderbolt Saber King’s question.
No—he couldn’t answer.
*Crack.*
The sound was so faint it could only be heard by someone listening closely. His crescent saber trembled, and in the next instant—
*KA-BOOM!*
—the blade shattered. Blood spraying from Jamukha’s shoulder fell onto the fragments of steel.
*FWASH! THUD-THUD-THUD!*
The blood bursting through his skin was red. Pain surged from his deeply cut shoulder and his internal organs, hot as lightning, as fire.
Through the searing agony, Jamukha steadied himself and spoke.
“Cough. How—how did you...?”
He could not understand it.

The martial arts of the Hebei Peng Family were the very embodiment of domineering power. For generations, its members had made their name throughout the world with strength honed through training and explosive internal energy cultivated through their techniques. That reliance was also their one limitation.
So Jamukha had pursued speed above all else.

For the past fifty years, he had trained in saber techniques of the utmost speed and studied the Thunderbolt Saber King’s martial arts, believing the speed he had perfected would overcome the Hebei Peng Family’s overwhelming power.
But—
“Why? How...!”
As the Thunderbolt Saber King approached, steadying himself despite his internal injuries, Jamukha cried out, his voice thick with blood.
Unlike Jamukha, who had been unable to answer the earlier question, the Thunderbolt Saber King replied calmly.
“The Great Faction War. On that damn battlefield, I learned there were plenty of monsters in this world worse than this old man.”
Enlightenment had no end. Progress was not a privilege reserved for the young.
Especially not for an old master like the Thunderbolt Saber King.
“Among them, there was this crazy old man who toyed with me and laughed at me. Said I was built like a bear and moved like molasses.”
The Fire King, Jeok Cheongang.
Hoping to surpass that deranged old monster someday, Peng Cheolhu had kept training even after peace returned.
He had not missed a single day.
“Still don’t understand?”
The Thunderbolt Saber King raised his massive saber upright and looked at Jamukha, who was groaning as he clutched his half-severed shoulder.
“How Peng Cheolhu, the Thunderbolt Saber, became the Thunderbolt Saber King?”
Only one character separated the two titles.
But in this vast world, only ten great martial artists had earned the right to be called kings. They stood beneath the endless sky and three stars.
“The only place you can be called a king is out there on the steppe.”
Peng Cheolhu, the Thunderbolt Saber King, looked at Jamukha’s wide eyes and laughed aloud.

chapters.title: Chapter 968
paragraphs: Someone once said:
*When three people walk together, one of them is sure to have something to teach me.*
Of course, the Thunderbolt Saber King wasn’t sure whether it had been Confucius or Mencius.
But the main reason he was smiling now was that he’d thought of someone who wasn’t there.
*If it weren’t for the Fire King—that crazy old man—I’d never have grown stronger.*
He had spent his life in the spotlight. Not merely because he’d been born into the Hebei Peng Family, one of the Five Great Families, but because he had the talent and skill to earn that attention.
Namgung Cheon. Murong Baek. Peng Cheolhu.

Of all the young prodigies born to prestigious families, those three had stood above the rest. Unexpected misfortune had kept Murong Baek from joining the other two at the top, while Namgung Cheon and Peng Cheolhu had come to be known as the Sword King and the Saber King.
But the Thunderbolt Saber King knew why he had made it that far.
Fire King Jeok Cheongang.
That old man had laid into him at every opportunity. Without him, Peng Cheolhu would have kept treading water instead of growing stronger.
“I’ll tell you something. That grassland you were born and raised on isn’t as vast as you think.”
The Thunderbolt Saber King slowly raised his great saber toward Jamukha, who trembled as he clutched the shoulder Peng’s Force had nearly severed.
Toward the king of the steppe, holding back a groan before a giant who stood tall beneath heaven.
“Now, let’s finish this.”
*Whoosh.*
With a single step, the space between them vanished.
The Thunderbolt Saber King’s form blurred. For a man of his enormous build, he moved at an unbelievable speed, yet the path of the great saber plunging down like lightning was precise and controlled.
*Shhk!*
A single slicing sound rang out. Pain spread through Jamukha like fire, and he clenched his teeth against the scream rising in his throat.
He’d dodged. He should have dodged.
But the wound in his shoulder throbbed without cease. The Thunderbolt Saber King’s internal energy had seeped through it and shaken his organs, slowing his feet.
*Wooooom.*
A resonant hum filled everyone’s ears.
Jamukha’s crescent saber lay shattered. The Thunderbolt Saber King’s great saber bore only a few scratches. It trembled, then surged forward once more.
No. It split as it advanced.
The single blade became five, then ten, then dozens. Its afterimages formed an enormous net and shot forward.
The Thunderbolt Saber King spoke quietly.
“Go.”
There was certainty in his voice and in his eyes as he faced Jamukha. Not a trace of carelessness toward a wounded, bleeding enemy—only confidence in his own strike and his own skill.
*Fwoooosh!*
The net of Force swept down. Jamukha threw himself backward, but the immense energy stayed close on his heels, cutting through everything it touched.
The cliffs on either side. The rocks and corpses scattered across the ground.
Even the loyal men who rushed in to save him.
“Stop him! The Khan is in danger—!”
*Puk! Fwoooooosh!*
No scream followed.
Those who had rushed forward with desperate cries crumpled into dozens of chunks of flesh. Jamukha, teeth clenched, reached for a weapon abandoned by its owner.
*Woom.*
The air shuddered. A crescent saber flew into his hand, drawn by Seizing an Object Through Empty Space, and he unleashed a burst of Force.
*BOOM!*
Part of the net scattered. Jamukha swallowed the blood that surged up his throat as the impact shook his entire body.
His saber techniques, wielded with only one arm, were slower. Every time he met a strike head-on, the impact battered his insides, which kept screaming in pain.
But—
*Do you think I’ll die like this? And at your hands?*
With that cry in his heart, Jamukha sent his crescent saber flashing in every direction.

Thunderous impacts rang out, flashes of light filling his vision. Beyond them, the distant past swept through his mind: his younger self struggling to survive, clenching his teeth until they bled as he swore revenge. And the voice of someone who had willingly reached out to him.
“Don’t you want to live?”
He had thought everything was over.

The warriors who had once numbered in the thousands had been all but wiped out by the Hebei Peng Family’s elite, led by Peng Cheolhu. His rivals had been waiting for his fall. They would take his livestock and wealth, then enslave the few people his tribe had left.
That was the law of the steppe, passed down through the survival of the strong.
But just when he thought it was over, one last chance appeared.
Sitting amid the wreckage of his ambitions and the bodies of his men, the young chieftain seized the hand held out to him—the lifeline dropped from heaven—with all his strength.
“I want to live. No—I must survive!”
“If you live, what will you live for?”
“Revenge. I’ll repay today’s humiliation and grudge, no matter what. If you save me, I swear by Tengri...”
“I’m not helping you.”
“What do you mean?”
“I’m using you.”
He did not think for long. The decision he made in that instant was as firm as an iron tower.
“Show me the path I must follow, my lord.”
The savior smiled, pleased to see him prostrate himself like a slave. He pointed beyond the endless horizon.
“Go. Build a new home where neither the Hebei Peng Family nor the eyes of the Central Plains can reach you.”
“You mean I should head west?”
“Don’t worry. The west is still in chaos, and you’re no longer alone. You have ‘us’ now.”
“Yes. We’ll help you, Jamukha—warrior of the Great Steppe, reborn here today.”
The savior had been right.
The young chieftain left with a new name and soon distinguished himself on the western steppe. The greatest reason he was able to build such a powerful force was the savior’s support.
Livestock and wealth in vast quantities. Even people and information.
“They’re quite capable. Make good use of them.”
And so Jamukha’s personal guard, the Keshik, was born.

“These are supreme martial arts for you to learn, along with the Hebei Peng Family’s martial arts. They don’t include the secret techniques passed down to only a select few, but studying them will certainly help you.”
The savior had even given him a sword and shield with which to face the enemy of a lifetime—the man who had since become the Thunderbolt Saber King.
*Clang!*
The crash shattered his reverie. Blood burst from his torn palm, and Jamukha swung his crescent saber wildly at the net of Force bearing down on him.

One arm was useless, its flesh, muscle, and even bone torn apart. But the immense internal energy he had accumulated over long years still flowed into his fingertips, along with the supreme martial arts he had learned.
So did a memory from years after he had settled on the western steppe.
“Tell me. When should we march?”
“Not yet. Wait. You are not to leave the west until you receive an explicit order.”
“Not yet? How much longer must I wait?”
*What?*
“If I keep waiting for that order, we’ll miss our chance. The Central Plains are in turmoil because of the Great Faction War. If we strike Hebei now...”
“Remarkable. A hunting dog that speaks like a man.”
“Draw your saber. Now.”

The savior’s eyes filled with killing intent. Jamukha did not refuse. He charged—and found himself facing a wall that seemed even higher and more imposing than the one he had encountered against Peng Cheolhu in his youth. He fell to his knees.
Only then did he understand.
“Remember this. Until ‘that person’ gives the order, we do not move.”
“...That person?”
Even the savior, who had seemed like heaven itself to Jamukha, was someone else’s hunting dog.
From the beginning, the “us” he spoke of had meant something far deeper and more powerful than Jamukha had imagined.
“Keep that in mind until the day you take your revenge and claim the steppe. You will not be forgiven twice.”
Jamukha felt neither humiliation nor defiance. He trembled with fear and joy.

If he followed the owner of the leash around his neck, he could reach the goal that had seemed to be slipping farther and farther away. Once that master had swallowed the world, he would toss the vast Great Steppe to the hunting dog who had carried out his task.
“...As you command.”
From that day on, every trace of defiance vanished from Jamukha’s heart. Years passed, frost settling in his hair, until one day he realized the time had finally come.
“What is this?”
“A kind of pill. It lets you draw on power beyond your limits for a short time, though you’ll pay a price to match.”
Its effects were too ominous for a spiritual elixir. The savior called it a Temporary Strength Pill.
“Why are you giving it to me?”
“Consider it an experiment. For the near future.”
“Then... could it be?”
“That person has awakened. Begin building a bridgehead for our advance into the Central Plains.”
After a wait of more than fifty years, the last few years passed in a flash.

On orders, Jamukha scattered pills and a number of martial arts manuals across the steppe. Each pill found its own owner. Armed with power they could never have imagined, those people spread chaos and disrupted the established order.
Not just on the steppe, but in the Central Plains beyond the Great Wall.
Pung Yang.

The leader of the mounted bandits known as the Red Wind Band on the eastern steppe was an ambitious man. With the Temporary Strength Pill’s help, he built his forces at an astonishing pace. Then he turned his horse toward Shanxi Province and met his death there.
His killer was the scion of a borderland martial family in slow decline, a young man with the unfamiliar epithet Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi.
*Jin Taekyung. Jin Taekyung...*
Roughly two years passed. So much happened in that time.

The Jin Family of Taiyuan rose to rule Shanxi Province. On the eastern steppe, where Jamukha’s old name had been forgotten, two young upstarts named Temur and Chinggen distinguished themselves. Far away in the Central Plains, the Star-Array Grand Banquet was held.
Then, like dams breaking one after another, everything that had been held back burst forth.
The bloodshed began with Shaolin Temple in Henan, swept through Sichuan and Anhui, then spread as far as distant Yunnan.

The Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi came to be called the Divine Dragon. Sensing danger, the people of the Central Plains gathered under the Murim Alliance’s banner. Even the great sects drew back, wary of an enemy blade that might strike at any moment.
Of course, none of this applied to Jamukha.
Dark Heaven, which everyone in the Central Plains dreaded, was “us” to him.
This was the moment he had waited for all his life.
“By the coming Double Ninth Festival, take control of the eastern steppe. Mobilize every soldier and seize Shanxi.”
Jamukha summoned his warriors at once. After so long a wait, he moved with lightning speed.
At last he assembled an army drawn from across the steppe. The savior, meanwhile, passed along timely news from beyond the Great Wall.
The strength of Shanxi Province, gathered around the Jin Family of Taiyuan. The place where the fiercest fighting was expected.
And one last thing.
“The Thunderbolt Saber King will go there. Without fail.”
He had even given Jamukha the place where he could finally settle his oldest grudge.
Everything had happened as the savior predicted.
Except for one thing.
*Why? Why?!*
With a cry that circled only on the tip of his tongue, Jamukha twisted his unsteady body around.
*Shhk! Puh-puh-puk!*
Pain like a branding iron.
He could see the attacks coming. His mind registered them. His body simply could not move fast enough.
The net of Force that had pursued him relentlessly had faded after leaving dozens of large and small wounds across his body. But beyond it stood a great tiger that would never let its prey escape.
Lips pressed tight. Eyes alight with a cold flame.
Both hands gripped the great saber so hard they had gone white. Brilliant light enveloped the blade from end to end.
*Whoooom.*
The Thunderbolt Saber King swung without hesitation. Jamukha watched the terrible strike, a fusion of defeat and swiftness, cut through the air.
And he understood.
Only one choice remained. Even if that choice left him drained and collapsed in this narrow gorge, it would be a hundred—a thousand—times better than dying at the Thunderbolt Saber King’s hands.
*Shk.*
As the Force came at him from several yards away, the world seemed to slow. Jamukha took something from inside his robe.
He tossed the small, blood-red pill into his mouth without hesitation.
Or tried to.
At that very moment, a flash of light fell from above.
*Thuk!*
Through a stab of pain and disbelief, Jamukha saw a spearhead gleaming in five colors.
It had pierced the back of his hand—and the Temporary Strength Pill in his grasp. His last hope.
Jamukha looked up, forgetting even the pain.
The owner of the spear that had fallen from the darkened sky spoke not to Jamukha, but to the Thunderbolt Saber King.
“With people like this, no amount of caution is ever enough. Don’t you agree?”
*Shwaa!*
The great saber, poised to sweep everything away, whistled through the air and stopped.
The Thunderbolt Saber King recognized the face. A surprised smile touched his lips.
“I knew you’d come.”
He looked at the graying, middle-aged man, who appeared twenty years younger than he truly was, and spoke with deep feeling.
“It’s been a long time, Murong Baek. Or should I call you Family Head Murong now?”

They had fought countless times for supremacy in the north. Through the Great Faction War, they had become true comrades and friends. The Thunderbolt Saber King grinned broadly at Murong Baek and lowered his saber.
Good.
The war was over.
Jamukha could no longer fight, and the elite fighters Murong Baek had brought from the Murong Family must already have joined the battle.
Just as he expected, a shout rose from beyond the gorge.
“The Murong Family! It’s the Murong Family!”
The tension that had held the Thunderbolt Saber King’s entire body taut began to ease.
At least, until a panicked shout from someone who was surely a member of the Hebei Peng Family followed in the next moment.
“Grand Family Head! The enemy—the Murong Family—!”
*What?*
For an instant, the Thunderbolt Saber King’s thoughts stopped. A sudden chill sank deep into his body.
*Shhk!*
Through the blinding pain, he heard a quiet voice.
“I told you. You can never be too careful.”
As his vision faded, the Thunderbolt Saber King understood.
Jamukha.
The young chieftain who should have lost all his forces and died a defeated man—how had he shaken off his pursuers and survived until now?
*The Murong Family.*
Of course.
More than fifty years ago, the man who had pursued him was Murong Baek.
The true source of all this calamity.

paragraphs: The people of Shanxi didn’t see what happened in that fleeting moment.
They were throwing all their strength into driving back the enemies who filled the gaps among the corpses of men and horses and between the scattered rocks.
No—even if they’d been nearby, they wouldn’t have seen a thing.
The strike was so natural and swift that it could deceive the Qi Sense of a Supreme Peak master ranked among the top three of the Ten Kings.
*Shhk!*
Through pain that felt like fire, the Thunderbolt Saber King summoned superhuman endurance to keep his body from collapsing.
He trembled at the unbelievable truth that had struck him like a giant iron hammer.
*So that’s what happened.*
Now he knew. At last, he understood.
Why the young chieftain who had crossed the Great Wall and invaded Hebei had survived.
Why a man who, for all his ambition and skill, had been no more than an exceptional nomad had gained such powerful internal energy and learned martial arts unknown on the steppe.
That day, Jamukha hadn’t survived.
He’d been spared.
By the Murong Family that had pursued him. By the man who had led them.
*Murong Baek.*
His vision blurred with rage and pain. Pressing a trembling hand to the deep gash in his chest to stop the bleeding, the Thunderbolt Saber King stared in shock at the middle-aged man before him.
His features looked as though they belonged somewhere between the Han Chinese and the nomads.
“Impressive. You managed to react even then.”
His voice was as still as a quiet pond.
Yet his sword—when had he drawn it?—was already coming down like a flash of light.
*Whoosh!*
The air screamed.
The Thunderbolt Saber King’s eyes widened at the merciless strike from Murong Baek, whom he had believed to be his friend.
Twisting away on instinct at the last moment had saved his life, but nothing more.
The Force that had cut deep across his chest left his whole body heavy as soaked cotton.
*Boom! Krrrk!*
His great saber wavered as it barely caught the sword.
Murong Baek let out a quiet exclamation. Even with his internal energy in disarray, the Thunderbolt Saber King had blocked the attack.
“As I thought. You’re still absurdly strong.”
“Murong Baek, how could you...!”
The Thunderbolt Saber King clenched his teeth until blood came.
The Murong Family and the Hebei Peng Family.
The Hebei Peng Family and the Murong Family.
It was true that the two families, known throughout the world, had once been at odds.
But that was the past.
An old feud long since buried by the years.

Even now, the Thunderbolt Saber King could hardly believe that Murong Baek had betrayed him. Murong Baek, who had fought back-to-back with him in the Great Faction War. The rival of his youth who had become his friend, who had grown old alongside him.
No. He had betrayed everyone on this land.
“When? When did you...”
His breathing was ragged with anger and shock. Beyond the trembling blades, he fixed the traitor with his gaze and moved his split lips.
“When did you join hands with Dark Heaven?”
Murong Baek answered by pressing his sword harder against the great saber. Force surged along the blade toward its tip.
*Shhk.*
The Thunderbolt Saber King swallowed a groan.
It burned. Murong Baek’s Force had reached his skin before the sword, and now it was digging into his collarbone.
Slowly. Little by little.
Cutting through flesh and bone as though it would not stop until it reached his heart.
“Graaaah!”
Blood burst between his clenched teeth.
Roaring like a furious tiger, the Thunderbolt Saber King drove his great saber upward.
His rage blotted out the pain. Through the Chaos Thunderbolt Divine Art, reserved for the Hebei Peng Family Head, he poured every last bit of internal energy in his body into the blade.
*BOOM!*
With a crash like the sky splitting apart, Murong Baek’s sword was knocked away.
Agony tore through his damaged acupoints and the collarbone split by Force. The Thunderbolt Saber King endured it with a will harder than steel and thrust out his hand.
“You bastard!”
*Poom!*
Compressed air burst outward.
A strike from the Great Strength Vajra Palm, a technique the Hebei Peng Family took pride in, swept toward Murong Baek with such ferocity that it outran its own sound.
For the briefest moment, at least, that was how it looked.
*Shwaa!*
A flash of light—and it was over.
Murong Baek’s figure blurred as he cut apart the palm force flying with the wind. The instant the Thunderbolt Saber King thought he saw him disappear, a red warning light flashed in his mind.
*Shifting Form and Position!*
There was no time to stop the bleeding from his collarbone. No time to swing his great saber.
He twisted with all his strength and turned toward the fleeting presence behind him, throwing a punch.
*Whoosh.*
It connected.
Not with a human body of flesh and bone, but with the wind, crushed beneath his fist.
At the same instant, he sensed it: a flash of light shooting beneath the fist he’d swung through empty air, scattering icy killing intent.
The world slowed. Eyes wide, the Thunderbolt Saber King moved by instinct rather than reason.
He let go of the great saber he had carried all his life and reached for the flash closing in on his chest.
*Thuk.*
The sound of flesh being pierced rang out, sharp and slow.
The pointed sword tip drove through the Palm Force he’d hastily summoned as though it were tofu, cut through the flesh and bone of his hand, and emerged from the back of it.
As though that obstacle were nothing, it kept driving toward its target.
Until the Thunderbolt Saber King, holding back a scream, gripped the blade with all his strength.
*Krrrk!*
The sword stopped.
No—more precisely, it broke.
*Plip.*
Fragments of the blade fell with his blood.
His whole body went rigid under the overwhelming pain of his hand being crushed in an instant.
All he could do was stare, eyes wide, at Murong Baek staring back. Then he watched, dazed, as Murong Baek—without so much as a scratch on him—thrust out a palm.
*Fwoosh.*
Beyond the dazzling light filling his vision, Murong Baek’s quiet voice reached him as faintly as a dream.
“You fought well. Like a true warrior.”
And then—
*Poom.*
An explosion sounded deep inside his body, and the Thunderbolt Saber King’s world turned upside down.
A massive tremor swept through the gorge.
*KABOOM!*
The ground shook. With a thunderous crash, part of the cliff collapsed.
Even rock built up by nature over ages too long to measure had given way. A human body of flesh stood no chance.
*Krrrrk!*
Boulders that had been part of the cliff came crashing down beneath the immense weight of earth and sand above them. Dust and debris flew wildly in every direction.
Yet even in the pale cloud, where he couldn’t see a hand in front of his face, Murong Baek kept his eyes fixed on one spot.
He slowly closed the hand that had brought about this devastation, taking in everything within several dozen *zhang* through his Qi Sense.
Including a faint cough that had just escaped from beneath a shifting mound of earth.
*Khk.*
Murong Baek didn’t turn his head. He merely reached out and eased the weight of earth pressing down on the person who had coughed.
He retrieved something that had once belonged to him as well.
*Wooooom.*
The air shuddered as immense qi flowed from his gesture. Then a spear buried deep in the ground flew into his grasp as though pulled by an invisible string.
Fresh blood ran down it—proof that it had pierced someone’s flesh and bone.
“Thank you.”
Jamukha’s voice came from behind him. Murong Baek spoke without turning.
“Why didn’t you follow my orders? I told you to buy as much time as possible.”
“Well...”
“I suppose you underestimated the Thunderbolt Saber King.”
Jamukha bit his lip instead of answering.
Murong Baek was right. He had disobeyed his savior.
Holding his own against the Thunderbolt Saber King had made him greedy. Little by little, he had pushed aside Murong Baek’s order to wait for him.
And there was one more order he had pushed aside.
He, at least, was never to take the Temporary Strength Pill.
“I have no excuse.”
“No, you don’t. If you’d swallowed it, we wouldn’t be having this conversation.”
The Temporary Strength Pill was a double-edged sword.

The early versions that had found their way into the hands of Pung Yang, the Red Wind Band Leader, and others were dangerous enough. Even the newly improved pill was highly addictive and carried severe side effects.
The ordinary foot soldiers might take it, but Jamukha could not. He was the commander-in-chief of a great army, with much yet to do.
Not from Murong Baek’s point of view, when he had placed Jamukha at the forefront.
“How are you?”
“Not as bad as you might think. Once I finish regulating my qi, my Internal Injury should heal soon.”
Despite his words, nearly half of one shoulder had been cut away. His future as a saber fighter was in danger, yet there was not a trace of gloom on his face.
Jamukha knew how mysterious and powerful his savior’s Dark Heaven was—the Dark Heaven Murong Baek had called “us” long ago.
With no worry at all showing on his face, he went on.
“Though that bastard will be wandering the Nine Springs now, unlike me.”
That was when Murong Baek’s gaze, fixed in one direction all this time, shifted to Jamukha.
“You still have a long way to go.”
“What do you...?”
Jamukha trailed off. Suddenly understanding what Murong Baek meant, he bit his lip.
“You’re saying he’s alive? The Thunderbolt Saber King? Even now?”
It was a natural question.
He had seen what happened with his own eyes: the Thunderbolt Saber King crumbling beneath Murong Baek’s attacks, delivered without hesitation or mercy.
A palm strike of terrifying power had driven him deep into the cliff, where he’d looked like a corpse as he spat blood.
But unlike Jamukha, Murong Baek could sense a thread of breath beneath the countless rocks and mounds of earth.
*Stubborn bastard. Just as always.*
Thinking back, the Thunderbolt Saber King—Peng Cheolhu—had always been like that.

His natural strength and sturdy body had made him stand out not only within the Hebei Peng Family but among the young prodigies of the entire world. The countless battlefields he had crossed had been no exception.
*He always survived. Always.*
So Murong Baek intended to end the Thunderbolt Saber King’s life with his own hands.

And now that the cliffs had collapsed in front of and behind them, shutting out every witness nearby, he needed to kill all the survivors, including the Thunderbolt Saber King. Any one of them might pose a risk.
The longer his secret remained hidden, the better.
Then he could deal another devastating blow to the reinforcements coming from the Nine Sects and One Gang.
*At least half a day until Huashan and Zhongnan arrive.*
There was still plenty of time.
Once everything was ready, Murong Baek would meet the orthodox faction’s reinforcements right here.
By then, he would have dealt with the Thunderbolt Saber King. The Hebei Peng Family martial artists beyond the gorge, now falling to the Murong Family’s unexpected ambush, would be dead as well.
So would the people of Shanxi, slaughtering nomads on the far side of the suddenly collapsed cliff.
First, though, he must not forget the rats hiding beneath the earth, holding their breath.
*Shhk.*
His spearhead swept through like a streak of light, splitting a huge boulder and the mound of earth beneath it as easily as tofu.
Murong Baek looked down impassively at Jin Mukyung, who held the bloodied Cheol Mubaek and Wipeng in his arms.
Without a word, he brought his spear straight down.
No—he was about to.
*Whoooom.*
A tremendous rush of air sounded from somewhere, and Murong Baek turned his head on instinct.
He saw it.
*KABOOOM!*
A spear came crashing through, smashing apart the great mass of cliff rock in its path.
A blue-white flame burned along its icy, translucent spearhead.

chapters.title: Chapter 970
paragraphs: In the hazy darkness, unable to see an inch ahead, Jin Mukyung faced the only path left to him. He saw it not with his eyes, but with his heart.
A future that could never come to pass.
Eternal death.
*So this is the end.*
Even Jin Mukyung was surprised by how calmly he accepted it.
He’d already done everything he could.
He’d fought with all his strength, enough to look up at the heavens without a shred of shame. At last, that strength had run out.
Body and soul.

He’d poured everything into the fight. There was nothing left. In a world that had slowed to a crawl, he watched a spear rise and knew the death in its blade was drawing near, yet he couldn’t twitch a finger.
And still, somewhere deep in his heart, one thread of regret remained. It was for the people he would leave behind.
*What will happen to them now?*
He didn’t care what awaited him after death.
Even if a pale-faced Grim Reaper dressed head to toe in black appeared right now, bound him in chains, and dragged him before Yama, it wouldn’t matter.
He had lived an honorable life as a martial artist and as the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s Second Young Master. The lives he’d taken had been taken to protect others, not because he wanted to kill.
But now he had to leave.
He had to leave everyone behind and be dragged into the unknown darkness. Not by choice.
Everything he’d wanted to protect, everything he had ultimately failed to save, would remain here.
*...No. Anything but that.*
In that instant, Jin Mukyung clenched his teeth.
He forced his fading consciousness awake and screamed silently.
*Everything I could? What did that even mean?*
How could he accept death so weakly?
If he was still alive, it wasn’t over. Not until his last breath.
He had to get up. He had to fight until his pounding heart stopped.
His fingertips trembled. The smell of blood rose between his clenched teeth.
But even biting his own tongue couldn’t rouse a body that had long since passed its limit. The cruel reality didn’t change.
*Whoosh.*
The sound of something cutting through the air rang clearly in his ears. In his blurred vision, the slanting flash seemed unusually slow.
Slow enough to look back on his entire life.
Slow enough to picture the most infuriating face in the world.
*If you were here instead of me... everything would be different.*
As the spearhead fell toward his head, Jin Mukyung spoke in his heart to the only younger brother he had. The words would never reach him.
*Looks like I won’t be able to keep that promise after all.*
Two years ago, the brothers had made a promise through the wall of the training hall.
They would meet at the Star-Array Grand Banquet, the gathering of countless stars that lit up the world.
In the end, Jin Mukyung hadn’t kept his promise.
He’d been ashamed. His accomplishments had felt nowhere near enough.

When he’d first picked up a sword, he’d wanted to become a great martial artist. Later, he’d wanted to become the pride of the Jin Family of Taiyuan and a younger brother his elder brother could be proud of.
But there was another reason—his greatest reason—for spending the past two years swinging his sword without rest in suffocating darkness.
He wanted to be an older brother who could hold his head high.
He wanted to become strong enough to surpass the wall that was Cheongpung, so his younger brother, who’d become the Divine Dragon and soared freely through the sky, wouldn’t be ashamed of him.
But...
*So this is how it ends.*
Jin Mukyung, the Heaven Shaking Sword.
The time of opportunity granted to a young genius, overshadowed by other monsters, was over.
The sword he’d honed in the dark had shone brightly enough to light this gorge today. But that fleeting light would be swallowed by the long, deep night.
Forever.
*Damn it.*
Jin Mukyung struggled to lift his half-closed eyelids.

He would not close his eyes in the face of death. It was the last pride he had as a martial artist, proof that his fighting spirit remained unbroken. And he wanted to say goodbye to his troublesome younger brother, even if his voice would never reach him.
“...I’m sorry.”
The words had barely left Jin Mukyung’s lips when—
*KABOOOOOM!*
The sky and earth shook.
His world, dark and hazy until then, turned blue-white. The flash falling toward his head changed course and swept sideways.
Toward the terrible heat that had arrived faster than light, outrunning even the thunder of its arrival.
No—toward the spear carrying that heat.
*Wooooom.*
The wind vanished. The air stood still.
Two currents of qi met. In that instant, they enveloped everything within dozens of *zhang*, then swelled.
*KRAAAAAASH!*
A tremendous shock wave tore across the gorge, its roar deafening.

Lying in the deep pit, Jin Mukyung reached out on instinct. He held the unconscious Cheol Mubaek and Wipeng with all his strength and watched the corpses of people and horses, along with countless fragments of rock, fly in every direction as if caught in a storm.
Amid the blinding light that engulfed everything around him, he could just make out someone’s back.
Jin Mukyung coughed up dark-red blood. A thought struck him.
Perhaps he was already dead. Perhaps his lingering attachment to life was making him see things even now.
But...
*No.*
Everything he saw, heard, and felt was too vivid to belong to the dead.
The stinging pain in his skin where the rock fragments had scraped past. The muscles screaming throughout his body. The blood surging from his insides, twisted by severe Internal Injury.
And, finally, the familiar voice that reached his ears.
“What are you throwing up for? Did you drink too much last night?”
Jin Mukyung’s body went rigid.
His eyes flew wide, a storm raging in their depths.
There was no mistaking it. This wasn’t a hallucination. He wasn’t hearing things.
This was...
“I’d pat you on the back, but, well, the situation’s a little tricky.”
The voice came through clearly as the roar died away.
In the fading light, he could see him.
That infuriating voice alone was enough to make Jin Mukyung want to raise a fist. That wastrel’s back had, at some point, grown broader and sturdier than his own.
Where had the strength come from?
Jin Mukyung squeezed out a voice rough as scraping metal and raised his hand. Though his fingers shook like leaves, he reached toward his only younger brother’s robe.
*Rustle.*
The sound of fabric brushing against something was so faint he had to strain to hear it.
Perhaps it was the wind, not Jin Mukyung’s hand, that touched the edge of the tattered robe.
But that was enough.
What he wanted to convey was more than a touch. It was a desperate wish for his brother to protect everyone.
*Thud.*
His hand fell limply. His whole body went slack.
At last, the pathetic older brother, having spent every last bit of his strength, lost consciousness.
Before him stood his wastrel younger brother, returned after two years away. A dozen *zhang* from him stood an unfamiliar, graying middle-aged man, watching him with a dark, steady gaze.
“I have one question.”
His eyes blazed with flame. His voice, by contrast, was cold as ice.
“Did you beat up my hyung?”
The wastrel had returned.
As a dragon whose roar shook the heavens.
Beyond his low voice rose the tearful cheers of the people of Shanxi.
Not long ago, someone told me not to carry everything alone.
To trust them a little more.
Now I knew they’d been right.
I could tell the moment I reached the battlefield.
Blood was everywhere. Limbs torn from bodies I couldn’t identify lay among countless corpses of people and horses. They had piled into small hills that filled the narrow gorge.
Most of the dead were nomads.
The enemy had outnumbered the people of Shanxi by at least two to one. They’d been badly outmatched in fighting strength, too. But they hadn’t given in.
No. They’d fought back with every bit of strength they had.
The Imperial Army. The martial artists. Even ordinary people who probably hadn’t learned a single move of martial arts.
And Jin Mukyung.
*They did everything they could. Even when it meant overcoming their fear of death.*
I knew how hard it was for the weak to stand against the strong.
And I’d taken Jin Mukyung’s wish to heart. There could be no more sacrifices like theirs.
*Wooooom. BOOM!*
I reached out. With a thunderous crash, the spear buried deep in the cliff twisted like a living creature and flew toward me.
White Flame trembled faintly in my grasp, back from its brief journey.
The blue-white flames coiling around its blade lit the pitch-black darkness and heated the cold night air as they surged toward the enemy before me.
**System** Lv.??? Murong Baek
A graying, middle-aged man stood before me, gripping a dark spear much like the charging spears the nomads used.
I’d be lying if I said the System window I read with my razor-sharp Qi Sense hadn’t caught me off guard. But the reality before my eyes was the truth.
I looked at the Family Head of the Murong Family, a man I’d heard of but never met.
Another blade Dark Heaven had hidden in the vast forest of the Central Plains’ Murim.
The North Heaven Demon Lord.
“I asked you. Did you beat up my hyung?”
The North Heaven Demon Lord was silent for a moment.
“Well, now.”
His gaze swept over me, and he gave a small sigh at the arrival of an uninvited guest.
“This complicates things. In more ways than one.”
I bet it was. In more ways than one.
I lifted my spearhead, ready to strike at any moment.
“Why so troubled? You’re making me worry.”
Why the Family Head of the Murong Family had become Dark Heaven’s lackey, or when, didn’t matter to me right now.
I had only one thing to do: take down Murong Baek, without a doubt the North Heaven Demon Lord, and the nomad behind him, standing there with a thoroughly stiff expression.
“So why not just crack your skull while we’re at it? Then it won’t hurt anymore.”
*Step.*
The North Heaven Demon Lord took a step forward and answered calmly.
“That’s a treatment I’ve never heard of.”
“I know more about medicine than you’d think. I picked up a thing or two watching the Divine Physician.”
“Maybe. Even so, I suspect that method would be a problem.”
The North Heaven Demon Lord looked at me with a clear gaze that seemed to see through everything, then added:
“Especially in your current condition.”
I wanted to deny it, but he was right.
I’d paid a price for crossing ten thousand *li* without proper sleep, meals, or time to circulate my qi.
So I answered without hesitation.
“Yeah. You’re right.”
*Step.*
The footsteps that had been steadily closing the distance suddenly stopped. The North Heaven Demon Lord furrowed his brow as he looked at me.
“What did you say?”
“I said you’re right. Honestly, like this, it’d be tough. Really tough.”
“What are you—”
His voice trailed off. I shrugged at the North Heaven Demon Lord, who was staring at me as if I were crazy.
“So I brought someone I know along while I was at it.”
Before the North Heaven Demon Lord could grasp what I meant, two sharp whistles swept through the air.

In a world that had slowed to a crawl, he watched a spear rise and knew the death in its blade was drawing near, yet he couldn’t twitch a finger.
And still, somewhere deep in his heart, one thread of regret remained.
It was for the people he would leave behind.
*What will happen to them now?*
He didn’t care what awaited him after death.
Even if a pale-faced Grim Reaper dressed head to toe in black appeared right now, bound him in chains, and dragged him before Yama, it wouldn’t matter.
He had lived an honorable life as a martial artist and as the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s Second Young Master.
The lives he’d taken had been taken to protect others, not because he wanted to kill.
But now he had to leave.
He had to leave everyone behind and be dragged into the unknown darkness.
Not by choice.
Everything he’d wanted to protect, everything he had ultimately failed to save, would remain here.
Anything but that.*
In that instant, Jin Mukyung clenched his teeth.
He forced his fading consciousness awake and screamed silently.
*Everything I could?
What did that even mean?*
How could he accept death so weakly?
If he was still alive, it wasn’t over.
Not until his last breath.
He had to get up.
He had to fight until his pounding heart stopped.
His fingertips trembled.
The smell of blood rose between his clenched teeth.
But even biting his own tongue couldn’t rouse a body that had long since passed its limit.
The cruel reality didn’t change.
*Whoosh.*
The sound of something cutting through the air rang clearly in his ears.
In his blurred vision, the slanting flash seemed unusually slow.
Slow enough to look back on his entire life.
Slow enough to picture the most infuriating face in the world.
*If you were here instead of me... everything would be different.*
As the spearhead fell toward his head, Jin Mukyung spoke in his heart to the only younger brother he had.
The words would never reach him.
*Looks like I won’t be able to keep that promise after all.*
Two years ago, the brothers had made a promise through the wall of the training hall.
They would meet at the Star-Array Grand Banquet, the gathering of countless stars that lit up the world.
In the end, Jin Mukyung hadn’t kept his promise.
He’d been ashamed.
His accomplishments had felt nowhere near enough.
When he’d first picked up a sword, he’d wanted to become a great martial artist.
Later, he’d wanted to become the pride of the Jin Family of Taiyuan and a younger brother his elder brother could be proud of.
But there was another reason—his greatest reason—for spending the past two years swinging his sword without rest in suffocating darkness.
He wanted to be an older brother who could hold his head high.
He wanted to become strong enough to surpass the wall that was Cheongpung, so his younger brother, who’d become the Divine Dragon and soared freely through the sky, wouldn’t be ashamed of him.
But...
*So this is how it ends.*
Jin Mukyung, the Heaven Shaking Sword.
The time of opportunity granted to a young genius, overshadowed by other monsters, was over.
The sword he’d honed in the dark had shone brightly enough to light this gorge today.
But that fleeting light would be swallowed by the long, deep night.
Forever.
*Damn it.*
Jin Mukyung struggled to lift his half-closed eyelids.
He would not close his eyes in the face of death.
It was the last pride he had as a martial artist, proof that his fighting spirit remained unbroken.
And he wanted to say goodbye to his troublesome younger brother, even if his voice would never reach him.
“...I’m sorry.”
The words had barely left Jin Mukyung’s lips when—
*KABOOOOOM!*
The sky and earth shook.
His world, dark and hazy until then, turned blue-white.
The flash falling toward his head changed course and swept sideways.
Toward the terrible heat that had arrived faster than light, outrunning even the thunder of its arrival.
No—toward the spear carrying that heat.
*Wooooom.*
The wind vanished.
The air stood still.
Two currents of qi met.
In that instant, they enveloped everything within dozens of *zhang*, then swelled.
*KRAAAAAASH!*
A tremendous shock wave tore across the gorge, its roar deafening.
Lying in the deep pit, Jin Mukyung reached out on instinct.

He held the unconscious Cheol Mubaek and Wipeng with all his strength and watched the corpses of people and horses, along with countless fragments of rock, fly in every direction as if caught in a storm.
Amid the blinding light that engulfed everything around him, he could just make out someone’s back.
Jin Mukyung coughed up dark-red blood.
A thought struck him.
Perhaps he was already dead.
Perhaps his lingering attachment to life was making him see things even now.
But...
*No.*
Everything he saw, heard, and felt was too vivid to belong to the dead.
The stinging pain in his skin where the rock fragments had scraped past.
The muscles screaming throughout his body.
The blood surging from his insides, twisted by severe Internal Injury.
And, finally, the familiar voice that reached his ears.
“What are you throwing up for?
Did you drink too much last night?”
Jin Mukyung’s body went rigid.
His eyes flew wide, a storm raging in their depths.
There was no mistaking it.
This wasn’t a hallucination.
He wasn’t hearing things.
This was...
“I’d pat you on the back, but, well, the situation’s a little tricky.”
The voice came through clearly as the roar died away.
In the fading light, he could see him.
That infuriating voice alone was enough to make Jin Mukyung want to raise a fist.
That wastrel’s back had, at some point, grown broader and sturdier than his own.
Where had the strength come from?
Jin Mukyung squeezed out a voice rough as scraping metal and raised his hand.
Though his fingers shook like leaves, he reached toward his only younger brother’s robe.
*Rustle.*
The sound of fabric brushing against something was so faint he had to strain to hear it.
Perhaps it was the wind, not Jin Mukyung’s hand, that touched the edge of the tattered robe.
But that was enough.
What he wanted to convey was more than a touch.
It was a desperate wish for his brother to protect everyone.
*Thud.*
His hand fell limply.
His whole body went slack.
At last, the pathetic older brother, having spent every last bit of his strength, lost consciousness.
Before him stood his wastrel younger brother, returned after two years away.
A dozen *zhang* from him stood an unfamiliar, graying middle-aged man, watching him with a dark, steady gaze.
“I have one question.”
His eyes blazed with flame.
His voice, by contrast, was cold as ice.
“Did you beat up my hyung?”
The wastrel had returned.
As a dragon whose roar shook the heavens.
Beyond his low voice rose the tearful cheers of the people of Shanxi.
Not long ago, someone told me not to carry everything alone.
To trust them a little more.
Now I knew they’d been right.
I could tell the moment I reached the battlefield.
Blood was everywhere.
Limbs torn from bodies I couldn’t identify lay among countless corpses of people and horses.
They had piled into small hills that filled the narrow gorge.
Most of the dead were nomads.
The enemy had outnumbered the people of Shanxi by at least two to one.
They’d been badly outmatched in fighting strength, too.
But they hadn’t given in.
No.
They’d fought back with every bit of strength they had.
The Imperial Army.
The martial artists.
Even ordinary people who probably hadn’t learned a single move of martial arts.
And Jin Mukyung.
*They did everything they could.
Even when it meant overcoming their fear of death.*
I knew how hard it was for the weak to stand against the strong.
And I’d taken Jin Mukyung’s wish to heart.
There could be no more sacrifices like theirs.
*Wooooom.
BOOM!*
I reached out.
With a thunderous crash, the spear buried deep in the cliff twisted like a living creature and flew toward me.
White Flame trembled faintly in my grasp, back from its brief journey.
The blue-white flames coiling around its blade lit the pitch-black darkness and heated the cold night air as they surged toward the enemy before me.
**System** Lv.???
Murong Baek
A graying, middle-aged man stood before me, gripping a dark spear much like the charging spears the nomads used.
I’d be lying if I said the System window I read with my razor-sharp Qi Sense hadn’t caught me off guard.
But the reality before my eyes was the truth.
I looked at the Family Head of the Murong Family, a man I’d heard of but never met.
Another blade Dark Heaven had hidden in the vast forest of the Central Plains’ Murim.
The North Heaven Demon Lord.
“I asked you.
Did you beat up my hyung?”
The North Heaven Demon Lord was silent for a moment.
“Well, now.”
His gaze swept over me, and he gave a small sigh at the arrival of an uninvited guest.
“This complicates things.
In more ways than one.”
I bet it was.
In more ways than one.
I lifted my spearhead, ready to strike at any moment.
“Why so troubled?
You’re making me worry.”
Why the Family Head of the Murong Family had become Dark Heaven’s lackey, or when, didn’t matter to me right now.
I had only one thing to do: take down Murong Baek, without a doubt the North Heaven Demon Lord, and the nomad behind him, standing there with a thoroughly stiff expression.
“So why not just crack your skull while we’re at it?
Then it won’t hurt anymore.”
*Step.*
The North Heaven Demon Lord took a step forward and answered calmly.
“That’s a treatment I’ve never heard of.”
“I know more about medicine than you’d think.
I picked up a thing or two watching the Divine Physician.”
“Maybe.
Even so, I suspect that method would be a problem.”
The North Heaven Demon Lord looked at me with a clear gaze that seemed to see through everything, then added:
“Especially in your current condition.”
I wanted to deny it, but he was right.
I’d paid a price for crossing ten thousand *li* without proper sleep, meals, or time to circulate my qi.
So I answered without hesitation.
“Yeah.
You’re right.”
*Step.*
The footsteps that had been steadily closing the distance suddenly stopped.
The North Heaven Demon Lord furrowed his brow as he looked at me.
“What did you say?”
“I said you’re right.
Honestly, like this, it’d be tough.
Really tough.”
“What are you—”
His voice trailed off.
I shrugged at the North Heaven Demon Lord, who was staring at me as if I were crazy.
“So I brought someone I know along while I was at it.”
Before the North Heaven Demon Lord could grasp what I meant, two sharp whistles swept through the air.

chapters.title: Chapter 971
paragraphs: Human senses provide far more information than you might imagine.

That was especially true of martial artists, whose five senses were incomparably sharper than those of ordinary people. Living by the law of the jungle, they honed those senses through brutal training until they could detect things happening far beyond what the naked eye could see.
Just as the North Heaven Demon Lord did now.
“So I brought someone I know along while I was at it.”
Jin Taekyung, the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon.

Despite the overwhelming force of his arrival, the young upstart looked plainly exhausted. But the moment the North Heaven Demon Lord heard his easygoing voice, a red warning light went on in his head.
A title and a name sprang to mind.
*The Fire King, Jeok Cheongang.*

A giant who stood astride the orthodox and unorthodox factions. An old monster of Mount Jiuhua. And the master who had taken the wastrel Third Young Master of the Jin Family of Taiyuan as his Disciple.
The North Heaven Demon Lord’s eyes widened.
*If that’s the case...*
He was certain something had gone wrong. He didn’t know when or where, but it had.
Not every plan went exactly as intended. Still, Jin Taekyung and Jeok Cheongang were not supposed to be here.
*Information leaked.*
But he never got as far as wondering who had leaked it, or how.
More precisely, he wasn’t given the chance.
*Whoosh! Whoooooom!*
One sound was faint and swift. The other swept in like a furious gale.
The two streaks of sound reached him through senses that had gone beyond the five and into the sixth. The North Heaven Demon Lord furrowed his brow.
Not one. Two.
That mattered even more than the direction they had come from: the cliffs on either side, not the ground ahead.
*KABOOOOOM!*
A crash rang out from atop the cliffs, more than thirty *zhang* high. Horrific screams mingled with it.
It sounded like thunder.
Thunder that swallowed someone’s life and summoned an untimely shower.
*Drip. Drip-drip.*
Beside the North Heaven Demon Lord, Jamukha stood silently looking up at the darkened cliff. Then he felt something hot land on his face.
Red, sticky blood.
The corners of Jamukha’s mouth trembled. The North Heaven Demon Lord’s gaze darkened.
They both knew what it meant.
Annihilation.
The nomads they had sent up the cliff at considerable cost were gone. In a span too brief to call even a moment, every one of them had been killed or captured.
What mattered most to the North Heaven Demon Lord was the identity of the two monsters who had swept the cliff clear so quickly.
“One of them is obviously your master. Who’s the other?”
At his dry question, the young monster—still a little green—put on a stern expression.
“Now, now. You should figure it out for yourself. What kind of upbringing did you have, trying to peek at the answer sheet at your age?”
For a moment, the North Heaven Demon Lord wanted to crack open Jin Taekyung’s skull and take a look inside. But the monsters on the cliff would not even let him take a step.
*Shwaa!*
The narrow gorge lit up. The North Heaven Demon Lord swung the spear in his hand without hesitation, striking a streak of light hurtling through the air.
*BOOM!*
The crash was far too loud to have come from two blades meeting.
The flash ricocheted from the impact and buried itself deep in the ground. The North Heaven Demon Lord frowned as he recognized it.
“A charging spear?”
There was no doubt. It was an utterly ordinary charging spear of the sort the steppe nomads used.
Yet the strike had been so swift he could hardly believe someone had simply thrown it.
It was as if the spear had been shot like an arrow.
*Wait. Could it be...?*
The North Heaven Demon Lord looked up.
Just then, moonlight slipped through a break in the clouds, revealing a woman holding a bow so enormous it could have been mistaken for a long spear.
“...The Bow Saint.”
The words left his lips like a groan.
At the same moment, flashes rained down again.
*KABOOOM!*
The bowstring moved at dazzling speed, each release ringing through the gorge. The Bow Saint fired a dozen or so charging spears as lightly as arrows, then slowly drew back the string.
*Wooooom.*
Space trembled.
Brilliant qi gathered along a silver line formed from internal energy, taking the shape of an arrow. Then it shot forth, charged with immense power.
Not toward the North Heaven Demon Lord, but toward other enemies.
*FWOOSH!*
The deep darkness tore open.
Everyone on the battlefield could see that dazzling, destructive flash.
The people of Shanxi, hacking their way through the enemies in the gorge with hoarse, unrelenting battle cries.
The nomads dying helplessly at their hands.
And the martial artists of the Hebei Peng Family, fighting desperately in the broad basin beyond the gorge while surrounded by nomads and the Murong Family.
“What in the world is that...?”
The Keshik centurion had only just spotted the dozen or so streaks of light raining down from the sky. He had no idea the bewildered words leaving his lips would be his last.
Nor that this would be the last sight he and hundreds of his comrades saw in this world.
*KABOOOOOM!*
The earth turned over with a terrifying crash.
Arms and legs flew up through fountains of blood, along with pieces of flesh and organs too mangled to recognize. They scattered in every direction.
*Krrrsh. Splatter.*
Blood and flesh pattered down onto the ground, their late arrival ringing in everyone’s ears.
Peng Cheolyeong, Family Head of the Hebei Peng Family and the Iron Blood Saber, blinked blankly. The Murong Family’s unexpected betrayal had left him surrounded on all sides and covered in blood.
*What just happened?*
He had been fighting dozens of enemies alone with his back to the gorge. He hadn’t seen a thing.
He had only sensed the sky brighten. A chill had run down his spine, and his hand had stopped on instinct.
And... that was all.
He shut his eyes against the brilliant light stabbing into them. When he opened them again, the enemies who had filled the space around him were gone.
No. To be precise, they were still there.
Just no longer in shapes that could be called human.
Some had lost their upper bodies. Others had limbs torn away.
“Ugh—aaah!”
“Graaaah!”
The body feels pain first, but the brain is what recognizes it.
As the survivors finally grasped the unbelievable reality, they let out desperate screams. Unlike the hundreds killed by the flash, those lucky enough to survive writhed in pain.
Before their horrific screams could die away, the sky lit up once more.
*FWOOSH.*
In that moment, Peng Cheolyeong understood.
That dazzling beam of light—something he would normally have stopped to stare at—meant death.
And that death was not meant for him or the martial artists of the Hebei Peng Family.
“Attack!”
Fear is contagious. Hope catches fire.
With the flash lighting up the blood- and corpse-covered basin behind them, the martial artists of the Hebei Peng Family surged forward, tearing apart the encirclement that had already crumbled.
Their fierce cries rang out across the battlefield, loud enough to echo all the way into the depths of the narrow gorge.
“Sounds nice. Not for you, though.”
The North Heaven Demon Lord silently watched Jin Taekyung’s smiling face.
For all the mischief in the young bastard’s voice, his eyes were dark and solemn. Reflected in them, the North Heaven Demon Lord saw his own face, stiff with tension.
*The Bow Saint.*
He had not anticipated her presence. She was a ghost from a past too distant to appear here.
“So that’s why you were so relaxed.”
After a brief silence, the North Heaven Demon Lord spoke again, the broad outline of what had happened finally falling into place.
“So it was the Imperial Palace.”
The Bow Saint’s appearance brought the scattered clues together.
Why Jin Taekyung had been able to come here. Whether Dark Heaven’s plan centered on the Imperial Capital had succeeded. And where the Bow Saint had taken refuge after vanishing without a trace.
“But how did you find out so quickly?”
“Your friend told me,” Jin Taekyung answered.
“My friend?”
“The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord.”
“You should’ve been friendlier with him. Had meals together more often, swapped catalog numbers like proper members of the martial world. Well, I’m just glad I found out before it was too late.”
Jin Taekyung shrugged with an irritating look on his face and added, “When you see him in a bit, thank him for me. He deserved to die, but at the end, I found myself a little concerned about him.”
The North Heaven Demon Lord understood what he meant and smiled bitterly.
“I’ll have to politely decline.”
“What, were you two that unfriendly? Was there a love triangle or something?”
“Crazy bastard. Does your tongue ever rest?”
“I was about to stop anyway. I can move a little now.”
The smile faded from Jin Taekyung’s lips.
He had already shaken off the weakness left by the strike he’d launched with all his strength to save Jin Mukyung, exhausted as he was.
“Thanks for waiting while I caught my breath.”
The North Heaven Demon Lord looked at him with a subdued gaze.
He had not given Jin Taekyung that time willingly. Someone else had forced him to.
“Enough of this. Why don’t you come out, Fire King?”
At his words to the empty air, a figure blended into the darkness drifted gently down.
“What a shame. If you’d taken so much as one step, I’d have burned your limbs off.”
“I wonder if you really could.”
The North Heaven Demon Lord gripped his spear at an angle. Unprecedented qi surged along its blade—nothing like what Jeok Cheongang remembered from their encounter on a battlefield long ago.
“You’ve grown bold, haven’t you? A mere pup, speaking to this old man like an equal and even daring to act tough.”
Jeok Cheongang grinned, baring his teeth. White hellfire rippled over both his outstretched hands.
“When did you join forces with them?”
“What a strange thing. The two of you, who were like cats and dogs, asking me the same question here today.”
The smile vanished from Jeok Cheongang’s face.
He knew whom the North Heaven Demon Lord meant. He knew, too, that the man’s life hung by a thread.
“...My Disciple owes that Peng bastard a great debt. I’ll repay it with your life.”
“You can both go together—to the afterlife.”
The North Heaven Demon Lord answered calmly and tossed what he held into his mouth.
*Slip.*
A red pill dissolved against his tongue. At the same moment, Jin Taekyung’s spearhead flashed behind him.
