If you’d taken so much as one step, I’d have burned your limbs off.”
“I wonder if you really could.”
The North Heaven Demon Lord gripped his spear at an angle.
Unprecedented qi surged along its blade—nothing like what Jeok Cheongang remembered from their encounter on a battlefield long ago.
“You’ve grown bold, haven’t you?
A mere pup, speaking to this old man like an equal and even daring to act tough.”
Jeok Cheongang grinned, baring his teeth.
White hellfire rippled over both his outstretched hands.
“When did you join forces with them?”
“What a strange thing.
The two of you, who were like cats and dogs, asking me the same question here today.”
The smile vanished from Jeok Cheongang’s face.
He knew whom the North Heaven Demon Lord meant.
He knew, too, that the man’s life hung by a thread.
“...My Disciple owes that Peng bastard a great debt.
I’ll repay it with your life.”
“You can both go together—to the afterlife.”
The North Heaven Demon Lord answered calmly and tossed what he held into his mouth.
*Slip.*
A red pill dissolved against his tongue.
At the same moment, Jin Taekyung’s spearhead flashed behind him.

chapters.title: Chapter 972
paragraphs: Jeok Cheongang and Jin Taekyung.
Jin Taekyung and Jeok Cheongang.
The moment it began, Master and Disciple moved as one.
As their heat closed in on him in a single step, fierce enough to set his whole body ablaze, the North Heaven Demon Lord realized once more:
He had made the right choice.
To make this plan—which had gone wildly off course from what he’d expected—succeed, he had to use everything he’d been given as quickly as possible.
*Fwoosh!*
Hot. Everything before his eyes turned red.
As the world slowed, the North Heaven Demon Lord felt a heat that seemed to burn through his entire body.
But it wasn’t only the power of the Fire Gate Divine Technique, passed down for more than three hundred years, that made him feel that way.
*KABOOOOOM!*
A tremendous roar, audible only to him, reverberated from deep within his body.
At the same time, the qi throughout his body surged.
Lava-hot energy raced through hundreds of acupoints, swelling and surging as if it might burst at any moment.
A colossal wave of power from a strange artifact he had never once used was tearing down part of the high, sturdy wall that had stood in his way.
The North Heaven Demon Lord groaned amid overwhelming pain and ecstasy.
Everything in his reddened field of vision—even things he couldn’t see—felt slow and vivid.
The wind. The air. The qi within it.
And the two streams of flame rushing toward him, smashing everything in their path to pieces.
*So this is what it feels like. This is what it is.*
The North Heaven Demon Lord thought.

He felt he could almost understand the world the Heavenly Demon had seen as he ruled over the Hundred Thousand Demonic Disciples with martial prowess that reached the heavens and sought to conquer the world. The world the Martial God had seen when he defeated him and brought peace to it.
Perhaps that was why he could smile, even amid heat fierce enough to melt his Body-Protecting Qi.
*Whoooom.*
Perhaps that was why their movements looked so slow and weak.
*Is that all you’ve got?*
The view changed depending on where you stood.
Seized by the sensation that the Temporary Strength Pill had carried him over the summit and above the clouds, the North Heaven Demon Lord looked down on them with disdain.
His gaze swept over the entire battlefield beyond the narrow gorge, taking in even the old monster and the young Divine Dragon—men whose names alone could make the world tremble.
At the same time, he flung out both arms with a speed and power he had imagined countless times, yet had always felt as distant as a dream.
*Fwoooosh!*
Space warped under the unprecedented energy. A spearhead and a fist, their forms obscured beneath dark crimson Force, shot in different directions.
Toward the foolish descendants of the Fire Gate Clan, who had failed to recognize the power of an absolute being.
*Die.*
In the North Heaven Demon Lord’s red-hot vision, Jeok Cheongang and Jin Taekyung stared wide-eyed at the overwhelming power before them.
Dark crimson Force swept toward them like a wave.
*KABOOOOOM!*
The entire gorge shook. The shock wave swelled and exploded, sweeping everything within a radius of more than ten *zhang*.
No—*seized* and *swallowed* would have been better words for it.
The blinding flash and thunderous roar robbed everyone in the gorge of sight and hearing. Everything within reach of the shock wave lost its shape and vanished.
*Rrrrrumble!*
Part of the cliff collapsed, unable to withstand the aftershock.
The pools of blood and countless corpses scattered all around had vanished into dust. Amid what remained, the North Heaven Demon Lord drew a slow breath.
He shuddered at the power still welling up from deep inside him after that outburst—and at the fact that he had unleashed a calamity like a natural disaster with his own two hands.
Then he turned his head toward somewhere beyond the choking silence and clouds of dust.
No—he sensed them.
The presences that had survived this horrific disaster, not yet entirely extinguished.
“You managed to survive. As you should have.”
His voice was calm and relaxed.
The Temporary Strength Pill had given him martial prowess far beyond what he’d possessed only moments ago. Still, he had never expected to win with a single strike.

His opponent was the old monster of Mount Jiuhua, returned stronger than he’d been fifty years ago. And his Disciple had grown beyond a young prodigy into a towering figure who was leaving his mark on this vast world.
Even so, the North Heaven Demon Lord could remain at ease. He knew better than anyone the scale of the power throbbing within him, ready to burst.
Even if someone else intervened, that wouldn’t change.
As someone did now.
*Whoom! KABOOM!*
In the blink of an eye, a mass of concentrated energy struck the spearhead the North Heaven Demon Lord had swung, bouncing off from an unseen blind spot.
The North Heaven Demon Lord looked up at the figure standing atop a fractured, crumbling cliff more than thirty *zhang* high. A faint smile touched his lips.
“You’ve had a rough time, Bow Saint.”
Deflecting that attack confirmed it for him once more: his martial prowess now surpassed that of the Three Saints.
He had set foot, if only by one step, into the realm of those called the Invincible—or the absolute.
*KRAKAKAKANG!*
A mass of light packed with such tremendous power it could hardly be called an arrow.
The North Heaven Demon Lord deflected a barrage of them, each powerful enough to kill even a skilled Peak master with one strike. His smile deepened.
“You should’ve come a little slower. If you’d taken your time and saved some strength, a lot might have turned out differently.”
The distance from Zhejiang Province, where the Imperial Capital stood, to Shanxi Province was well over a few thousand *li*.
And for those three to have crossed that distance and appeared here without catching the North Heaven Demon Lord’s attention meant they’d moved faster than a messenger eagle or a courier.
They had rushed here without sparing even a moment, let alone taking proper rest before a battle.
That guess was enough to convince the North Heaven Demon Lord that victory was certain.
“Unfortunately, it’s too late to turn back now.”
*Shhhh...*
Dark crimson energy rose from his whole body like heat haze.
As the Bow Saint’s attacks bounced off his densely concentrated Force, exhilaration swept through him more intensely than ever before.
An absolute being.
Here, today, he was the absolute being.
The Fire Gate Clan’s Master and Disciple, who must be lying beyond that cloud of dust, groaning, could not stand against him now. Neither could the Bow Saint.
They were all exhausted, while his power continued to well up without end.
*Crack.*
A deep rumble spread from the tip of his foot as he stepped forward lightly.
The colossal power had frozen everyone in the gorge.
An unprecedented energy no one had ever imagined a human could possess expanded his dantian and raced through hundreds of acupoints.
The North Heaven Demon Lord laughed aloud.
*It feels like I could do anything right now.*
No—he *could*.
And just as his senses stretched out to envelop the entire gorge—
“Old Master, that bastard’s laughing.”
“Leave him be. He must think he’s the Lord of Heaven just because he took a Temporary Strength Pill.”
The North Heaven Demon Lord’s smile vanished. Two voices were conversing through Sound Transmission inside the dust cloud that had yet to settle.
“Uh, he’s not laughing anymore.”
“He was ugly to begin with, but now he’s scowling. His face looks like shit.”
“Why would you say it like that? My little guy is handsome and looks plenty clever.”
“All right, I get it. Take your damn hand off your waistband right now, before I turn you into a eunuch with one palm strike.”
The North Heaven Demon Lord’s gaze darkened. Confusion and shock unmistakable in his eyes, he looked in one direction.
“Uh, he’s looking this way.”
“Must’ve just gotten lucky. This old man knows at a glance.”
“We need to jump him all at once. What if he’s spotted us? Try moving to the side.”
“I was about to. Stop pushing me. How dare you touch this old man’s body?”
“That’s not a hand.”
“Huh?”
At that moment, the North Heaven Demon Lord’s mouth twitched.
“Come out.”
At the low words that slipped between his lips, a breathless silence descended.
*Seemed* to.
“He says come out. And he’s looking right at us.”
“Didn’t I tell you? He definitely guessed.”
“I don’t think so. Wait, can he hear our Sound Transmission?”
“Just because he took some pill? There’s no way that bastard can do that. I’ll stake that Hyuk bastard’s balls on it.”
*Tap.*
The last thread of the North Heaven Demon Lord’s patience broke. A cold voice slipped through his clenched teeth.
“What a shame. I don’t know who he is, but he’s going to lose his balls.”
At last, he received the answer he’d been waiting for.
*Poom!*
The dust cloud split as if cut by a sword. Jeok Cheongang emerged in tattered clothes, brushed the dirt from his shoulder, and replied, “That’s fine. Just in case, I didn’t stake my own.”
Behind the Master, who had said something so embarrassing with an unnecessarily solemn expression, his Disciple—several heads taller—spoke with an uneasy look.
“Why stake the balls of someone who isn’t even here? You won’t need them anyway. You might as well stake your own.”
“Isn’t that true of you, too?”
“Hey, that’s crossing a line. Why would you say—”
*KABOOM!*
A thunderous crash swallowed the rest of his words.
A moment later came a cough.
“Cough. Jeez, look at all this fine dust. Wouldn’t want anyone thinking you’re not a Chinese bastard.”
“Ahem. Stop making a fuss. You’ll bring shame on the Fire Gate Clan.”
“My God, is there even more shame left to bring?”
At the sight of Jin Taekyung and Jeok Cheongang standing there unharmed, the North Heaven Demon Lord’s gaze darkened.
He hadn’t attacked at full power, but they had evaded a strike backed by more than seventy percent of his strength. They clearly still had plenty in reserve.
The North Heaven Demon Lord had no choice but to admit that, at some point, he’d come to trust too much in the power he’d been given.
And that he had underestimated the enemies before him.
“Jamukha.”
At his quiet call, the hunting dog he had commanded for decades answered.
“Give your command, my lord.”
“We won’t stand by any longer. Change the plan.”
“You mean...”
“I will not tolerate any more interference. Before things go wrong, use every force we have and wipe them out at once.”
Jamukha understood exactly what the North Heaven Demon Lord meant by using every last bit of their strength.
Today, the Thunderbolt Saber King and the Hebei Peng Family had been invited guests on this battlefield. The three Supreme Peak masters who had appeared unexpectedly, however, were uninvited.
The die had been cast. They had to secure victory before the whole game was overturned.
As the North Heaven Demon Lord had just done, they would use every means at their disposal.
“As you command.”
With that curt reply, Jamukha pulled a signal flare from his robes and yanked its cord without hesitation.
*Fwish! Fwish! Fwish!*
Smoke shot up into the night.
The Bow Saint swiftly fired arrows of light that swept away most of it, but even she could do nothing about the wisps that scattered through the air.
*Poom! Poom! Poom!*
Fireworks blossomed across the blackened sky.

Obeying his master’s command, Jamukha had let the countless hunting dogs under him off their leashes. Now he tipped into his mouth the Temporary Strength Pill the North Heaven Demon Lord had stopped him from taking earlier.
Beyond the gorge, the Keshiks who had just seen the signal did the same.
*Swish. Shhhh...*
Red heat haze began to rise across the battlefield.

chapters.title: Chapter 973
paragraphs: The word *unavoidable* applied to everyone.
To farmers who faced drought before the harvest. To the sick who lay in bed, waiting for death to draw closer by the moment.
And to a woman whose astonishing power made it hard to believe she was human like them.
*I should have stopped them.*
The Bow Saint let out a low groan.
High atop a sheer cliff, she stared down at a group spewing streams of ghastly blood-red light.
*Shhk! Krrrunch!*
Every one of them had bloodshot eyes. A thick mist of blood gathered in the wake of their spears and blades as they advanced without hesitation.

On a battlefield where tens of thousands clashed, two hundred people were only a handful. But the Temporary Strength Pills had pushed each of them beyond their limits, making them more dangerous than any other enemy there.
Especially to the Hebei Peng Family’s fighters, of whom only about two thousand remained.
*Graaaah!*
A harrowing scream rang through the night air.
As the enemy finally broke the Hebei Peng Family’s vaunted Linked Tyrant King Formation, the Bow Saint lowered her drawn bow and bit her lip.
They were not only dangerous. They were clever.
After suffering heavy losses from several of her attacks, they had immediately spread out and plunged into the heart of her allies’ formation to guard against any more.
*If I keep attacking like this, I’ll hit our own people too.*
Even apart from the two hundred or so Keshiks, she had more than enough enemies to deal with.

The vast steppe army seemed endless, no matter how many she killed. The battle had already gone on for several *shichen*, and the steppe forces had surely suffered far greater losses than the people of Shanxi. Yet nearly twenty thousand of them remained.
If she held the high ground and rained arrows down until she had no strength left, she could inflict tremendous damage. That much was obvious.
But she had only one choice.
To gain one thing was to lose another. If she kept attacking, she could bring down countless enemies—but by then, every last fighter of the Hebei Peng Family would be dead.
Her mind was made up. There was no need to hesitate.
*I have to go. I have to do it myself.*
*Click.*
She twisted her enormous bow with a sharp wrench, revealing two strangely shaped curved blades.
Their cool grips settled into her hands. The Bow Saint kicked off the cliff and soared into the sky.
*Whoosh.*
The cold night wind swept over her, setting her long hair streaming behind her.
She stepped through the empty air toward the ground as though descending an invisible staircase. Then she turned to look behind her.
The narrow gorge lay hidden in darkness now, its depths awash with waves of powerful qi. To someone there, she said silently:
*Survive. Then prove yourself once more.*
The Chosen One.
The Blazing Flame Divine Dragon, Jin Taekyung.
His name weighed heavily on her heart as the Bow Saint plunged toward the distant ground.
*Shwaa!*
The two curved blades in her hands became razor-sharp winds, carving through space.
The Bow Saint was gone.
She had crossed to the other battlefield beyond the gorge—not to help Jeok Cheongang and me, but to aid the Hebei Peng Family’s fighters.
I watched her disappear across the distant sky without feeling hurt that she’d left. Jeok Cheongang met my eyes and simply nodded, his expression calm.
Someone else here felt differently, of course.
“I expected as much, but it still amazes me.”
The North Heaven Demon Lord spoke up without warning and went on without waiting for a reply.
“Why do you people always make such foolish choices? Every single time.”
He shook his head with a hollow laugh. I answered calmly.
“Of course you’d think that. Bastards like you wouldn’t understand even if you died and came back dozens of times.”

The North Heaven Demon Lord thought of his followers as nothing more than pawns to secure victory. He could never understand that all of us here were risking our lives not to kill someone, but to protect someone.
Or that this small difference was the most important measure of what separated the righteous from the demonic.
“What a rotten age. The Murong Family Head goes and stabs someone in the back, then starts popping pills the moment things get a little rough. Right?”
Jeok Cheongang answered me.
“Live long enough, and you’ll meet things worse than beasts. Creatures wearing human skin and pretending to be people, hiding their black hearts behind pretty words and smiles.”
His voice was cold. His eyes burned.
At that moment, all his anger was directed at the North Heaven Demon Lord.
“I used to think you just had a sly streak... If I’d known it would come to this, I should have killed you back then.”
To me, he was the North Heaven Demon Lord. To Jeok Cheongang, he was Murong Baek.
Unlike me, Jeok Cheongang had known him. They had once fought alongside each other as comrades. Now their gazes met across the air.
“Why didn’t you, Fire King? That was your first and last chance to kill me.”
Jeok Cheongang’s eyes darkened at the mocking reply.
“First and last? Do you truly believe that?”
“You don’t?”
*Rrrrumble.*
The space around us shook as though an earthquake had struck. A mighty aura rose from the North Heaven Demon Lord, pressing down on everything around him.
An unprecedented surge of qi, rougher and greater than Jeok Cheongang’s.
“I’ll show you now. You’ll never get a second chance.”
His low words reached everyone’s ears, and the North Heaven Demon Lord vanished.
*Swish.*
He moved faster than the faint whistle of air left in his wake.
But I could see him, if only faintly. No—I could *sense* him.
The North Heaven Demon Lord shot forward faster than sound. His spearhead cut through space, and his loyal hunting dog rushed after its master.
*Shwaa!*
A belated gust of wind followed the descending spearhead.
I swung White Flame up toward the flash driving at my upper body.
*BANG!*
The roar hardly sounded as though it had come from two spears colliding.
Tremendous pressure traveled down White Flame’s shaft to my toes. The ground split into a spiderweb of cracks.
Beyond the spearhead I had stopped, I met the North Heaven Demon Lord’s eyes for an instant. I could almost hear the question in them.
*How can a brat like you...?*
I knew that look all too well.
The eyes gone wide. The question mark in them.
And every enemy I’d faced had found an exclamation point in its place before that question had even faded.
Just like now.
*Ka-drrrk!*
I gritted my teeth and drove my spear shaft upward.

The muscles throughout my body swelled as if they were about to burst. A power no one but me could understand—supernatural powers—surged up and shook off the tremendous pressure bearing down on the spearhead.
*KABOOOOOM!*
The North Heaven Demon Lord’s eyes widened as the force drove him back.
That was when the hunting dog, arriving a step behind its master, bared its teeth.
*Shwaek!*
Before the dust kicked up by the shock wave could rise, a blade split through it.
The curved blade flashed through space toward the crown of my head. Just as it was about to strike, the air behind me blazed with heat.
*Fwoosh.*
A terrible heat. Merely touching it felt as though it would melt flesh and bone and burn even the soul.
*Flame Divine Palm.*
The instant I felt that familiar energy swell, I ducked without hesitation.
*Paaang!*
A mass of concentrated flame skimmed past the back of my head.
I looked up again, the back of my head burning as though scorched. The old nomad who had brought his curved blade down like a wild beast was already hurtling backward.
*Krrrunch!*
His feet gouged deep furrows in the ground. He was driven back nearly three *zhang* before Jeok Cheongang sniffed in his direction.
“Damn it. I was wondering where that horse shit smell was coming from. Turns out it was this barbarian.”
“That’s quite a face you’re making. What, now that you’ve had a taste of the heat, are you homesick for a steppe full of horse shit and weeds?”
Style may be temporary, but class is forever.
The old nomad’s face went rigid under Jeok Cheongang’s inspired verbal assault. Then a low voice rang out.
“Still the same. That tongue of yours still knows how to get under people’s skin.”
The remark was aimed at Jeok Cheongang, but the North Heaven Demon Lord’s gaze was fixed on me.
Jeok Cheongang tapped my shoulder.
“When it comes to running his mouth, this brat is several steps ahead of this old man.”
“He’s surpassed his Master in all the wrong ways.”
Jeok Cheongang gave a quiet laugh.
“Come now. You know it isn’t just that.”
The North Heaven Demon Lord said nothing. He looked at me as though he couldn’t make sense of what he was seeing.
Honestly, that was only natural.
It wasn’t just him. Anyone would have felt the same.
The Blood Lord, the Western Heaven Demon Lord, the Southern Heaven Demon Empress, the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord—and the other enemies I’d faced.
None of them had been able to make sense of me. None had found an answer, and the question had only grown with time.
No. More accurately...
*I’d gotten that much stronger.*

Looking back, every battle I’d fought over the last two years had been hard. My enemies were always strong, and I was always weaker than they were. I’d had to struggle with everything I had just to survive. Just to win.
But then, one day, I suddenly realized something.
I kept finding myself at death’s door not because I was weak, but because stronger enemies kept appearing.
And somewhere along the way, I’d started catching up to them.
The Head Elder, whose martial prowess had been so mighty. Pung Yang, whom I’d barely managed to defeat in a joint attack with Jin Mukyung.
The Demon Lords and Demon Empresses of Dark Heaven, each of them a nightmare in their own right.
Whenever I thought back on those battles that had brought me close to death, one thought would come to me:
*Back then—if I’d moved like this, I could’ve won so much more easily.*
Now I understood.
What I’d taken for regret and lingering misgivings was proof that I’d grown. It wasn’t just a change in the numbers on the System window. I’d grown as a martial artist.
And maybe I was still growing, even now.
“Hey. This is just something I’m personally curious about.”
I spoke up out of nowhere, then carefully put my question to the North Heaven Demon Lord.
Like a student asking a professor about a difficult assignment.
“Just now, wouldn’t kicking you in the balls have been a lot better than knocking your spear up?”
The professor’s face twisted beyond description.

sentences.text: The word *unavoidable* applied to everyone.
To farmers who faced drought before the harvest.
To the sick who lay in bed, waiting for death to draw closer by the moment.
And to a woman whose astonishing power made it hard to believe she was human like them.
*I should have stopped them.*
The Bow Saint let out a low groan.
High atop a sheer cliff, she stared down at a group spewing streams of ghastly blood-red light.
*Shhk!
Krrrunch!*
Every one of them had bloodshot eyes.
A thick mist of blood gathered in the wake of their spears and blades as they advanced without hesitation.
On a battlefield where tens of thousands clashed, two hundred people were only a handful.
But the Temporary Strength Pills had pushed each of them beyond their limits, making them more dangerous than any other enemy there.
Especially to the Hebei Peng Family’s fighters, of whom only about two thousand remained.
*Graaaah!*
A harrowing scream rang through the night air.
As the enemy finally broke the Hebei Peng Family’s vaunted Linked Tyrant King Formation, the Bow Saint lowered her drawn bow and bit her lip.
They were not only dangerous.
They were clever.
After suffering heavy losses from several of her attacks, they had immediately spread out and plunged into the heart of her allies’ formation to guard against any more.
*If I keep attacking like this, I’ll hit our own people too.*
Even apart from the two hundred or so Keshiks, she had more than enough enemies to deal with.
The vast steppe army seemed endless, no matter how many she killed.
The battle had already gone on for several *shichen*, and the steppe forces had surely suffered far greater losses than the people of Shanxi.
Yet nearly twenty thousand of them remained.
If she held the high ground and rained arrows down until she had no strength left, she could inflict tremendous damage.
That much was obvious.
But she had only one choice.
To gain one thing was to lose another.
If she kept attacking, she could bring down countless enemies—but by then, every last fighter of the Hebei Peng Family would be dead.
Her mind was made up.
There was no need to hesitate.
*I have to go.
I have to do it myself.*
*Click.*
She twisted her enormous bow with a sharp wrench, revealing two strangely shaped curved blades.
Their cool grips settled into her hands.
The Bow Saint kicked off the cliff and soared into the sky.
*Whoosh.*
The cold night wind swept over her, setting her long hair streaming behind her.
She stepped through the empty air toward the ground as though descending an invisible staircase.
Then she turned to look behind her.
The narrow gorge lay hidden in darkness now, its depths awash with waves of powerful qi.
To someone there, she said silently:
*Survive.
Then prove yourself once more.*
The Chosen One.
The Blazing Flame Divine Dragon, Jin Taekyung.
His name weighed heavily on her heart as the Bow Saint plunged toward the distant ground.
*Shwaa!*
The two curved blades in her hands became razor-sharp winds, carving through space.
The Bow Saint was gone.
She had crossed to the other battlefield beyond the gorge—not to help Jeok Cheongang and me, but to aid the Hebei Peng Family’s fighters.
I watched her disappear across the distant sky without feeling hurt that she’d left.
Jeok Cheongang met my eyes and simply nodded, his expression calm.
Someone else here felt differently, of course.
“I expected as much, but it still amazes me.”
The North Heaven Demon Lord spoke up without warning and went on without waiting for a reply.
“Why do you people always make such foolish choices?
Every single time.”
He shook his head with a hollow laugh.
I answered calmly.
“Of course you’d think that.
Bastards like you wouldn’t understand even if you died and came back dozens of times.”
The North Heaven Demon Lord thought of his followers as nothing more than pawns to secure victory.
He could never understand that all of us here were risking our lives not to kill someone, but to protect someone.
Or that this small difference was the most important measure of what separated the righteous from the demonic.
“What a rotten age.
The Murong Family Head goes and stabs someone in the back, then starts popping pills the moment things get a little rough.
Right?”
Jeok Cheongang answered me.
“Live long enough, and you’ll meet things worse than beasts.
Creatures wearing human skin and pretending to be people, hiding their black hearts behind pretty words and smiles.”
His voice was cold.
His eyes burned.
At that moment, all his anger was directed at the North Heaven Demon Lord.
“I used to think you just had a sly streak...
If I’d known it would come to this, I should have killed you back then.”
To me, he was the North Heaven Demon Lord.
To Jeok Cheongang, he was Murong Baek.
Unlike me, Jeok Cheongang had known him.
They had once fought alongside each other as comrades.
Now their gazes met across the air.
“Why didn’t you, Fire King?
That was your first and last chance to kill me.”
Jeok Cheongang’s eyes darkened at the mocking reply.

Do you truly believe that?”
“You don’t?”

chapters.title: Chapter 974
paragraphs: Sometimes, your true feelings just don’t get through to the other person.
It was sad to cause a misunderstanding I’d never intended, but there was nothing I could do about it.
We weren’t going to settle this by talking anyway.
“That mouth of yours...”
The words died before he could finish, leaving only a breath that scattered into the air.
The professor—or rather, the North Heaven Demon Lord—looked dizzy with rage. His face twisted as he steadied his breathing.
Since he seemed to be struggling, I spoke for him.
“I’ll tear it open.”
“What?”
“That’s what you were going to say, right? I’ve heard it plenty of times. I know.”
The North Heaven Demon Lord stared at me, momentarily at a loss for words, then clenched his teeth.
“Shut up.”
“Come on. A man has to say what’s on his mind. Even a shameless pill-popping bastard.”
“I said shut up.”
“But I’ve heard that line so many times, it feels a little stale. ‘I’ll tear your mouth open so you can never wag that unruly tongue again.’ Doesn’t that have more flavor?”
“Words truly are wasted on you.”
“Force won’t work either. The guys who said that to me and died could line up in formation, count off, and circle the Murim Alliance training ground twice.”
Jeok Cheongang, standing beside me, added, “For the record, mine would circle it more than ten times.”
“That’s because you’ve lived a lot longer than me.”
“If you don’t like it, live a long, healthy life yourself.”
“You’ve lived a long, sickly life. Don’t you remember? When I first met you...”
*Fwoosh!*
A sharp whistle swallowed the rest of my words.
I ducked on instinct, without a moment’s hesitation. A dagger shot past overhead at the speed of a streak of light and slammed into the cliff face.
*KABOOM!*
It struck with the force of a cannonball.
But no matter how much power an attack carried, it didn’t matter if it missed.
I brushed off the grit thrown up by the shock wave and stared wide-eyed at the North Heaven Demon Lord, who had thrown the dagger.
“Wow. That almost hit me.”
“Those pills really do make you strong. Old Master, I’d never beat him one-on-one.”
Jeok Cheongang frowned. “Was that even a question? Of course you wouldn’t. Keep going as you have been, though, and in another year or two at the earliest, you might have a chance.”
Only a year or two.
Jeok Cheongang knew my past and even my deepest secrets, so it was a fairly reasonable assessment. To someone listening, though, it was an intolerable insult.
“Jamukha.”
There was no anger left on the North Heaven Demon Lord’s face. At his low voice, the old nomad bowed his head.
“Give your command, my lord.”
“Do you remember the promise we made long ago?”
“I have never forgotten it for a single moment.”
“Then stake your life on it.”
“If you survive, I’ll give you Hebei along with the vast grasslands. Everything the Peng Family possessed—even their lives—I’ll put in your hands.”
The old nomad Jamukha’s eyelids trembled.
“That is the very reason I have lived until now.”
“Then what will you give me?”
“Today’s victory, and the head of Jin Taekyung, the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon.”
“Yes. That is the answer I wanted.”
*Step. Shhhhh...*
With a heavy step, the dark crimson energy that had risen like heat haze gathered into a thick mist.
The two men had finally drawn out every last drop of their strength. Watching them, Jeok Cheongang spoke calmly.
“Taekyung.”
“Yes?”
“Do you remember the promise we made long ago?”
I answered without hesitation. “No.”
“And what do you mean, ‘long ago’? It’s only been two years since we first met.”
Jeok Cheongang fell silent for a moment, then sighed.
“Do you have some kind of disease that makes blood gush from your seven apertures and kills you if you play along at a time like this?”
“What’s the point? We can’t even get our timing right. Better to land another hit on those bastards.”
“Hmm. Hard to argue with that.”
“Just do what you’ve always done. Be the Fire King.”
Jeok Cheongang’s gaze shifted from the North Heaven Demon Lord and Jamukha, who were approaching slowly and cautiously, to me.
“What? Is there something else you want to say?”
“No, nothing much. It just struck me that accepting you as my Disciple was the right choice.”
For a moment, I didn’t know what to say. Then Jeok Cheongang’s quiet voice reached my ear.
“We’ve never made any embarrassing promises to each other, but as always, remember one thing.”
“What should I keep in mind...?”
“This old man is always by your side.”
“So don’t do anything stupid like fighting to the death. Even if Yama comes for you, I’ll kick him in the ass and send him packing.”
The more I thought about it, the stranger it seemed.
People were all made of the same flesh and blood. How could they think so differently?
One person offered another everything he wanted in exchange for his life. Another asked for nothing—he only wanted the other person to survive.
And that was exactly what I wanted to say to Jeok Cheongang, too.
“If I keep that promise, what will you give me?”
Step by step, the two enemies drew closer. I watched the dark crimson mist grow thicker as I spoke, and Jeok Cheongang gave a dry laugh.
“You shameless bastard. Fine, what do you want?”
“Nothing much. You’ve already been sick once, so a long, healthy life is out of the question. Just make sure you live a long, sickly one from now on.”
“A long life at my age, huh? Seems I have a reason to live at least another hundred years.”
Jeok Cheongang laughed heartily, clearly delighted.
Pale light-flames gathered in his outstretched hands. Alongside them, blue-white flames surged over the spearhead of White Flame, burning away the chill of the deep night.
*Fwoooosh.*
Beyond the darkness melting before those two flames—alike, yet different—
I stepped toward the ominously thick dark crimson mist.
No. *We* stepped forward together, as if we’d promised to.
*Shwaa!*
Everyone who faced that mist, red as blood and frighteningly thick, felt a chill sink deep into their spines and stopped.
No. They had no choice but to stop.
Their instincts knew before their minds did.
*If I get close, I’ll die.*
The sight alone was chilling.
The qi hanging thick in the air had become almost tangible. Entering it would be like walking into a forest of blades and spears, ready to slice and tear their bodies apart.
But the greatest reason so many people from Shanxi were held back was the terrifying battle raging inside it.
*KABOOM! KABOOOOM!*
What could describe the scene better than *heaven and earth shaking*?
Beyond the mist, writhing like a living creature, four Supreme Peak masters were entangled with one another at the speed of flashes of light.
Without a moment’s pause.
Even now.
*Shhk!*
Force sliced through the hard ground as if it were tofu.
Jeok Cheongang narrowly dodged the North Heaven Demon Lord’s strike and clenched his fist.
Pale light-flames surged over the fist of a man whose regained youth had erased his wrinkles.
*Fwoosh!*
Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist.
A tremendous blaze erupted from a technique he had brought to the tenth level of mastery through more than a century of training.
It stained the air and shot toward the enemy before him—toward the North Heaven Demon Lord.
*KABOOOOOM!*
Compressed air exploded in layers.
The ground melted and the cliff walls shook, but at the last instant, the North Heaven Demon Lord’s figure blurred and vanished.
Or rather, it vanished from human sight, with all its limitations.
*Whoosh.*
A tiny, faint whistle slipped quietly into his ear.
But he knew well that movement faster than sound could fool his hearing, too.
*Above!*
He felt it.
His opponent’s presence, plunging down from the unseen space above his head.
And the immense Force riding the spearhead as it thrust forward, erasing the wind in its path.
*Poom!*
Jeok Cheongang struck out with both palms without hesitation.
The dark crimson mist surrounding them scattered in an instant.
Flame Divine Palm, unleashed at full strength, surged upward as a pillar of fire.
It raced toward an opponent who had tried to hide his presence, but whose immense energy made it impossible to conceal himself completely.
And in the next moment, Jeok Cheongang understood all over again.

With the Temporary Strength Pill’s power behind him, the North Heaven Demon Lord could look down on even Jeok Cheongang—who had reached his current realm through several moments of enlightenment—as half a step beneath him.
*Shwaa!*
The spearhead pierced a single precise point.
The immense Force at its tip split flames that had seemed capable of burning the whole world, and the distance between the two men vanished.
Jeok Cheongang’s eyes widened at the overwhelming force.
This wasn’t a question of enlightenment in the martial arts.

The North Heaven Demon Lord’s movements, enhanced to an extreme, made everything possible—along with internal energy so powerful it made Jeok Cheongang wonder if he had drawn out every last bit of his innate qi.
*Damn it.*
Swallowing the curse rising to his lips, Jeok Cheongang drew on all the internal energy in his body.
He slammed both hands together against the spearhead plunging toward his chest.
*Krrrrk!*
The spearhead trembled between his palms, pressed together as if in prayer.
Dark crimson Force tore into flesh and bone despite his Body-Protecting Qi. Jeok Cheongang clenched his teeth against the pain.
*Crack.*
The pain of breaking a molar was nothing beside what came from his hands as they grew more mangled by the second.
Jeok Cheongang swallowed the blood rising in his throat and held fast to the spearhead. The North Heaven Demon Lord bared his teeth in a grin.
“Why not stop now and get some rest? You look exhausted.”
Jeok Cheongang’s reply came through clenched teeth, edged with mockery.
“Right back at you.”
The North Heaven Demon Lord’s eyes darkened.
He could feel throughout his body that Jeok Cheongang wasn’t bluffing.
*What kind of monster is this old man?*
*Crack. Krrrunch.*
Though he drove it with all his strength, the spearhead could go no farther.
Jeok Cheongang’s skin was crushed by the Force, but his toes were dug deep into the ground, perfectly still.
The old monster of Mount Jiuhua had returned decades younger—and far stronger than the North Heaven Demon Lord remembered.
Strong enough that even after taking the Temporary Strength Pill, he couldn’t bring him down easily.
*It ends here.*
The moment that thought formed, the North Heaven Demon Lord twisted the spear shaft with every ounce of strength he had.
This time, even Jeok Cheongang would be unable to bear the pain.
*Crack.*
At the grisly sound of flesh tearing, Jeok Cheongang’s body shuddered. Then a thunderous shout burst from Jamukha’s lips.
“Jamukha!”
At that instant—
*KABOOM! Shhk!*
With a thunderous crash, a razor-sharp gust of wind shot toward Jeok Cheongang’s back.

“What’s the point?
We can’t even get our timing right.
Better to land another hit on those bastards.”
“Hmm.
Hard to argue with that.”
“Just do what you’ve always done.
Be the Fire King.”
Jeok Cheongang’s gaze shifted from the North Heaven Demon Lord and Jamukha, who were approaching slowly and cautiously, to me.
“What?
Is there something else you want to say?”
“No, nothing much.
It just struck me that accepting you as my Disciple was the right choice.”
For a moment, I didn’t know what to say.
Then Jeok Cheongang’s quiet voice reached my ear.
“We’ve never made any embarrassing promises to each other, but as always, remember one thing.”
“What should I keep in mind...?”
“This old man is always by your side.”
“So don’t do anything stupid like fighting to the death.
Even if Yama comes for you, I’ll kick him in the ass and send him packing.”
The more I thought about it, the stranger it seemed.
People were all made of the same flesh and blood.
How could they think so differently?
One person offered another everything he wanted in exchange for his life.
Another asked for nothing—he only wanted the other person to survive.
And that was exactly what I wanted to say to Jeok Cheongang, too.
“If I keep that promise, what will you give me?”
Step by step, the two enemies drew closer.
I watched the dark crimson mist grow thicker as I spoke, and Jeok Cheongang gave a dry laugh.
“You shameless bastard.
Fine, what do you want?”
“Nothing much.
You’ve already been sick once, so a long, healthy life is out of the question.
Just make sure you live a long, sickly one from now on.”
“A long life at my age, huh?
Seems I have a reason to live at least another hundred years.”
Jeok Cheongang laughed heartily, clearly delighted.
Pale light-flames gathered in his outstretched hands.
Alongside them, blue-white flames surged over the spearhead of White Flame, burning away the chill of the deep night.
*Fwoooosh.*
Beyond the darkness melting before those two flames—alike, yet different—
I stepped toward the ominously thick dark crimson mist.
No. *We* stepped forward together, as if we’d promised to.
*Shwaa!*
Everyone who faced that mist, red as blood and frighteningly thick, felt a chill sink deep into their spines and stopped.
No.
They had no choice but to stop.
Their instincts knew before their minds did.
*If I get close, I’ll die.*
The sight alone was chilling.
The qi hanging thick in the air had become almost tangible.
Entering it would be like walking into a forest of blades and spears, ready to slice and tear their bodies apart.
But the greatest reason so many people from Shanxi were held back was the terrifying battle raging inside it.
*KABOOM!
KABOOOOM!*
What could describe the scene better than *heaven and earth shaking*?
Beyond the mist, writhing like a living creature, four Supreme Peak masters were entangled with one another at the speed of flashes of light.
Without a moment’s pause.
Even now.
*Shhk!*
Force sliced through the hard ground as if it were tofu.
Jeok Cheongang narrowly dodged the North Heaven Demon Lord’s strike and clenched his fist.
Pale light-flames surged over the fist of a man whose regained youth had erased his wrinkles.
*Fwoosh!*
Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist.
A tremendous blaze erupted from a technique he had brought to the tenth level of mastery through more than a century of training.
It stained the air and shot toward the enemy before him—toward the North Heaven Demon Lord.
*KABOOOOOM!*
Compressed air exploded in layers.
The ground melted and the cliff walls shook, but at the last instant, the North Heaven Demon Lord’s figure blurred and vanished.
Or rather, it vanished from human sight, with all its limitations.
*Whoosh.*
A tiny, faint whistle slipped quietly into his ear.
But he knew well that movement faster than sound could fool his hearing, too.
*Above!*
He felt it.
His opponent’s presence, plunging down from the unseen space above his head.
And the immense Force riding the spearhead as it thrust forward, erasing the wind in its path.
*Poom!*
Jeok Cheongang struck out with both palms without hesitation.
The dark crimson mist surrounding them scattered in an instant.
Flame Divine Palm, unleashed at full strength, surged upward as a pillar of fire.
It raced toward an opponent who had tried to hide his presence, but whose immense energy made it impossible to conceal himself completely.
And in the next moment, Jeok Cheongang understood all over again.

With the Temporary Strength Pill’s power behind him, the North Heaven Demon Lord could look down on even Jeok Cheongang—who had reached his current realm through several moments of enlightenment—as half a step beneath him.
*Shwaa!*
The spearhead pierced a single precise point.
The immense Force at its tip split flames that had seemed capable of burning the whole world, and the distance between the two men vanished.
Jeok Cheongang’s eyes widened at the overwhelming force.
This wasn’t a question of enlightenment in the martial arts.

The North Heaven Demon Lord’s movements, enhanced to an extreme, made everything possible—along with internal energy so powerful it made Jeok Cheongang wonder if he had drawn out every last bit of his innate qi.
*Damn it.*
Swallowing the curse rising to his lips, Jeok Cheongang drew on all the internal energy in his body.
He slammed both hands together against the spearhead plunging toward his chest.
*Krrrrk!*
The spearhead trembled between his palms, pressed together as if in prayer.
Dark crimson Force tore into flesh and bone despite his Body-Protecting Qi.
Jeok Cheongang clenched his teeth against the pain.
*Crack.*
The pain of breaking a molar was nothing beside what came from his hands as they grew more mangled by the second.
Jeok Cheongang swallowed the blood rising in his throat and held fast to the spearhead.
The North Heaven Demon Lord bared his teeth in a grin.
“Why not stop now and get some rest?
You look exhausted.”
Jeok Cheongang’s reply came through clenched teeth, edged with mockery.
“Right back at you.”
The North Heaven Demon Lord’s eyes darkened.
He could feel throughout his body that Jeok Cheongang wasn’t bluffing.
*What kind of monster is this old man?*
*Crack.
Krrrunch.*
Though he drove it with all his strength, the spearhead could go no farther.
Jeok Cheongang’s skin was crushed by the Force, but his toes were dug deep into the ground, perfectly still.
The old monster of Mount Jiuhua had returned decades younger—and far stronger than the North Heaven Demon Lord remembered.
Strong enough that even after taking the Temporary Strength Pill, he couldn’t bring him down easily.
*It ends here.*
The moment that thought formed, the North Heaven Demon Lord twisted the spear shaft with every ounce of strength he had.
This time, even Jeok Cheongang would be unable to bear the pain.
*Crack.*
At the grisly sound of flesh tearing, Jeok Cheongang’s body shuddered.
Then a thunderous shout burst from Jamukha’s lips.
“Jamukha!”
At that instant—
*KABOOM!
Shhk!*
With a thunderous crash, a razor-sharp gust of wind shot toward Jeok Cheongang’s back.

chapters.title: Chapter 975
paragraphs: No matter how well trained a hunting dog was, it couldn’t take down a predator on its own.
There was no getting around the difference between what they had been born to be.
But Jamukha was different. Born a predator, he had become a hunting dog to achieve his own ends.
He was a trained beast, with both the strength to face any enemy and the loyalty of a hunting dog.
That was why, the moment he heard his master call, he could spring into action without a second’s hesitation.
“Jamukha!”
The signal he’d been waiting for had barely sounded when Jamukha swung his curved blade with all his might.
*BOOM!*
Two waves of Force collided in midair.

The dark green Force of his blade, made darker and larger by the effects of the Temporary Strength Pill, pushed back the blue-white flames, if only for a moment. Just then, Jamukha’s foot shot forward like an arrow.
*Whoosh.*
His figure blurred.
Using Shifting Form and Position in that fleeting instant, Jamukha became a streak of wind and crossed more than ten *jang*.
He raced toward the Fire King—a predator more ferocious and powerful than any quarry he’d ever faced.
*One strike. One strike is all it takes.*
There was near-certainty in Jamukha’s movements, and it was no baseless boast.
For more than fifty years, he had pursued speed above all else, honing his martial arts to counter the Hebei Peng Family’s overbearing style.
Jamukha had no doubt that even Jin Taekyung, called the Divine Dragon, had his limits. He couldn’t make up for all those years of difference.
And besides...
*With this power, I can do anything.*
Everything had changed. Like a caterpillar shedding a layer and being born anew, he saw the whole world afresh.
His feet, skimming over the ground, and the beloved weapon gripped in both hands felt lighter than ever.
The Temporary Strength Pill had drawn his power beyond its limits. Even now, that power seethed ceaselessly deep within him.
His sixth sense, awakened beyond the five, let him easily evade even the streak of flame bearing down on him from behind.
*Shweeeee!*
Jamukha picked up speed and turned his head. A spearhead that had left Jin Taekyung’s hand tore through the air, grazed the back of his neck, and buried itself in the cliff face.
*KABOOM!*
Sharp fragments of rock flew in every direction. Jamukha leaped over the rising cloud of dust and raced on, his figure seeming to erase the wind.
*I’ll bring him down. No matter what.*
Jamukha’s resolve wasn’t a hunting dog’s loyalty to its master.
No—he couldn’t have called it loyalty from the start.
It hadn’t come from his heart. The other man’s strength and his own ambitions had simply come together to force him into submission.
But that was enough.
Even if his loyalty was feigned, the North Heaven Demon Lord had promised him a sure reward. Dark Heaven had enough power to make him king of the steppe and ruler of the north.
And now, Jamukha’s mighty downward slash was bringing him one step closer to that grand ambition.
*Shwack.*
In the slowed world, Jeok Cheongang still had his back to him, seemingly unable to react at all. He remained locked in combat with the North Heaven Demon Lord, his back utterly exposed.
Dark green Force, arriving before its own sound, filled Jamukha’s eyes.
*It’s over.*
Jamukha was certain.
No one could dodge this strike.
Even if his opponent was the giant known as the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, the outcome would be the same: death.
But it took only an instant for that certainty, which had risen like an exclamation point, to turn into a question mark.
*Fwoosh.*
A terrible heat suddenly washed over him from behind.
At the same time, someone’s fingertips flashed out and touched Jamukha’s long hair, braided into a queue in the custom of the steppe.
No—by the time he felt them touch it, his head was already being wrenched backward.
*Grab.*
A hand seized his hair with brutal force. His upper body bent back, and his curved blade wavered off course.
Through the sudden pain and shock, Jamukha understood why Jeok Cheongang hadn’t even turned his head in the face of such danger.
*It wasn’t that he couldn’t react.*
There was no doubt about it.
Jeok Cheongang had known from the beginning.
No—he had trusted him.
His one and only Disciple.
His Disciple’s might, something no number of years could measure.
*Whoosh!*
The dark green Force skimmed past Jeok Cheongang’s head by a hair and slashed through empty air.
As Jamukha clenched his teeth against the pain and frustration, a quiet voice reached his ear.
“Nice braid.”
“Looks easy to rip right off.”
*Krrk, krrrunch!*
The world before Jamukha’s eyes turned white.
The pain of having his hair and scalp torn off together drew a silent scream from him. He spun around and swung his curved blade.
*Whoooosh!*
The dark green Force hadn’t died out despite his terrible pain. If anything, it surged more fiercely, tearing through space.
A blade technique perfected over more than half a century in pursuit of ultimate speed.
But Jamukha had no idea.
More precisely, he could never have imagined it.

The strength and speed with which he had subdued the vast steppe in a flash fell short of the enlightenment and rewards Jin Taekyung had gained over the past two years, crossing the line between life and death again and again.
*Poom!*
Flame Divine Palm.
The tremendous blaze swept in, burning even the air. Jamukha’s upper body lurched. Unimaginable heat burned through the acupoints all over his body and ravaged them.
*Ah.*
As his vision faded, Jamukha swallowed the blood surging up from deep in his dantian.
But even after taking that horrifically powerful strike, he could still feel a spark of hope that hadn’t gone out.
The Temporary Strength Pill.
A source of power that kept welling up.
The vitality holding his body together when it should have crumpled long ago.
*Not yet. Not yet...!*
Jamukha gritted his teeth.
With all his might, he tightened his grip on the hilt as it began to slip from his hand and drove the blade down toward Jin Taekyung’s chest.
*Ka-drrk, crack!*
Two opposing sounds mingled in midair.
And then—
“Ah, that hurts like hell.”
Jin Taekyung was drenched in dark red blood and groaning in pain. Staring at him, Jamukha forced out a question.
His voice broke apart like stepping-stones in a stream.
He couldn’t understand it.
Setting everything else aside, he genuinely wanted to know.
How had Jin Taekyung blocked that strike?
What kind of sorcery had made red-tinged armor appear over the bare skin showing through his tattered clothes just moments ago?
“This... *cough*, this doesn’t make—”
*Krrrunch.*
His voice scattered in a silent scream.
Twisting the five fingers he had driven into Jamukha’s flank like a hook, Jin Taekyung answered with a tired look.
“Why couldn’t we just make this easy? Why’d you have to keep hanging on? I was saving this for later.”
What did he mean?
How was any of this possible?
His questions unanswered, Jamukha tightened his grip as if in a daze.
He had forgotten that the Force once surging like waves had died away, and that his once razor-sharp blade had gone dull.
*Scrape. Clang.*
The curved blade never pierced Fire Dragon Armor. As if clinging to its owner’s regret, it scraped across the armor’s surface before slipping from his hand.
*Poom.*
With another burst of heat from Flame Divine Palm, Jamukha heard an explosion deep inside his body.
“Guh—!”
His vision dimmed. His ears went muffled.
Everything felt strange, as if it belonged to someone else.
Distant, as though he were watching from hundreds of *ri* away.
The heat of the blood spilling from his lips. The shout that could only have come from the North Heaven Demon Lord.
And yet one thing remained vivid.
The blows that kept pounding and breaking his body.
*Poom. Poom. Pooom.*
Jamukha staggered. Even as that terrifying force battered him, he couldn’t take a single step back.
Through pain so intense it felt as if his soul were burning white, the five fingers buried in his flank held him fast like a hook.
One punch, one palm strike—each carrying terrifying power—filled his vision, raining down in a blue-white torrent.
Until everything the Temporary Strength Pill had given him was spent.
Until that vast sea of power, which had seemed as though it would spring forth forever, ran dry.
And at some point, Jamukha realized he could no longer feel pain.
*Thud.*
Like a leaf falling at the end of autumn, Jamukha crumpled.
His eyes moved weakly upward. Reflected in them were the endless dark night sky and Jin Taekyung, standing tall as a giant.
*You... You’re...*
*What are you?*
Before he could finish the thought, Jamukha’s world tilted.
*Thud.*
Heat rose in a wavering haze. Jin Taekyung looked down at the king of the steppe, blackened and lifeless, then let out the breath he had been holding.
*Hoo.*
A quiet breath.
But despite unleashing strike after strike infused with tremendous internal energy, his lips, white a moment ago, were flushing red.
As if time were running backward.
As if everything spent and worn away were returning to its original state.
*Ding. Ding. Ding.*
**System** You have defeated Lv. 173 Jamukha! You have gained a tremendous amount of EXP! You have gained a tremendous amount of Fame! Your Fame makes the Great Steppe tremble! . . .
Clear chimes rang in only one person’s ears as translucent letters filled the air.
At the end of them were the words he’d been waiting for so long.
**System** Level Up!
“Now I’m finally feeling alive.”
Feeling that stroke of luck arrive just when he needed it, Jin Taekyung shivered.
Then he smiled past the shoulder of Jeok Cheongang, who stood firm as Mount Taishan, at the North Heaven Demon Lord staring back with wide eyes.
“There were two of you. Now you’re alone.”
*Crack.*
The North Heaven Demon Lord clenched his teeth hard enough to break them and drove Jeok Cheongang back with all his might.
*Krrrunch! Bang!*
Their tremendous clash flung them in opposite directions.
Rather than absorb the shock wave, the North Heaven Demon Lord used it to speed his retreat. Jeok Cheongang saw through his intent at once and shouted.
“You—!”
But the North Heaven Demon Lord didn’t stop.
He cut through the wind and seemed to erase the space around him as he shot toward the narrow gorge’s exit.
*Shweeeee! Boom!*

A casually thrown punch shattered the massive rocks filling the gorge. The North Heaven Demon Lord thrust his spear toward the people of Shanxi, still unable to advance past the obstacles blocking their way and the force of the collisions.
*Rrrrrum.*
Space warped. At its center, the spearhead gave off a blindingly ominous flash.
But that strike, carrying an unprecedented force, never swept across the people of Shanxi.
*Shwack!*
A gigantic arrow of light tore through the air and plunged toward the North Heaven Demon Lord.

*Krrrrk!*
Space shuddered as if struck by an earthquake. A tremendous shock wave burst forth with a deafening roar, sweeping everything within a dozen or so *zhang*.
An enormous cloud of dust swallowed the narrow gorge in an instant. Through it came two gusts of wind, hotter than a midsummer afternoon and more suffocating than the desert sands far to the west.
*Fwoosh.*
The North Heaven Demon Lord felt that sudden blast of heat all too clearly.
And he saw them.
Two figures shooting toward him through the flash of light.
Two fists, born of the same root, wreathed in flames of different colors.
*Gooooong.*
Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist.
Staring into the terrifying heat burning its way through space, the North Heaven Demon Lord thrust out his spear with all his strength.
*Rrrrrum!*
At its tip, a distant flash of light blazed.
It all began and ended in an instant.
Pangu.
As if the primordial giant said to have split the world with a single axe had drawn a deep breath, the air on every side pulled taut. Then it burst outward, sweeping everything away.
*Rrrrrum!*
What could they call it?
An explosion? A catastrophe?
Jin Wikyung and the people of Shanxi had no answer.
Crushed beneath an overwhelming force they had never experienced before—no, one they couldn’t even have imagined—they could only watch as a vast wave of power swept toward them.
*KABOOM! KAAAAABOOM!*
The world turned upside down.
To keep from being flung away by the invisible shock wave, the people of Shanxi braced one another and drove their blades deep into the ground.
Their ears rang. Instinctive awe and terror gripped their bodies.
All of them, that was, except the few people responsible for the shock wave.
*Shhk.*
A spearhead cleaved through space.
Moving in a realm beyond sight and sound, Jin Taekyung and Jeok Cheongang dodged the Force shooting along its path and thrust out their fists.
*Poom!*
Air erupted with a blast of terrible heat.
The boom came late. By the time the flames that preceded it coiled through space, the North Heaven Demon Lord was already swooping down over their heads.
*Shwaa!*
His spearhead slashed down at an angle.
Just as Jin Taekyung twisted aside, the Force carried on the spearhead swelled and fell toward his shoulder.
*Shhk.*
*I cut him.*
The North Heaven Demon Lord was certain of it. He was right.
Except he had cut faintly red armor, not flesh and bone.
*Pshk!*
Blood spurted from the split in the Fire Dragon Armor, cut open by the Force.
That tiny amount—not even a handful—was all he had managed to draw. Master and disciple seized the opening.
*Crack.*
The instant Jin Taekyung clamped both hands around the spear shaft like hooks, the North Heaven Demon Lord understood on instinct.

Even with his physical abilities pushed to their limits by the Temporary Strength Pill, even with several *jiazi* of internal energy welling up without end, he could not withstand the strength of the young man before him.
*What kind of monster is this...!*
The higher you climbed, the farther you could see.
But even across the North Heaven Demon Lord’s vast world, Jin Taekyung was a monster the likes of which he had never seen.

His accomplishments were unbelievable for his age. His physical abilities far surpassed even those called superhuman. And for some reason, ever since defeating Jamukha, his movements had grown faster and stronger, and his internal energy more powerful.
That alone made him a dangerous opponent. But what chilled the North Heaven Demon Lord’s spine even more was the old monster fighting at the young one’s side.
*Whoom.*
The moisture in the cold dawn air evaporated in an instant.
Jeok Cheongang charged in with a palm strike brimming with terrifying heat. Its glow lit the North Heaven Demon Lord’s eyes red.
*The Fire King...!*
There was no other choice. No time even to look for one.
The North Heaven Demon Lord let go of the cherished spear he had carried for so many years and kicked off the ground.
*Sss!*
Burning pain seemed to seep into his very soul.
The flames surged after him as he retreated. Even a glancing touch melted his armor and scorched his skin.
And as the North Heaven Demon Lord endured that instant of pain and stumbled backward in a desperate retreat, the spearhead that had left him for a new master flashed toward him.
*Shshshshk!*

Dozens of spear images poured down, filling the air. The North Heaven Demon Lord drew on every sense, twisting and turning without pause, but the spearhead pursued him relentlessly. Blue-white flames surged from its tip.
*Fwoosh! Shhk!*
Hot.

Blood spurted through gaps in his armor where it had been cut and melted open. More blood than Jin Taekyung had shed, dark crimson blood that stained the North Heaven Demon Lord’s vision as dizziness swept over him.
Then a quiet voice reached his ear.
“It’s not over yet.”
“Grit your teeth.”
*Shhk, shhk, shhk!*
It takes years to build something up. It takes only an instant to bring it down.
The spearhead swung again and again. The armor that had covered the North Heaven Demon Lord’s entire body without a gap was all but useless.
*Clank. Clatter!*
Blood sprayed across shattered iron plates.
The North Heaven Demon Lord gritted his teeth against the searing pain.
His armor was not the only thing melting and breaking beneath the flames that struck him without pause.
Everything.
Everything he had accomplished as Murong Baek. Everything he had hoped to accomplish as the North Heaven Demon Lord. His past and future were turning to ash and scattering bit by bit.
*Why!*
He screamed inwardly, gathered the immense power he had left into his fist, and hurled it outward.
*BOOM!*
Space shook with a roar like the heavens splitting open.
Yet the strike, powerful enough to bring down a mountain, touched nothing. It only tore through empty air.
“Long ago, whenever I saw you, I had the same thought.”
The Fire King, Jeok Cheongang.
The old monster of Mount Jiuhua, who had lived for more than a hundred years, stepped toward the North Heaven Demon Lord.
*Whoosh.*
Jeok vanished as if he had evaporated. At the same instant, tremendous heat scorched the North Heaven Demon Lord’s side.
*Fwoosh.*
Blinding light-flames swallowed the darkness. The North Heaven Demon Lord instinctively looked up, his eyes turning white with their light.
“You really do have the kind of eyes no one can trust.”
In that instant, the North Heaven Demon Lord saw it.
A savage blaze at odds with Jeok Cheongang’s calm voice.
A dazzling wave of fire, neither red nor blue.
*BOOOOM!*
The roar followed the movement a moment later, shaking everything around them.
Unable to withstand the force, the North Heaven Demon Lord crashed deep into the cliff wall and swallowed the blood surging up his throat.
*Not yet. Not yet.*
It wasn’t over. He couldn’t fall.
His vision blurring, he pushed against the cliff wall cradling his body and tried to rise.
Tried to.
Until a flash of light flickered through the dust cloud rising pale beyond the countless rock fragments raining down from the collision.
*Thud! Krrrk!*
The spearhead, wreathed in blue-white flame and terrible heat, pierced his shoulder. It smashed through bone and flesh and lodged deep in the cliff.
His entire body quivered with indescribable pain.
But the North Heaven Demon Lord refused to give up. Though pain turned his vision white, he struggled with all his strength.
“GRAAAAAH!”
*Crack! Fwoosh!*
At last, the spearhead came free—or rather, his body did.
Rather than pull the spear from the cliff, the North Heaven Demon Lord gritted his teeth and tore his shoulder off the blade. Then he kicked off the ground and shot upward.
He burst through the churning dust cloud, bounding off the cliff face and the very air.
Away from the two monsters who had driven him to the brink of death.
Toward the only path of escape left to him.
*Shweee!*
The pain and injuries should have felled him long ago. His internal energy should have dwindled to a mere handful. But the Temporary Strength Pill made him forget both.
The North Heaven Demon Lord pushed onward with every ounce of strength he had.
Thinking of the prey who would be frozen in disbelief beyond the thick dust cloud settling all around.
The only lifeline that could save him.
*Jin Wikyung.*
The Lesser Family Head of the Jin Family of Taiyuan, and the Alliance Leader from Shanxi Province who had led its forces in today’s battle.
And someone’s precious flesh and blood.
*If I capture him, I have a way out.*
He had spent his life first as heir, then as Family Head of the Murong Family, one of the Five Great Families.
Black on the inside, white on the outside.
How many years had he lived among the orthodox faction, hiding the teeth of a beast?
The North Heaven Demon Lord knew those who called themselves orthodox better than anyone: their nature, their habits, the way they thought.
He knew, too, that the young upstart of the Jin Family of Taiyuan who had cornered him alongside the Fire King was bound more tightly than anyone by the word *righteousness*.
*That’s why. It’s the greatest reason you can’t defeat me—or us.*
They had lost a battle in which both sides had given everything, and the grand plan they had been certain would succeed had come to nothing.
But that didn’t mean the end.
If he survived, another chance would come.
And the North Heaven Demon Lord would return.
In the not-too-distant future, before the sting of his defeat and his enemies’ cheers had faded, he would once more unfurl the Murong Family’s banner and stride across the land.
Beneath a dark sky, with his hidden fangs bared to the fullest.
*I will return. Even if I have to stake everything on it.*
Remembering the defeat and humiliation he had suffered today, the North Heaven Demon Lord renewed his resolve.
He failed to notice that pain and hope had numbed his reason into making a foolish judgment.
He couldn’t even properly wonder why Jeok Cheongang and Jin Taekyung weren’t chasing him, even in this situation.
At last, beyond the dispersing dust, he saw Jin Wikyung—the man he had been so desperate to find.
And someone else standing tall before him, in front of Jin Wikyung, who had led everyone from the front since the beginning.
“Bow... Saint.”
*Splash.*
A low groan escaped the North Heaven Demon Lord’s lips.
Just as his steps—which had seemed as if they would go on forever—stopped in a pool of blood, he stared at the Bow Saint with hollow eyes. Then someone’s voice drifted into his ears.
“Poppy. Where did you go, Poppy?”
An anxious voice rang through the dust cloud.
Moments later, Jin Taekyung suddenly emerged from within it and stared wide-eyed at the North Heaven Demon Lord.
“Oh my god, Poppy! What are you doing here?”
The North Heaven Demon Lord’s eyelids twitched.
