chapters.title: Chapter 977
paragraphs: Shame was only one of the many emotions every human being felt, but its weight varied enormously from person to person.

For a slave scorned from the moment they were in their mother’s womb, shame might be no different from fate. For the noble and the wealthy, it could tear at the heart more cruelly and sharply than any blade.
And the North Heaven Demon Lord was very much the latter.
“Our Poppy! I was wondering where you’d run off to in such a panic. There you are.”
A face and voice full of concern.
And a smile whose lopsidedly raised corners made that concern look all the more absurd.
“I was so worried. I thought I might’ve lost you for good.”
With every mocking word Jin Taekyung spoke, the North Heaven Demon Lord’s eyelids twitched.
As if walking into an obvious trap of his own accord weren’t bad enough, now he was being treated like a dog that had run away from home.
The shame and despair gripping him were unlike anything he had ever felt before.
“How dare a nobody like you—”
“Shut up.”
Jeok Cheongang appeared beyond the thinning cloud of dust, cutting the North Heaven Demon Lord off. His gaze had gone cold and deep.
“Who do you think you are, running your mouth like that? You’re a nobody.”
The North Heaven Demon Lord gritted his teeth.
Why was this happening?
In his eyes, Jeok Cheongang had grown as imposing and brilliant as he had been long ago, during the Great Faction War.
The sight brought back the man he had once been, shrinking without realizing it before the giant known as the Fire King.
*Step.*
Footsteps rang unusually clear in his ears.
But Jeok Cheongang stopped on his way toward him and let out a short laugh.
“I’ve walked a good ten paces, yet I’m no closer. I feel like I’ve been bewitched. Don’t you?”
At his Master’s question, Jin Taekyung frowned as if puzzled.
“Come on, that can’t be right. Maybe you’re imagining it?”
“Imagining it?”
“That makes no sense. It’s not like you’re walking in place. Why wouldn’t you be any closer?”
Scratching his chin, Jin Taekyung went on with a perfectly straight face. He glanced at the North Heaven Demon Lord’s stiff expression.
“Unless some coward got scared and started backing away.”
“Oh, wait. Is that it? Seriously?”
*Crack.*
Skin split, and blood flowed.
The North Heaven Demon Lord had clenched his teeth hard enough to split his lips. He looked down at the legs that had carried him backward on instinct.
Or perhaps he’d looked away because he couldn’t bear to face the mockery on that bloodied brat’s face.
If he didn’t at least look away, he felt he might lose the last thread of reason he had left.
“Wow, it really was true. A minute ago, you took a pill and started acting all high and mighty, throwing a goddamn fit.”
Jin Taekyung strode closer with another taunt.
But this time, the North Heaven Demon Lord didn’t retreat.
No—he couldn’t.
*Soft step.*
Unlike the master and Disciple blocking his path, the footsteps behind him were light as feathers.
He half-turned. A woman approached like a gentle breeze.
*The Bow Saint.*
Caught between them. Surrounded on all sides.
Neither phrase came close to describing his situation.
Three Supreme Peak masters.

One was a member of the Three Saints, known throughout the world. Another was an old sovereign who stood shoulder to shoulder with her. And the last was a young Divine Dragon, soaring toward the heavens with that sovereign’s teachings as his dragon pearl.
*This can’t be happening. It can’t.*
The words slipped out alone from a hollow corner of his heart.
Then, at some point, the trembling in the North Heaven Demon Lord’s eyes subsided. His gaze settled.
“Even if you defeat me here today, nothing will change.”
Jin Taekyung shot back without hesitation.
“Do you people go around memorizing speeches or something? Is there a punishment if you get even one word wrong? Your internal energy gets confiscated for a week?”
“Say whatever you want. It makes no difference. That is the only truth.”
“We’ve done a pretty good job stopping you so far, though. Today included.”
At Jin Taekyung’s reply, the North Heaven Demon Lord let out a short laugh despite himself.
“If that’s what you believe, then so be it. There’s nothing wrong with holding on to hope.”
“What?”

“Finding myself in this situation made me wonder. Why did the Western Heaven Demon Lord, the Southern Heaven Demon Empress, and the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord fail? How did a plan they’d spent so long preparing fall apart in an instant?”
Jin Taekyung’s face hardened at the unexpected words. So did everyone else’s.
“What are you trying to say?”
Jeok Cheongang’s voice was cold. He looked ready to burn the man alive on the spot, but the North Heaven Demon Lord answered calmly.
“I don’t know. I’m not sure what I’m trying to say.”
“You bastard—!”
“Don’t rush, Fire King. Even if you don’t hurry me, we don’t have much time left.”
With his mind emptied, his voice was calm as well. The North Heaven Demon Lord looked inward, contemplating the energy that remained in his body, and continued.
“Half a year at most. That’s all.”
The war had already begun.
It had begun the day the absolute ruler in the darkness awoke from a long slumber.
No—long before that.
“Power beyond anything the hundred thousand followers of the Demonic Path possessed. Unbelievable powers. ‘A new heaven’ refers to that person.”
Everyone there knew whom the North Heaven Demon Lord meant.
“The Lord of Heaven...”
The Bow Saint murmured to herself, then lifted her clear eyes to look at the North Heaven Demon Lord.
“Was that why you abandoned the comrades who shared life and death with you, and betrayed the world?”
“Comrades? Did you just call them comrades?”
The North Heaven Demon Lord suddenly burst into a hearty laugh.
Comrades. People who walked the same path.
The meaning held in those two words—their utterly worthless value and the past they called to mind—made him laugh in spite of himself.
“It seems you lived in a different world from me. Well, what could you possibly know, when you shut yourselves away in remote mountain valleys without roots, turning your backs on the world?”
His bloodshot eyes moved over Jeok Cheongang and the Bow Saint in turn.
Neither of them had been known by name before the Great Faction War. They had been eccentric, reclusive masters.
But the North Heaven Demon Lord—Murong Baek—was different.
As a direct descendant of the Murong Family, one of the Five Great Families, he had seen the world. He had to wage covert battles against others who shared the same orthodox fold.
“Everyone smiled and spoke of righteousness while hiding unseen blades in their sleeves. Is that what you call comrades? Is this the orthodox faction?”
Even the stars looking down on the world would one day lose their light and fade.
Everything grew old and declined.
The world of martial artists was no different.
As time passed, the martial world had disappeared. All that remained was a cold Murim.
Chivalry had lost more and more of its worth, while the orthodox faction—including the Nine Sects and One Gang and the Five Great Families—poured its strength into struggles for power.
Taking in countless lay disciples to expand the sects under their control had become commonplace.
Some even committed the taboo of bringing the unorthodox faction into their fold. Others caused numerous casualties in clashes waged in secret.
Expansion ended in an explosion.
The power they had built up over so many years was eating away at the orthodox faction in the form of conflict.
And the northern lands, far from the Central Plains, were no exception.
If anything, things were harsher there.
At least for the Murong Family.
“You can’t claim you don’t know what roots I—or rather, the Murong Family—come from.”
The North Heaven Demon Lord looked down at the pool of blood beneath his feet.
He had the handsome features of a man who had spent his life as the Family Head of a prestigious great family, and the authority and strength to match.
Yet even after all the years the Murong Family had been rooted in Liaoning Province, the faint traces of his foreign ancestry still flowed through his veins.
Enough to bring to mind, for a moment, the face of Jamukha lying dead.
“Nomad?”
At Jin Taekyung’s murmured question, the North Heaven Demon Lord’s fist clenched on instinct, his knuckles turning white.
He had heard that word countless times.
The pointing fingers and voices that had followed him from out of sight were still there in his eyes and ears.
Nomad. Invader. Outsider.
And barbarian.
Long ago, the northeastern people called the Murong Xianbei had occupied the edge of the continent and founded a nation.
It was an age of chaos.
Five foreign peoples and sixteen small kingdoms stood divided across the land.

But the divided land eventually found stability, and the invaders who had used the turmoil to charge across the continent with lances and composite bows were either driven beyond the Great Wall or absorbed.
The Murong Xianbei were among those absorbed.
They remained in Liaoning Province and laid new foundations, establishing a great family.
The Murong Family was born.
A family of invaders descended from barbarian blood.

Their peerless martial arts and superb horsemanship had made them a towering force in Murim. Yet the other towering forces—the Nine Sects and One Gang and the Five Great Families—had looked down on them and treated them with contempt, though never openly.
“Sometimes I wondered: if the Great Faction War had never happened, would the Murong Family have survived to this day?”
Expansion ended in an explosion, but the aftermath of an explosion beyond anyone’s imagination could leave reconciliation and peace behind.
The arrival of the Demonic Cult as an outside enemy changed everything.
To survive, everyone had to join forces and fight together. The Murim Alliance, formed around the Martial God, united the feuding orthodox faction.
But Murong Baek—and the Murong Family—hadn’t forgotten.
They remembered it all clearly.
“There is no more chivalry. No more benevolence or righteousness. In the end, the only ones who survive through the years are the strong.”
The strong prey on the weak.
That was the only truth of the world the North Heaven Demon Lord had learned.
The only value and purpose in a Murim built on violence.
And so Murong Baek became the North Heaven Demon Lord.
“That was why. Nothing else.”
*Rumble. Rumble.*
A powerful tremor spread across the ground.
The North Heaven Demon Lord’s eyes were now so red that “bloodshot” no longer described them. His blood-red gaze swept over everyone in the gorge as he roared.
“Who dares! What hypocrite has the right to condemn me!”
*BOOOOM!*
The internal energy carried in his aged shout burst outward as a mighty sonic wave.
The aura was truly terrifying.
Blood flowed from the ears of the people of Shanxi, frozen like statues. Several who had been shaken to their cores by the roar alone coughed up blood and dropped to their knees.
*Vrrrrm.*
Terrible power churned around one man.
Though gravely wounded, he radiated a vast wave of qi that seemed to squeeze the air on every side. Jeok Cheongang realized the North Heaven Demon Lord had already crossed the point of no return.
Innate qi.
Just like the heads of Dark Heaven who had gone to the afterlife before him, the North Heaven Demon Lord was burning up everything he had been given in that moment.
Even knowing death waited at the end.
“If I tell you to back off, will you?”
At Jeok Cheongang’s quiet question, his Disciple reached out without a word.
*Whoosh—tap.*
A spear shaft shot toward Jin Taekyung from behind like an arrow, and he caught it firmly. Blue-white flames surged up and wound around the almost transparent spearhead. That was answer enough.
“I’ve had to listen to this bullshit for so long my whole body aches.”
“You’re too young to ache all over.”
Jeok Cheongang gave a short laugh, and Jin Taekyung laughed with him.
“I’ll go on ahead. You two can take your time catching up.”
At the same moment, dirt and rock crumbled beneath Jin Taekyung’s toes.
*Crack—BOOM!*
The ground split like a spiderweb, and a streak of flame shot forward.
The two old monsters blurred, following the Divine Dragon as he charged ahead with greater speed and force than ever.
*Flash.*
As the distance vanished between them, a blood-red glow surged upward.

sentences.text: Shame was only one of the many emotions every human being felt, but its weight varied enormously from person to person.
For a slave scorned from the moment they were in their mother’s womb, shame might be no different from fate.
For the noble and the wealthy, it could tear at the heart more cruelly and sharply than any blade.
And the North Heaven Demon Lord was very much the latter.
“Our Poppy!
I was wondering where you’d run off to in such a panic.
There you are.”
A face and voice full of concern.
And a smile whose lopsidedly raised corners made that concern look all the more absurd.
“I was so worried.
I thought I might’ve lost you for good.”
With every mocking word Jin Taekyung spoke, the North Heaven Demon Lord’s eyelids twitched.
As if walking into an obvious trap of his own accord weren’t bad enough, now he was being treated like a dog that had run away from home.
The shame and despair gripping him were unlike anything he had ever felt before.
“How dare a nobody like you—”
“Shut up.”
Jeok Cheongang appeared beyond the thinning cloud of dust, cutting the North Heaven Demon Lord off.
His gaze had gone cold and deep.
“Who do you think you are, running your mouth like that?
You’re a nobody.”
The North Heaven Demon Lord gritted his teeth.
Why was this happening?
In his eyes, Jeok Cheongang had grown as imposing and brilliant as he had been long ago, during the Great Faction War.
The sight brought back the man he had once been, shrinking without realizing it before the giant known as the Fire King.
*Step.*
Footsteps rang unusually clear in his ears.
But Jeok Cheongang stopped on his way toward him and let out a short laugh.
“I’ve walked a good ten paces, yet I’m no closer.
I feel like I’ve been bewitched.
Don’t you?”
At his Master’s question, Jin Taekyung frowned as if puzzled.
“Come on, that can’t be right.
Maybe you’re imagining it?”
“Imagining it?”
“That makes no sense.
It’s not like you’re walking in place.
Why wouldn’t you be any closer?”
Scratching his chin, Jin Taekyung went on with a perfectly straight face.
He glanced at the North Heaven Demon Lord’s stiff expression.
“Unless some coward got scared and started backing away.”
“Oh, wait.
Is that it?
Seriously?”
*Crack.*
Skin split, and blood flowed.
The North Heaven Demon Lord had clenched his teeth hard enough to split his lips.
He looked down at the legs that had carried him backward on instinct.
Or perhaps he’d looked away because he couldn’t bear to face the mockery on that bloodied brat’s face.
If he didn’t at least look away, he felt he might lose the last thread of reason he had left.
“Wow, it really was true.
A minute ago, you took a pill and started acting all high and mighty, throwing a goddamn fit.”
Jin Taekyung strode closer with another taunt.
But this time, the North Heaven Demon Lord didn’t retreat.
No—he couldn’t.
*Soft step.*
Unlike the master and Disciple blocking his path, the footsteps behind him were light as feathers.
He half-turned.
A woman approached like a gentle breeze.
*The Bow Saint.*
Caught between them.
Surrounded on all sides.
Neither phrase came close to describing his situation.
Three Supreme Peak masters.
One was a member of the Three Saints, known throughout the world.
Another was an old sovereign who stood shoulder to shoulder with her.
And the last was a young Divine Dragon, soaring toward the heavens with that sovereign’s teachings as his dragon pearl.
*This can’t be happening.
It can’t.*
The words slipped out alone from a hollow corner of his heart.
Then, at some point, the trembling in the North Heaven Demon Lord’s eyes subsided.
His gaze settled.
“Even if you defeat me here today, nothing will change.”
Jin Taekyung shot back without hesitation.
“Do you people go around memorizing speeches or something?
Is there a punishment if you get even one word wrong?
Your internal energy gets confiscated for a week?”
“Say whatever you want.
It makes no difference.
That is the only truth.”
“We’ve done a pretty good job stopping you so far, though.
Today included.”
At Jin Taekyung’s reply, the North Heaven Demon Lord let out a short laugh despite himself.
“If that’s what you believe, then so be it.
There’s nothing wrong with holding on to hope.”
“What?”
“Finding myself in this situation made me wonder.
Why did the Western Heaven Demon Lord, the Southern Heaven Demon Empress, and the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord fail?
How did a plan they’d spent so long preparing fall apart in an instant?”
Jin Taekyung’s face hardened at the unexpected words.
So did everyone else’s.
“What are you trying to say?”
Jeok Cheongang’s voice was cold.
He looked ready to burn the man alive on the spot, but the North Heaven Demon Lord answered calmly.
“I don’t know.
I’m not sure what I’m trying to say.”
“You bastard—!”
“Don’t rush, Fire King.
Even if you don’t hurry me, we don’t have much time left.”
With his mind emptied, his voice was calm as well.
The North Heaven Demon Lord looked inward, contemplating the energy that remained in his body, and continued.
“Half a year at most.
That’s all.”
The war had already begun.
It had begun the day the absolute ruler in the darkness awoke from a long slumber.
No—long before that.
“Power beyond anything the hundred thousand followers of the Demonic Path possessed.
Unbelievable powers.
‘A new heaven’ refers to that person.”
Everyone there knew whom the North Heaven Demon Lord meant.
“The Lord of Heaven...”
The Bow Saint murmured to herself, then lifted her clear eyes to look at the North Heaven Demon Lord.
“Was that why you abandoned the comrades who shared life and death with you, and betrayed the world?”
“Comrades?
Did you just call them comrades?”
The North Heaven Demon Lord suddenly burst into a hearty laugh.
Comrades.
People who walked the same path.
The meaning held in those two words—their utterly worthless value and the past they called to mind—made him laugh in spite of himself.
“It seems you lived in a different world from me.
Well, what could you possibly know, when you shut yourselves away in remote mountain valleys without roots, turning your backs on the world?”
His bloodshot eyes moved over Jeok Cheongang and the Bow Saint in turn.
Neither of them had been known by name before the Great Faction War.
They had been eccentric, reclusive masters.
But the North Heaven Demon Lord—Murong Baek—was different.
As a direct descendant of the Murong Family, one of the Five Great Families, he had seen the world.
He had to wage covert battles against others who shared the same orthodox fold.

chapters.title: Chapter 978
paragraphs: Every now and then, I catch myself realizing how much I’ve changed.
In this miserable fight, where every moment demands that I risk my life, I keep moving forward—and feel a thrill I can’t explain.
“Jin Taekyung!”
A shout like a lion’s roar lashed at my ears.
Beyond the wind whipping around me, I brought White Flame down on the blood-red light bursting from the North Heaven Demon Lord’s fingertips.
*Shhk!*
The enormous Palm Force split in two along the path of my spearhead.
Leaving behind the tremendous impact and explosion as the deflected Palm Force shook the cliffs on either side, I planted my foot on the ground once more.
*Tap.*
The flames that should have burst forth from Flamefire Path were nowhere to be seen.
My feet, guided by the Slaughter Saint’s teachings, felt lighter than ever. I shot forward like a flash of light.
Like the beam that had suddenly come streaking from far across the gorge.
*Shwaaa!*
Compressed air tore apart. At the arrow of light that had outrun even sound, the North Heaven Demon Lord swung a fist seething with rage and internal energy.
*BOOOOM!*
Contact. Then an explosion.
Within the swelling flash, I saw the beam the Bow Saint had shot vanish into the dark red glow.
I seized the opening. By the time the North Heaven Demon Lord’s eyes caught my reflection, I was right in front of him.
*I can see it.*
The world slowed in an instant.
Everything around me was sharp and vivid.
His lips moving slowly, as though he were trying to say something.
His eyes, so red there wasn’t a trace of white left in them.
And the condensed Palm Force blocking the spearhead I had thrust forward with all my might.
*Krrrk!*
Two different Forces collided. Blue-white flames and dark red shadows met in midair, mingling as they sent out a violent wave of force.
“Just... this much.”
His words came in broken fragments.
The North Heaven Demon Lord glared at me, gripping my spearhead in one hand. Streams of blazing red seemed to pour from his eyes.
“Did you think you could defeat me—Murong Baek—with this?”
*Zzzzzzt!*

An unprecedented energy flared up like a wildfire, pressing down on the flames carried by my spearhead. The power the North Heaven Demon Lord had gained by burning even his own life came at a steep and tremendous price: a death already set in stone.
Even with all my fatigue and injuries completely healed after I took down Jamukha, victory seemed impossible.
But...
*Yeah. This is about what I expected.*
I smiled.
The strength I sensed from the North Heaven Demon Lord was within the range I’d expected.
And the energy rushing in from behind me, fast as a flash of light, was immense enough to rival his.
*Now.*
There was no shouted warning. No Sound Transmission.
But I knew. So did he.
Even without seeing each other, we knew each other too well.
So, without the slightest fear or hesitation, we moved as the thought flashed through our minds.
*Slip.*
The instant I let go of the spear shaft and turned halfway around—
A streak of flame, hidden behind my body—a frame massive enough to be called a giant—filled the space I’d left and exploded.
*Gooooong.*
Like the breath of a fire dragon from legend, pure white hellfire blazed across the darkness.
It burned away the dew in the dawn air, vaporizing it as it rushed toward the North Heaven Demon Lord.
*Fire. King.*
His lips moved ever so slightly, forming a soundless cry. His eyes, heated by the scorching air, wavered, losing their focus.
Confusion and fear he couldn’t hide.
Those emotions, revealed on instinct, meant the North Heaven Demon Lord had sensed someone else—not me or Jeok Cheongang.
*Shwaaa!*
Behind him, two gently curved blades traced beautiful arcs.
The strike was utterly unlike the furious flames bearing down on him from the front, yet the energy it carried was no less deadly.
In the slowed world, the North Heaven Demon Lord’s eyes flew wide.
Jeok Cheongang’s Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist came from the front. From behind, the Bow Saint’s twin blades, transformed into curved swords, came down on him.
Two Supreme Peak masters unleashed a terrifying combined attack. With neither time nor room to dodge, he had no choice left.
*BOOM! KAAAAAABOOM!*
In an instant, all the darkness hanging over the gorge lifted.
A blood-red glow burst out, wrapping around the North Heaven Demon Lord’s entire body.
*Krrrrrk!*
The world shook. A relentless wave of force swept in every direction, and the ground crumbled beneath the three combatants’ feet.
*Crack! Krrrk!*
The ground split like a spiderweb, unable to withstand the tremendous pressure.
As I had done at the last moment, the North Heaven Demon Lord twisted his body and changed direction. His whole frame shuddered violently like a tree caught in a typhoon.
His face twisted like a Fiend’s as he caught Jeok Cheongang’s fist in one hand and both of the Bow Saint’s curved blades in the other.
*No. He was already a Fiend. Had been for a long time.*
No matter how many years a monster spent wearing a human face, its nature didn’t disappear.
The North Heaven Demon Lord—Murong Baek—had crossed a river from which there was no return.
Like so many other monsters who had pursued the Demonic Path for their own reasons, heading off somewhere.
*Crack—splatter!*
Blood gushed from the flesh and joints of bone, slowly being cut and crushed.
The North Heaven Demon Lord convulsed in pain beyond anything he had imagined.
Both hands, holding off the Fire King and the Bow Saint, were losing their shape even now.
Yet one thing would remain unchanged to the end: those eyes filled with bitter hatred.
“Why? Why...?”
I could feel all the pain and hatred in the North Heaven Demon Lord’s voice as he ground the words out through teeth clenched hard enough to draw blood.
I could feel the sliver of fear he couldn’t quite hide as I slowly approached, too.
“I... won’t... die.”
The North Heaven Demon Lord’s words broke apart between gasping breaths. Jeok Cheongang answered, his expression calm.
“Everyone dies. People and monsters alike.”
The blood-red light that seemed about to devour the whole world and the force that had been pressing down on everything around us were nowhere to be seen now.
Even if some remained, they were fading like a lamp before the wind.
*Krrrk.*
The pressure was more than one hand could withstand.
Before the white hellfire Jeok Cheongang drew forth with all his strength, alongside his quiet reply, the North Heaven Demon Lord finally dropped to one knee.
*BOOM!*
The ground caved in beneath him. The Bow Saint’s voice reached the North Heaven Demon Lord as he stared with eyes bulging wide.
“We’re born human, and we make our choices by our own judgment. There is no right answer. But... this is the consequence of your choice.”
What life has a right answer?
Life isn’t multiple choice. It isn’t a test graded on short answers or essays, either.
Whatever life a person has lived, looking back, there will always be at least one thing they regret. That is what human life is.
But both the judgment and the consequences are your own. That’s all.
“Murong Baek, the Divine Spear of the Imugi. No—the North Heaven Demon Lord. It’s time to accept the consequence of your choice.”
There’s a reason and a history behind every martial artist’s sobriquet.
When I heard that unfamiliar one from the Bow Saint’s lips, I felt as though I’d caught a glimpse of the life Murong Baek had lived.
The imugi.
An imugi that never became a dragon.
And at the same time, an imugi that had wanted to become a dragon more than anyone.
Maybe that was why.
Why he had struggled so desperately to obtain the dragon pearl.
Why he had searched for every excuse and justification to remain beneath Dark Heaven’s shadow, hoping to become a dragon soaring freely through the azure heaven.
But knowing something and understanding it are different.
Even if every story he’d told us was true, I would never understand Murong Baek, the North Heaven Demon Lord.
No. I would refuse to understand him.
The day I understood him would be the day I became a monster, too, on the far side of that deep, dark river.
“Before you go, know this.”
With a quiet voice, I reached out.
The pure white spear shaft the North Heaven Demon Lord had been forced to let go of to face Jeok Cheongang and the Bow Saint flew into my grip as though drawn there.
“Not everyone in the world makes the same choice you did.”
The weak are cast aside, and the strong survive.
That’s how this world has always been—always, without fail.
The law of the jungle existed not just in Murim, but in the modern world, too. And it would continue to exist, with means other than spears and swords.
But if everyone made the same choice as the North Heaven Demon Lord out of fear of being cast aside, the world would already have become a hellscape.
A place without even the barest sense of decency or benevolence.
A terrible world that went on endlessly for one purpose alone: to devour others or be devoured.
But not everyone is like the North Heaven Demon Lord. That’s why I still think this world is worth living in.
And I believe, too—
Among all those countless people scattered like stars across the night sky, whoever gave such inexplicable power to an unremarkable F-rank Hunter must feel the same way.
“Now, go.”
I didn’t wait for an answer.
I simply thrust my spearhead, wreathed in blue-white flames, into him—quietly and without hesitation.
Toward the North Heaven Demon Lord, who still refused to give up, struggling as he burned through every bit of life left in his body.
Toward the chest of a monster who had lived not simply to protect what was precious to him, but to seize what belonged to others and make himself greater.
*Thud.*
The blazing flames pierced flesh and bone.
As if someone had lit a candle, the being in the darkness suddenly opened its eyes.
How long had it been asleep?
How much time had passed in that abyssal dream where everything was tangled together?
It couldn’t know.
The question was familiar, and the conclusion was always the same.
It had always been that way for the being in the darkness.
Whenever it woke, the world had changed. It had once slept for decades, after all.
But as the years passed and the intervals between its awakenings grew shorter, it had begun to realize something.
The day it had thought it would never reach had, at some point, drawn right up to its doorstep.
*Fwoooosh.*
A cool wind swept through the area. In moments, it became a raging gale.
It extinguished the torches that faintly lit the thick darkness and shook the ground and roof.
That sudden upheaval, like great waves rising on a tranquil lake, was proof that the being in the darkness had realized why it had opened its eyes.
North Heaven.
The fourth heaven had fallen. Another faithful servant was gone.
The news would soon shock all beneath the heavens.
But alone in the darkness, the being smiled.

Behind him, two gently curved blades traced beautiful arcs.
The strike was utterly unlike the furious flames bearing down on him from the front, yet the energy it carried was no less deadly.
In the slowed world, the North Heaven Demon Lord’s eyes flew wide.
Jeok Cheongang’s Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist came from the front.
From behind, the Bow Saint’s twin blades, transformed into curved swords, came down on him.
Two Supreme Peak masters unleashed a terrifying combined attack.
With neither time nor room to dodge, he had no choice left.
*BOOM!
KAAAAAABOOM!*
In an instant, all the darkness hanging over the gorge lifted.
A blood-red glow burst out, wrapping around the North Heaven Demon Lord’s entire body.
*Krrrrrk!*
The world shook.
A relentless wave of force swept in every direction, and the ground crumbled beneath the three combatants’ feet.
*Crack!
Krrrk!*
The ground split like a spiderweb, unable to withstand the tremendous pressure.
As I had done at the last moment, the North Heaven Demon Lord twisted his body and changed direction.
His whole frame shuddered violently like a tree caught in a typhoon.
His face twisted like a Fiend’s as he caught Jeok Cheongang’s fist in one hand and both of the Bow Saint’s curved blades in the other.
*No.
He was already a Fiend.
Had been for a long time.*
No matter how many years a monster spent wearing a human face, its nature didn’t disappear.
The North Heaven Demon Lord—Murong Baek—had crossed a river from which there was no return.
Like so many other monsters who had pursued the Demonic Path for their own reasons, heading off somewhere.
*Crack—splatter!*
Blood gushed from the flesh and joints of bone, slowly being cut and crushed.
The North Heaven Demon Lord convulsed in pain beyond anything he had imagined.
Both hands, holding off the Fire King and the Bow Saint, were losing their shape even now.
Yet one thing would remain unchanged to the end: those eyes filled with bitter hatred.
“Why?
I could feel all the pain and hatred in the North Heaven Demon Lord’s voice as he ground the words out through teeth clenched hard enough to draw blood.
I could feel the sliver of fear he couldn’t quite hide as I slowly approached, too.
“I... won’t... die.”
The North Heaven Demon Lord’s words broke apart between gasping breaths.
Jeok Cheongang answered, his expression calm.
“Everyone dies.
People and monsters alike.”
The blood-red light that seemed about to devour the whole world and the force that had been pressing down on everything around us were nowhere to be seen now.
Even if some remained, they were fading like a lamp before the wind.
*Krrrk.*
The pressure was more than one hand could withstand.
Before the white hellfire Jeok Cheongang drew forth with all his strength, alongside his quiet reply, the North Heaven Demon Lord finally dropped to one knee.
*BOOM!*
The ground caved in beneath him.
The Bow Saint’s voice reached the North Heaven Demon Lord as he stared with eyes bulging wide.
“We’re born human, and we make our choices by our own judgment.
There is no right answer.
But... this is the consequence of your choice.”
What life has a right answer?
Life isn’t multiple choice.
It isn’t a test graded on short answers or essays, either.
Whatever life a person has lived, looking back, there will always be at least one thing they regret.
That is what human life is.
But both the judgment and the consequences are your own.
That’s all.
“Murong Baek, the Divine Spear of the Imugi.
No—the North Heaven Demon Lord.
It’s time to accept the consequence of your choice.”
There’s a reason and a history behind every martial artist’s sobriquet.
When I heard that unfamiliar one from the Bow Saint’s lips, I felt as though I’d caught a glimpse of the life Murong Baek had lived.
The imugi.
An imugi that never became a dragon.
And at the same time, an imugi that had wanted to become a dragon more than anyone.
Maybe that was why.
Why he had struggled so desperately to obtain the dragon pearl.
Why he had searched for every excuse and justification to remain beneath Dark Heaven’s shadow, hoping to become a dragon soaring freely through the azure heaven.
But knowing something and understanding it are different.
Even if every story he’d told us was true, I would never understand Murong Baek, the North Heaven Demon Lord.
No.
I would refuse to understand him.
The day I understood him would be the day I became a monster, too, on the far side of that deep, dark river.
“Before you go, know this.”
With a quiet voice, I reached out.
The pure white spear shaft the North Heaven Demon Lord had been forced to let go of to face Jeok Cheongang and the Bow Saint flew into my grip as though drawn there.
“Not everyone in the world makes the same choice you did.”
The weak are cast aside, and the strong survive.
That’s how this world has always been—always, without fail.
The law of the jungle existed not just in Murim, but in the modern world, too.
And it would continue to exist, with means other than spears and swords.
But if everyone made the same choice as the North Heaven Demon Lord out of fear of being cast aside, the world would already have become a hellscape.
A place without even the barest sense of decency or benevolence.
A terrible world that went on endlessly for one purpose alone: to devour others or be devoured.
But not everyone is like the North Heaven Demon Lord.
That’s why I still think this world is worth living in.
And I believe, too—
Among all those countless people scattered like stars across the night sky, whoever gave such inexplicable power to an unremarkable F-rank Hunter must feel the same way.
“Now, go.”
I didn’t wait for an answer.
I simply thrust my spearhead, wreathed in blue-white flames, into him—quietly and without hesitation.
Toward the North Heaven Demon Lord, who still refused to give up, struggling as he burned through every bit of life left in his body.
Toward the chest of a monster who had lived not simply to protect what was precious to him, but to seize what belonged to others and make himself greater.
*Thud.*
The blazing flames pierced flesh and bone.
As if someone had lit a candle, the being in the darkness suddenly opened its eyes.
How long had it been asleep?
How much time had passed in that abyssal dream where everything was tangled together?
It couldn’t know.
The question was familiar, and the conclusion was always the same.
It had always been that way for the being in the darkness.
Whenever it woke, the world had changed.
It had once slept for decades, after all.
But as the years passed and the intervals between its awakenings grew shorter, it had begun to realize something.
The day it had thought it would never reach had, at some point, drawn right up to its doorstep.
*Fwoooosh.*
A cool wind swept through the area.
In moments, it became a raging gale.
It extinguished the torches that faintly lit the thick darkness and shook the ground and roof.
That sudden upheaval, like great waves rising on a tranquil lake, was proof that the being in the darkness had realized why it had opened its eyes.
North Heaven.
The fourth heaven had fallen.
Another faithful servant was gone.
The news would soon shock all beneath the heavens.
But alone in the darkness, the being smiled.

chapters.title: Chapter 979
paragraphs: At some point, everyone realized.
“Waaaaah!”
A tremendous roar shook heaven and earth as it rolled over the narrow gorge called Eight Spring Gorge.
The fighters locked in fierce battle across the vast basin all turned their heads at once.
Their lips were cracked like drought-stricken fields. Their hands and feet trembled with exhaustion and fear of death.

After hours of fighting, they were covered in blood from head to toe. They stared desperately toward the gorge’s entrance, praying that the roar drawing closer—and the countless footsteps pounding the earth—belonged to their allies.
Then, beyond the thinning darkness, a streak of light flashed.
*Shwaaaaa! BOOM!*
In an instant, a deafening crash mingled with screams.
But Iron Blood Saber Peng Cheolyeong, Family Head of the Hebei Peng Family, recognized the light and laughed at the top of his lungs.
“Ha! Hahahaha!”
*Crack!*
With that booming laugh, he swung his great saber and swept through a dozen nomads in a single stroke.
Beneath the fountain of blood soaring into the air, the fewer than one thousand remaining warriors of Hebei pressed forward behind their Family Head.
Just moments ago, their bodies and weapons had felt as heavy as waterlogged cotton. Now, they felt impossibly light.
As they advanced, laughing like madmen, a thick mist of blood rose in their wake.
*Shhk! Shhk-shhk!*
“Aaargh!”
“Guh!”

Screams erupted everywhere. Neither the Murong Family’s martial artists, trained in their family’s secret arts, nor the nomads who had once swept across the land with lance and bow could stop the Hebei Peng Family.
No—more precisely, they had frozen at the unbelievable sight before them.
*Rumble!*
The ground shuddered.
As dawn approached and the darkness faded, thousands of figures poured from the narrow gorge’s entrance. A blood-soaked banner rose high above them.
The Great Jin Family of Taiyuan.
It could mean only one thing.
Eyes fixed on the characters embroidered on the banner trembled.
Some with shock and despair. Others with hope and joy.
But there were those who belonged to neither side.
“Enough! What are you all thinking?”
The Murong Family’s Head Elder, Murong Wijin, who had been directing the battlefield in Murong Baek’s place, shouted with internal energy behind his voice.
His followers flinched beneath his venomous glare.
“Don’t fall for their petty tricks! This is—this is just...”
Murong Wijin clenched his teeth, unable to finish.
What else could he say?
Anyone who wasn’t a fool could see what was happening.
Reality was chillingly cold.
They had lost. Their enemies had won.
And the ones who had returned to finish it all were neither Jamukha nor Murong Baek. They were the people of Shanxi.
Holding the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s banner so high it seemed to pierce the sky, they approached in tight formation. There was certainty in every step.
Certainty of victory.
Perhaps certainty in the four people leading them.
“Hold on. I’ve seen that guy’s face somewhere.”
His hair had grown into prickly stubble, like a lazy monk’s, and was so red it seemed to be on fire.
Facing the old monster who looked decades younger than he ought to, Murong Wijin trembled.
“F-Fire King...!”
“Oh, now I vaguely remember. Murong... whatever. Right?”
Jeok Cheongang nodded as if he’d finally figured it out. The woman beside him sighed.
“Murong Wijin. Not ‘whatever’—Wijin. And if he’s wearing the Murong Family’s uniform, obviously his surname is Murong.”
“Wijin? Who’s that?”
“That’s understandable. During the Great Faction War, he wasn’t even thirty. He was a child.”
Though Murong Wijin was nearing eighty, he couldn’t say a word.
In front of two monsters like the Fire King and the Bow Saint, he was still no more than a hot-blooded novice in Murim.
In age and in martial arts.
And there was someone else here who didn’t give a damn about either.
“Hey, what’s your name again? Murong... thingy.”
Murong Wijin’s face stiffened at being renamed by both Master and Disciple. Then Jin Taekyung stepped forward and swung his spear.
*Whoosh!*
The spear’s fierce whistle crossed dozens of yards. The round shape impaled on its tip fell precisely at Murong Wijin’s feet.
*Thump.*
When Murong Wijin saw what touched the tips of his shoes—an object that was, in fact, a person’s head—a groan escaped him before he could stop it.
“...Family Head.”
Once spoken, words couldn’t be taken back.
Murong Wijin belatedly realized his mistake and clamped his mouth shut, but the damage was done.
“You... You dare...”
“What? Not enough? Want another?”
Jin Taekyung swung his spear again, and another head sailed through the air.
This time, the nomads bit their lips as they recognized the face of Jamukha, the steppe’s greatest warrior and Great Chieftain.
“If you need more, say so. No, wait. I take that back.”
Jin Taekyung shook his head and started walking.
*Thud.*
His footsteps rang out with unusual weight and clarity.
His reddish, smoldering eyes swept across the vast basin.
“There are too many to bring here one by one. Better to make them on the spot. Fresh from the source.”
The Murong Family and the nomads—every one of them—instinctively stepped back.
Though they still had nearly ten thousand troops, an overwhelming aura and killing intent flowed from Jin Taekyung. No one dared stand against him.
And in that suffocating silence, another voice rang out.
“If you lay down your weapons and surrender now, your lives will be spared.”
One man had been overshadowed by the three Supreme Peak masters.
He had neither several jiazi of internal energy nor the godlike power to stand shoulder to shoulder with them. Yet he carried an inexplicable authority.
Perhaps it was an authority only someone who had raised a declining family and become the Alliance Leader of Shanxi Province could possess.
“You have my word. On my name, and on the authority of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”
Jin Wikyung continued calmly.
His gaze rested on a young chieftain who looked particularly haggard.
“Choose, Temur.”
“I know you. And I know you didn’t come here of your own will.”
Temur clenched his teeth.
“I’ve... come too far.”
His brother, with whom he’d shared years of hardship, was dead. And Temur had submitted.
He meant what he said. He had come too far to return to the steppe, to his homeland.
But Jin Wikyung shook his head.
“It’s not too late. Not yet.”
“...Why? Why are you offering me this?”
“Because too much blood has already been spilled. If I can prevent any more deaths, I’ll do whatever it takes.”
Despite his composed voice, a tear ran down Jin Wikyung’s cheek.
“That’s all.”
Seeing Jin Wikyung weep, feeling the sincerity in his words, Temur could hardly breathe.
He thought of the path he had chosen, so different from Jin Wikyung’s. Of all the tribespeople who had died here today because he had submitted to save his own life.
“What... do you want me to do?”
“You bastard!”
At Murong Wijin’s furious shout, the Murong Family’s martial artists moved. But a dense forest of lances had already closed in around them.
Before the army of ten thousand, now split in two in the blink of an eye, Jin Wikyung spoke.
“Surrender and submit to us. Completely.”
“Too much? Then refuse. You can join forces with the Murong Family right now if you wish. But—”
Jin Wikyung’s voice hardened, then burst into a mighty shout.
“We will fight. We will cross the Great Wall and trample the steppe. Whatever the cost, we will drive you out of there!”
At that moment, a chill ran down Temur’s spine.
The thousands of surviving nomads felt it, too.
They all heard and felt Jin Wikyung’s resolve to repay this grudge, even if it took hundreds of years and cost countless lives.
They heard the sincerity in his tightly restrained voice, seeping through clenched teeth.
And then, Temur had no choice but to decide.
“...Temur of the Golden Clan.”
Temur—the only chieftain who could fill Jamukha’s place—bowed his head.
To the Han Chinese beyond the Great Wall.
To the Alliance Leader of Shanxi and the Lesser Family Head of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
“I offer my greetings, my lord.”
In that instant, time on the battlefield—which had stood still—began to flow again.
*Shhk-shhk-shhk!*
The forest of lances swallowed the Murong Family. Behind it, thousands of people of Shanxi charged beneath the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s fluttering banner.
The blood-soaked night of the Double Ninth Festival finally woke to the dawn.
In the hazy space between dream and reality, the young man had forgotten even his own existence. He was trapped in the layers of memory piled up in his mind.
*Shwaack!*
The child could have been no more than four or five.
With a seriousness that didn’t suit his age, he swung a wooden sword as tall as he was. Each stroke cut the air with a sharp hiss.
No one knew when he’d begun or how many times he’d swung it. His little body was already soaked with sweat.
People standing at one side of the training ground watched in amazement, repeatedly letting out cries of admiration.
“Incredible. He’s held a sword for only six months, and he can already deliver a strike like that.”
“Good heavens. What a martial talent.”
“Look at that speed and trajectory. Fast and precise. It’s hard to believe he’s so young.”
“What’s truly remarkable is that he knows how to work hard. Think about it. Have any of you ever seen a child like him?”
“Never. Even the Head Elder, who was called Shanxi Province’s greatest prodigy in his youth, wasn’t like this. Though the Central Plains did have so many outstanding talents.”
“The Lesser Family Head showed such promise as a child, but then one day he became more interested in books than martial arts.”
“A shame. If he’d kept training with the sword, he’d have reached at least the Supreme First Rate realm by now.”
“What can you do? It’s in the past. The Family Head has always been unpredictable. I suppose the son inherited it from him.”
Family Head.
At the two words someone let slip, everyone clicked their tongues.
They exchanged strange glances and fell silent, but only for a moment.
Watching the child practice his sword with flawless form, stroke after stroke, they resumed their conversation as if nothing had happened.
“In any case, I don’t know much about the great sects of the Central Plains, but I doubt they have many talents like him. No, they must be quite rare.”
“He’s a great blessing to our family. Though it troubles me how gloomy he’s become for a child his age since his mother died in childbirth...”
“Mm.”
The words trailed off, and everyone’s face darkened.
“It’s tragic, but there’s nothing to be done.”
“What can we do? It’s the fate ordained by Heaven.”
“Fate? What fate?”
At the voice from somewhere nearby, the murmured conversation stopped short.
The next moment, as if by agreement, everyone fell silent and looked urgently in the same direction.
So did the young man, who had been watching it all from a spot neither near nor far.
“F-Family Head!”
Hearing someone blurt out the cry in a rush, the young man—who had just turned his head—furrowed his brow.
Perhaps it was the sunset glow spreading from the west. He couldn’t make out the face of the man slowly approaching.
Only a voice reached him, strangely familiar and faintly wistful.
“Well, judging by your reactions, I must be an unwelcome guest.”
He was a man of ordinary build.
Nothing more to add, nothing to take away.
Yet even without seeing his face, the young man could sense something distinctive about him as he scratched the back of his head.
The others facing the man, of course, couldn’t hide their confusion.
“N-No, of course not.”
“Don’t give me that. Do I look so oblivious?”
Beneath the face hidden by the sunset, his faintly visible lips curved into a smile.
He looked over the people silently watching him, then spoke again.
“I was passing by and stopped in for a moment. Don’t mind me. It seems you were watching my second son train.”
“We could hardly claim to be teaching him. The Second Young Master is so gifted that we wouldn’t dare try to correct him.”
“Of course he is. Whose son do you think he is?”
The man puffed out his chest, plainly proud. But the young man saw the smile at his lips falter and turn bitter.
Nor were the people who’d been restless ever since the man appeared any different.
“We’re sorry, Family Head.”
“We spoke out of turn. Please punish us.”
Their voices and expressions were heavy.
As they lowered their heads, the young man clicked his tongue softly without realizing it.
He didn’t know who he was or where he was, but he could infer what was happening from what he’d heard and seen.
Speaking of Heaven’s fate in front of a Family Head who had recently lost his wife...
Whatever they had intended, they deserved punishment.
Just as a nation needed strict laws to stand firm, a family had rules that must be observed.
But the man called Family Head answered in a way the young man hadn’t expected at all.
“Punishment? What are you talking about all of a sudden?”
“Pardon?”
“I told you, I just stopped by on my way past. Oh, was that talk about fate related to me? I wondered what profound conversation you were having.”
“W-Well, that is...”
“Now I’m starting to get the picture. I know how this goes. You were bad-mouthing the Family Head who lazes around all day again, weren’t you?”
“F-Family Head, that’s not...”
“Enough. You people, honestly. I may be the Family Head, but you can’t just gossip about me behind my back.”
The man folded his arms. The others, now on tenterhooks, glanced at one another.
Should they tell the truth, or let it go?
As they agonized, their mouths going dry, the man let out a deep sigh.
“Whew. You’ve confessed this much, so there’s no choice. As Family Head, I can’t just pretend I didn’t hear it. I’ll punish you now.”
Around him, people let out breaths they’d been holding.
Better to take the punishment than keep carrying the weight of guilt. Their faces relaxed as the man continued.
“Confined to your quarters. For half a day.”
“F-Family Head...”
“You’ve looked tired lately. Stay in your quarters for half a day, then get back to work. Oh, and make sure you give our eldest plenty of help.”
That was all.
The man waved away the retainers who tried to say something, dismissing them. Then he looked toward the child, who kept swinging his sword, unaware anyone had arrived.
Only after every pair of eyes around them had turned away did he murmur softly.
“Fate. Fate...”
His eyes lifted suddenly to the sky, empty. His next words were filled with nothing but bitterness.
“No. It’s all my fault.”
Then he turned his head abruptly and added,
“I’m sorry, Mukyung.”
As the man looked straight at him, the young man’s—Jin Mukyung’s—vision turned white.
*Father.*
At that moment—
*Rrrrrumble.*
The world around Jin Mukyung crumbled away. Brilliant light poured down from above, and a familiar voice reached his ears.
“Hey, you awake?”

The thousands of surviving nomads felt it, too.
They all heard and felt Jin Wikyung’s resolve to repay this grudge, even if it took hundreds of years and cost countless lives.
They heard the sincerity in his tightly restrained voice, seeping through clenched teeth.
And then, Temur had no choice but to decide.
“...Temur of the Golden Clan.”
Temur—the only chieftain who could fill Jamukha’s place—bowed his head.
To the Han Chinese beyond the Great Wall.
To the Alliance Leader of Shanxi and the Lesser Family Head of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
“I offer my greetings, my lord.”
In that instant, time on the battlefield—which had stood still—began to flow again.
*Shhk-shhk-shhk!*
The forest of lances swallowed the Murong Family.
Behind it, thousands of people of Shanxi charged beneath the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s fluttering banner.
The blood-soaked night of the Double Ninth Festival finally woke to the dawn.
In the hazy space between dream and reality, the young man had forgotten even his own existence.
He was trapped in the layers of memory piled up in his mind.
*Shwaack!*
The child could have been no more than four or five.
With a seriousness that didn’t suit his age, he swung a wooden sword as tall as he was.
Each stroke cut the air with a sharp hiss.
No one knew when he’d begun or how many times he’d swung it.
His little body was already soaked with sweat.
People standing at one side of the training ground watched in amazement, repeatedly letting out cries of admiration.
“Incredible.
He’s held a sword for only six months, and he can already deliver a strike like that.”
“Good heavens.
What a martial talent.”
“Look at that speed and trajectory.
Fast and precise.
It’s hard to believe he’s so young.”
“What’s truly remarkable is that he knows how to work hard.
Think about it.
Have any of you ever seen a child like him?”
“Never.
Even the Head Elder, who was called Shanxi Province’s greatest prodigy in his youth, wasn’t like this.
Though the Central Plains did have so many outstanding talents.”
“The Lesser Family Head showed such promise as a child, but then one day he became more interested in books than martial arts.”
“A shame.
If he’d kept training with the sword, he’d have reached at least the Supreme First Rate realm by now.”
“What can you do?
It’s in the past.
The Family Head has always been unpredictable.
I suppose the son inherited it from him.”
Family Head.
At the two words someone let slip, everyone clicked their tongues.
They exchanged strange glances and fell silent, but only for a moment.
Watching the child practice his sword with flawless form, stroke after stroke, they resumed their conversation as if nothing had happened.
“In any case, I don’t know much about the great sects of the Central Plains, but I doubt they have many talents like him.
No, they must be quite rare.”
“He’s a great blessing to our family.
Though it troubles me how gloomy he’s become for a child his age since his mother died in childbirth...”
“Mm.”
The words trailed off, and everyone’s face darkened.
“It’s tragic, but there’s nothing to be done.”
“What can we do?
It’s the fate ordained by Heaven.”
“Fate?
What fate?”
At the voice from somewhere nearby, the murmured conversation stopped short.
The next moment, as if by agreement, everyone fell silent and looked urgently in the same direction.
So did the young man, who had been watching it all from a spot neither near nor far.
“F-Family Head!”
Hearing someone blurt out the cry in a rush, the young man—who had just turned his head—furrowed his brow.
Perhaps it was the sunset glow spreading from the west.
He couldn’t make out the face of the man slowly approaching.
Only a voice reached him, strangely familiar and faintly wistful.
“Well, judging by your reactions, I must be an unwelcome guest.”
He was a man of ordinary build.
Nothing more to add, nothing to take away.
Yet even without seeing his face, the young man could sense something distinctive about him as he scratched the back of his head.
The others facing the man, of course, couldn’t hide their confusion.
“N-No, of course not.”
“Don’t give me that.
Do I look so oblivious?”
Beneath the face hidden by the sunset, his faintly visible lips curved into a smile.
He looked over the people silently watching him, then spoke again.
“I was passing by and stopped in for a moment.
Don’t mind me.
It seems you were watching my second son train.”
“We could hardly claim to be teaching him.
The Second Young Master is so gifted that we wouldn’t dare try to correct him.”
“Of course he is.
Whose son do you think he is?”
The man puffed out his chest, plainly proud.
But the young man saw the smile at his lips falter and turn bitter.
Nor were the people who’d been restless ever since the man appeared any different.
“We’re sorry, Family Head.”
“We spoke out of turn.
Please punish us.”
Their voices and expressions were heavy.
As they lowered their heads, the young man clicked his tongue softly without realizing it.
He didn’t know who he was or where he was, but he could infer what was happening from what he’d heard and seen.
Speaking of Heaven’s fate in front of a Family Head who had recently lost his wife...
Whatever they had intended, they deserved punishment.
Just as a nation needed strict laws to stand firm, a family had rules that must be observed.
But the man called Family Head answered in a way the young man hadn’t expected at all.
“Punishment?
What are you talking about all of a sudden?”
“Pardon?”
“I told you, I just stopped by on my way past.
Oh, was that talk about fate related to me?
I wondered what profound conversation you were having.”
“W-Well, that is...”
“Now I’m starting to get the picture.
I know how this goes.
You were bad-mouthing the Family Head who lazes around all day again, weren’t you?”
“F-Family Head, that’s not...”
“Enough.
You people, honestly.
I may be the Family Head, but you can’t just gossip about me behind my back.”
The man folded his arms.
The others, now on tenterhooks, glanced at one another.
Should they tell the truth, or let it go?
As they agonized, their mouths going dry, the man let out a deep sigh.
“Whew.
You’ve confessed this much, so there’s no choice.
As Family Head, I can’t just pretend I didn’t hear it.
I’ll punish you now.”
Around him, people let out breaths they’d been holding.
Better to take the punishment than keep carrying the weight of guilt.
Their faces relaxed as the man continued.
“Confined to your quarters.
For half a day.”
“F-Family Head...”
“You’ve looked tired lately.
Stay in your quarters for half a day, then get back to work.
Oh, and make sure you give our eldest plenty of help.”
That was all.
The man waved away the retainers who tried to say something, dismissing them.
Then he looked toward the child, who kept swinging his sword, unaware anyone had arrived.
Only after every pair of eyes around them had turned away did he murmur softly.
“Fate.
Fate...”
His eyes lifted suddenly to the sky, empty.
His next words were filled with nothing but bitterness.
“No.
It’s all my fault.”
Then he turned his head abruptly and added,
“I’m sorry, Mukyung.”
As the man looked straight at him, the young man’s—Jin Mukyung’s—vision turned white.
*Father.*
At that moment—
*Rrrrrumble.*
The world around Jin Mukyung crumbled away.
Brilliant light poured down from above, and a familiar voice reached his ears.
“Hey, you awake?”

chapters.title: Chapter 980
paragraphs: Jin Mukyung’s wide-eyed expression was quite a sight.
Maybe that was because, in my memory, he was always so stiff and curt.
“Hey, you awake?”
I greeted him, glad to see him.
He was looking right at me, but the focus in his dazed eyes wavered.
“F-Father...”
Maybe he’d been unconscious for too long. His voice was so hoarse that the word faded before he could finish it.
Mukyung looked thoroughly confused. Beside me, Hyuk Mujin spoke up, worry plain on his face.
“Um, could there be something wrong with his head?”
“That’s strange. The Medicine King Hall Master examined him and said there wasn’t much to worry about.”
“Even monkeys fall from trees. The Medicine King Hall Master might be one of the best physicians in Shanxi Province, but he can still make a mistake. He’s getting on in years, too.”
“Hmm. You think so?”

“To be honest, I had a bad feeling about him. Isn’t he the old geezer who threatens to ram a giant needle into a patient’s Huiyin Acupoint if they refuse treatment? Captain, don’t you remember when he pulled that on you while we were trading blows with the Mount Heng Sword Sect?”
Of course I remembered.
The Medicine King Hall Master had been terrifying when he’d announced he was going to perform a forced opening ceremony with a needle as thick as my forearm.
*Still, for all his temper, he seemed to know his stuff.*
I’d checked Mukyung myself several times, too.
There were limits to examining someone’s insides by channeling internal energy into them. Even taking that into account, though, his condition wasn’t all that serious.
Not for someone who’d just fought a Supreme Peak master a level above him.
“Go get the Medicine King Hall Master first. Oh, and if you can...”
“I’ll bring Great Hero Jeok too, if possible. Right?”
“Yeah.”
That kid was quick on the uptake. These days, he knew what I meant before I even finished saying it.
Hyuk Mujin gave a small bow and turned away. He was just about to take his first step when—
“Where... am I?”
His lips were cracked like drought-stricken fields. His voice came out in broken, hoarse bursts.
But it was too soon to relax.
His eyes were only beginning to focus again, so I cautiously waved my hand in front of them.
“Can you see this?”
“I can... see it. But where am I...?”
“Where do you think? The Jin Family of Taiyuan.”
“If that’s... the case...”
I could guess what he was trying to ask. Since he was struggling to get the words out, I gave him the answer he wanted most.
“We won.”
“Ah.”
“The nomads who were left surrendered to us completely, and everyone in the Murong Family was either killed or captured.”
“What about... the others?”
His questions kept coming, one after another. I pretended not to hear and ignored them.
I couldn’t tell him yet.
Not yet.
“I’ll tell you later.”
“What?”
“Look at you. Your eyes are still out of it. Tell me how many fingers I’m holding up.”
Mukyung knew better than anyone that he hadn’t fully come around. I held up three fingers, slipping the change of subject in while he frowned at me.
“Three.”
“Good. And now?”
“Five.”
He answered both without hesitation. His head seemed to be clearing.
But the most important final step remained.
With a grave expression, I took off my shoe and stuck out my toes.
“And now?”
Mukyung was quiet for a moment. Then he spoke, his voice astonishingly firm.
“Move your filthy foot before I kill you.”
“Hmm. Perfect. Feeling more like yourself now, patient?”
Mukyung let out a shallow sigh.
“Yeah, you son of a bitch.”
“Now, now. You can’t talk like that to your own brother. Spit while lying down, and it’ll land on your own face.”
I didn’t bother adding *though in reality, I was an outsider with not a drop of their blood in me.*
At least in the world I was living in now—Murim—the three sons of the Jin Family of Taiyuan had been born to the same parents.
But at that teasing remark, an odd swirl of emotion surfaced on Mukyung’s face for the briefest moment.
“What? Why are you looking at me like that?”
“None of your business. I just...”
Mukyung hesitated.
“I just had a strange dream.”
“A strange dream? A nightmare?”
“Not quite a nightmare... I don’t know. It was strange. That’s all.”
He still looked a little confused, but I shrugged it off.
*Well, it happens. I have all kinds of dreams every time I pass out.*
I was used to it.
No—maybe it was one of the chronic problems shared by Hunters and Murim people alike.
Keep coming close to death, and your state of mind is bound to change. That unease often comes out in dreams.
“So, how do you feel?”
“How do I feel...”
Mukyung tried to sit up too quickly and frowned.
“Broken bones. Three, from what I can tell.”
I nodded, satisfied. A patient who could feel the pain and assess his own condition was showing a good sign.
“Exactly. That matches the Medicine King Hall Master’s diagnosis.”
“My muscles hurt so much I can’t even move. It feels like someone tore every muscle in my body to shreds.”
“Of course you’re in pain. You fought like a maniac. Perfectly normal.”
“My internal injury... For some reason, it’s not as bad as I expected.”
I puffed out my chest, as if I’d been waiting for him to say that.
“I put in a little effort.”
“You did?”
“Yep. You can thank me.”
Mukyung stared at me for a while, then nodded.
“I see.”
“That’s it?”
“Yeah.”
“Hmm. Strange. People who were raised right usually say thank you in a situation like this.”
“...Didn’t you just say something about spitting while lying down?”
“Me? When?”
I put on an innocent, confused expression. Mukyung sighed softly.
“Thank you.”
“I don’t feel any sincerity.”
“Thank you. I mean it.”
“Hmm. Somehow it feels like I’m making you bow down and thank me.”
“Let’s call that practice. One more time, and mean it this time.”
Mukyung took a deep breath.
“I survived thanks to you. I’m truly grateful.”
I wanted to tease him some more, but the look in his eyes told me I’d better stop there. Hiding my disappointment, I patted his shoulder.
“Good. That’s more like it. I’ll pass along your thanks.”
“Even after all this time, you’re exactly the same... What? Pass them along? What do you mean?”
“It’s nothing. Don’t worry about it. Some people helped treat your internal injury, that’s all.”
“Helped? Who?”
“They’re here. The Fire King and the Bow Saint. They’re both pretty nice people.”
“Oh, right. You passed out early, so you wouldn’t know. Somehow, they ended up coming with me.”
Mukyung had seen Jeok Cheongang while I was staying with the Jin Family of Taiyuan. But hearing that the Bow Saint was here, too, must have been a shock in his weakened state.
He struggled to steady his ragged breathing before forcing out his next words.
“The Bow Saint? The one I know?”
“Yeah.”
“The Bow Saint from the Great Faction War? The one who uses a bow?”
“Ah. I thought so too, but if you mess with that bow, it turns into a pair of blades. Kind of like a transforming robot. Pretty amazing the first time you see it.”
“A crippled old servant...?”
“No, not a disabled old servant. A transforming robot. Though you probably wouldn’t understand even if I explained it.”
As expected, Mukyung hadn’t understood a word. He gave me a flat look.
“What the hell are you talking about?”
“Forget it. Let’s move on.”
“Fine. That’s probably for the best. So this crippled old servant you mentioned... No, the Bow Saint. You mean the one I know, one of the Three Saints?”
His words were starting to trip over themselves. I kindly nodded.
“Exactly.”
“...How did you even meet them?”
“At the Imperial Palace.”
“The Imperial Palace?”
“Yeah. The very same Imperial Palace everyone in the land knows about.”
“No, how did you get *there*?”
“It’s a long story, so I’ll give you the short version.”
Mukyung looked even more confused than when he’d first woken up. For his sake, I quickly organized the events in my brilliant mind and gave him a brief summary.
First: I went to the Imperial Palace and met the Emperor. It was a pretty scary place.
Second: We all pulled together and defeated the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord.
Third: Right afterward, I learned about the conspiracy surrounding Shanxi Province. The Emperor gave me an official post and even saw me off.
“...And that’s what happened. Got it?”
Hyuk Mujin, who’d listened to my clear and concise explanation, muttered under his breath.
“My diary from when I was six was more detailed than that.”
Mukyung, who’d stared blankly through the whole story, finally spoke.
“Are you actually insane?”
Hmm.
Ordinary people who couldn’t understand the thought process of a genius were everywhere.
In any case, after hearing the bare minimum, Jin Mukyung finally understood the situation and nodded.
“So those two treated my internal injury.”
“Right. They lived up to their reputations.”
“And you got thanked even though you did nothing.”
“Nothing? They’re my connections. I accepted your thanks on their behalf, as their representative.”
“Do you know something?”
“No. How would I? I haven’t said anything yet.”
“Sometimes, talking to you makes me feel like I’m losing my mind.”
“I’m a pretty cheerful guy. Ordinary people can’t always handle it.”
I flashed him a deliberately obnoxious grin. A bitter smile touched Mukyung’s lips.
“Is that all?”
“What?”
“I asked if that’s the only reason you’re pretending to be even cheerier than usual. Talking nonstop. Acting restless.”
I scratched the back of my head.
“Who knows? I’m not sure what you’re getting at.”
“It reminds me of two years ago. I came back to the family after a long time, and the hopeless good-for-nothing had become a completely different person.”
“The sudden change was strange, but deep down, I was a little happy. The youngest seemed to have been reborn as someone entirely new, and the more I got to know him, the more decent he seemed.”
Mukyung added, “At the very least, he wasn’t someone who’d laugh and chatter thoughtlessly while leaving behind the deaths and sacrifices of so many people.”
The corners of my mouth, which I’d forced upward, slackened.
Mukyung looked straight at me as my smile disappeared.
“You know you can’t avoid this any longer. So tell me the truth.”
The air grew heavy. My face, gone stiff, was reflected in his wavering eyes.
“Who was it, and how many people were sacrificed?”
