chapters.title: Chapter 986
paragraphs: Truth be told, I’d had some idea from the start.
Jeok Cheongang’s expression and tone were nothing like usual. Grief lay beneath his low, subdued voice—something the giant known as the Fire King rarely let anyone see.
But...
As always, a bad feeling never misses.
“You’ve arrived.”
The first person to greet us was the Medicine King Hall Master, who had been standing guard at the door.
As he picked up his bundle and prepared to leave, Jeok Cheongang spoke quietly.
“As I asked, please don’t tell anyone.”
“Thank you. You’re an excellent physician.”
The Medicine King Hall Master bowed his head slightly without a word and left. Only then could we face the man waiting inside.
“Oh, you brought him sooner than I expected. That old man’s legs are so short, I figured it’d take another seven days and nights.”
Another giant had regained consciousness after several days.
I watched the Thunderbolt Saber King laugh heartily at his own joke. Only when Jeok Cheongang nudged my shoulder did I belatedly clasp my hands in a salute, showing him all the respect I could.
“I am Jin Taekyung, a humble junior of Murim. It’s an honor to meet you, Great Hero Peng.”
“Enough. Too much humility can be its own poison. If you’re a humble junior, are all the other juniors in the world dead?”
The Thunderbolt Saber King smiled at me with satisfaction, then turned to Jeok Cheongang.
“Now that I’ve seen him, I’d say you were complaining for nothing. You kept telling me he ran wilder every day, like a brat with no respect for his elders.”
“Friend, my ass. You’ve got a lot of nerve talking to someone so much older than you like that.”
Jeok Cheongang tried to sound as gruff as ever, but he couldn’t hide the heaviness in his eyes.
Whether the Thunderbolt Saber King noticed or not, he laughed even louder.
“Wahaha! What are you so sore about? We’re both getting old.”
“Don’t you know the Three Bonds and Five Relationships? Never heard of respect for elders?”
“Would knowing them get someone to feed me? Or make my martial arts stronger?”
“Forget it. I’m the fool for trying to discuss this with an ignorant Peng.”
“Admitting your own shortcomings. I like it. I was just getting tired of talking to a stinky old man, so this works out nicely. Don’t you agree?”
At the Thunderbolt Saber King’s offhand question, I nodded.
“Well, my Master *is* a little old.”
“What did you say? Hahaha!”
A booming laugh rang out.
It didn’t suit the Thunderbolt Saber King’s pallid face. It was so loud it sounded forced.
*No. It probably was forced.*
What you could see with your eyes wasn’t everything. I could feel it.
Even now, the qi within the Thunderbolt Saber King wavered precariously, like a glass vessel cracked all over.
Like a flame that could go out at any moment.
“I heard you wanted to see me.”
At my somber words, the Thunderbolt Saber King seemed to realize I’d noticed his condition. He spoke with a smile still on his face.
“Perceptive, aren’t you? You’re worlds apart from the last time I saw you. The Fire King may not be good at much else, but he’s raised his Disciple well.”
“No need to look so miserable. For martial artists like us, life and death come with the territory.”
He was right.
That was the life of a martial artist.

The Thunderbolt Saber King had spent his life making his way through a mountain of sabers and a forest of swords, past countless threats and schemes. Now he accepted what lay ahead with calm composure.
“I had a very long dream. In it, I looked back on my whole life. I even saw my friend Murong Baek as a young man again, for the first time in ages.”
“Friend, my ass. That bastard deserved to die.”
The Thunderbolt Saber King let out a quiet laugh at Jeok Cheongang’s remark and continued.
“That’s all in the past. Nothing to be done about it now. No use trying to gather up spilled water. In the end, we stopped Dark Heaven’s plot and saved more people. That’s enough for me.”
He was famous for a temper as fiery as Jeok Cheongang’s, yet he looked at me with eyes as still as a pond.

“When I first saw you at the Star-Array Grand Banquet, I had a feeling you’d accomplish great things before long. We could all tell you’d become a pillar of the world, protecting it alongside the Sword Saint’s Disciple.”
Of course, I’d been inexperienced back then.
I couldn’t stand shoulder to shoulder with so many powerful masters the way I could now. The monster known as the Blood Lord had crushed me.
“But no one expected you to grow so much, so quickly.”
The threats to my life had come one after another, each greater than the last, and I’d grown at a staggering pace because of them.
Fast enough to make even those who’d watched me most closely doubt their eyes.
“That’s why I asked for you right away. This is my last chance to put the little time and energy I have left to the best possible use.”
“...You mean...”
“They say an ordinary tiger leaves its hide behind when it dies. The great tiger of Hebei will be different.”
At the Thunderbolt Saber King’s faint smile, I finally understood why he’d asked to see me before his own flesh and blood. He had barely regained consciousness, and death was already at his door.
“Take it. Everything I have left.”
The moment his calm voice rang out—
*Ding.*
**System** An emergency Quest, **Transmitting Internal Energy Across the Body**, has been created. **!! Warning, warning!!** This Quest carries extreme risk. Do you accept the emergency Quest? Y / N
Through the holographic window that had appeared with the clear chime, I stared silently at the Thunderbolt Saber King’s smiling face.
Then, all at once, I spoke.
“Why... Why did you choose me?”
His answer came without the slightest hesitation.
“Because I believe in you.”
“And I’m not the only one. The Dharma King believes in you. Your Master believes in you. Now the whole world believes in you.”
I could hardly breathe.
My heart tightened, and my blood seemed to surge through my veins.
Through it all, the Thunderbolt Saber King’s voice reached me clearly.
“This is all for the world, not for you. Do you need any other reason?”
“No.”
I took a small, steadying breath and continued.
“That’s reason enough.”
A smile crossed the Thunderbolt Saber King’s pallid face.
“Sit in the lotus position.”
*Ding.*
**System** You have accepted the emergency Quest, **Transmitting Internal Energy Across the Body**!
Internal energy was an intangible force that existed everywhere in the world.
Those who practiced martial arts accumulated it within their bodies. Through grueling training, they strengthened body and mind, hoping to step beyond human limits into the realm of the superhuman.
But not everyone wanted that kind of power.
The more energy they accumulated, the greater the backlash it could bring.

If someone tried to circulate their internal energy recklessly by following an incorrect formula, they were likely to end up crippled. And without enlightenment, many fell into a heart demon and became half-mad.
Even so, martial artists’ desire to reach ever higher realms rarely faded.
Theirs was a world ruled by the law of the jungle.
They devised all kinds of ways to grow stronger more safely and quickly. In the process, they discovered one astonishing method.
*What if, instead of spending years accumulating internal energy, you received someone else’s in its entirety?*
*Inherit the power of an old master on the verge of death? Huh? Isn’t that basically rock honey?*
That was how Transmitting Internal Energy Across the Body came into being in the distant past.
And from the moment it did, it became a taboo—something never to be attempted.
The reason was simple.
It looked sweet on the surface, but in reality, it was a double-edged sword.
No, even calling it that was laughable. Failures overwhelmingly outnumbered successes.
“M-Master!”
“No!”
People died. And died. And died again.

Even those lucky enough to survive often ended up crippled, their qi and blood tangled within them, or could never regain their former martial prowess. The attempts cost the world Supreme Peak masters who had dominated their eras, along with gifted young prodigies.
So when the Thunderbolt Saber King told Jin Taekyung he intended to transmit his internal energy to him, Jeok Cheongang could only ask in disbelief:
“Have you gone mad?”
“Not at all.”
“No, you’re definitely mad. Normally, you’d be flying into a rage by now.”
“I’ve only been awake for half a shichen, but my mind is unbelievably clear. I can’t remember ever being this sharp in my life.”
“Well, that’s a hell of a thing to celebrate. Does that mean you can finally finish the Thousand Character Classic?”
“Cut the nonsense. You know this isn’t simply madness.”
In truth, the Thunderbolt Saber King was right.
Jeok Cheongang had answered that way only on reflex. In his heart, he was already weighing the chances that this insane undertaking could succeed.

“I hate to admit it, but that precious Disciple of yours could withstand Transmitting Internal Energy Across the Body. He and that child Cheongpung were both born with the good fortune of a Heavenly Martial Physique, weren’t they?”
“...The Heavenly Martial Physique.”
“If that were all, I wouldn’t be having this conversation with you. He has the Muscles and Bones Heaven granted him, as well as enough potential and insight as a martial artist.”
A few months earlier, Jeok Cheongang would never have accepted a proposal that put his Disciple’s life at risk, no matter how strongly anyone pressed him.
Not even from the Thunderbolt Saber King, who now stood at death’s door after decades in which their rivalry had grown into a grudging affection.
But Jeok Cheongang had since heard the truth from Jin Taekyung himself.
*There’s a chance. No, he has what it takes.*
A transfer of internal energy between two Supreme Peak masters who had reached their realms. There was no precedent for it in the long history of Murim.
And Jin Taekyung, whose superhuman body could only be described as a Heavenly Martial Physique, possessed one more strange power.
The Prison of Karma.
A divine strength that could purify his body and even heal injuries.
With that power, he had a chance as long as he remained alive.
Besides...
*He’s already succeeded at Transmitting Internal Energy Across the Body once.*

Jeok Cheongang had heard about it only later: Jin Taekyung had received the internal energy of the Heavenly Power Demon, a great fiend of the Demonic Cult imprisoned in the Sichuan Tang Clan’s underground prison, and gone on to defeat the Western Heaven Demon Lord.
When Jeok Cheongang first heard, the knowledge that his Disciple had nearly died had almost made his heart burst. But the differences between then and now were clear.
The desperate circumstances were different. So was the martial prowess Jin Taekyung had since achieved.
*He can do it. No...*
He *will* do it.
He had to.
Jeok Cheongang steadied his wavering heart with firm resolve and watched the two men, joined through the Great Palace acupoint, his gaze deep and subdued.
*Whoosh.*
Internal energy beyond anything ever seen surged out in every direction.

sentences.text: Truth be told, I’d had some idea from the start.
Jeok Cheongang’s expression and tone were nothing like usual.
Grief lay beneath his low, subdued voice—something the giant known as the Fire King rarely let anyone see.
But...
As always, a bad feeling never misses.
“You’ve arrived.”
The first person to greet us was the Medicine King Hall Master, who had been standing guard at the door.
As he picked up his bundle and prepared to leave, Jeok Cheongang spoke quietly.
“As I asked, please don’t tell anyone.”
“Thank you.
You’re an excellent physician.”
The Medicine King Hall Master bowed his head slightly without a word and left.
Only then could we face the man waiting inside.
“Oh, you brought him sooner than I expected.
That old man’s legs are so short, I figured it’d take another seven days and nights.”
Another giant had regained consciousness after several days.
I watched the Thunderbolt Saber King laugh heartily at his own joke.
Only when Jeok Cheongang nudged my shoulder did I belatedly clasp my hands in a salute, showing him all the respect I could.
“I am Jin Taekyung, a humble junior of Murim.
It’s an honor to meet you, Great Hero Peng.”
“Enough.
Too much humility can be its own poison.
If you’re a humble junior, are all the other juniors in the world dead?”
The Thunderbolt Saber King smiled at me with satisfaction, then turned to Jeok Cheongang.
“Now that I’ve seen him, I’d say you were complaining for nothing.
You kept telling me he ran wilder every day, like a brat with no respect for his elders.”
“Friend, my ass.
You’ve got a lot of nerve talking to someone so much older than you like that.”
Jeok Cheongang tried to sound as gruff as ever, but he couldn’t hide the heaviness in his eyes.
Whether the Thunderbolt Saber King noticed or not, he laughed even louder.
“Wahaha!
What are you so sore about?
We’re both getting old.”
“Don’t you know the Three Bonds and Five Relationships?
Never heard of respect for elders?”
“Would knowing them get someone to feed me?
Or make my martial arts stronger?”
“Forget it.
I’m the fool for trying to discuss this with an ignorant Peng.”
“Admitting your own shortcomings.
I like it.
I was just getting tired of talking to a stinky old man, so this works out nicely.
Don’t you agree?”
At the Thunderbolt Saber King’s offhand question, I nodded.
“Well, my Master *is* a little old.”
“What did you say?
Hahaha!”
A booming laugh rang out.
It didn’t suit the Thunderbolt Saber King’s pallid face.
It was so loud it sounded forced.
*No.
It probably was forced.*
What you could see with your eyes wasn’t everything.
I could feel it.
Even now, the qi within the Thunderbolt Saber King wavered precariously, like a glass vessel cracked all over.
Like a flame that could go out at any moment.
“I heard you wanted to see me.”
At my somber words, the Thunderbolt Saber King seemed to realize I’d noticed his condition.
He spoke with a smile still on his face.
“Perceptive, aren’t you?
You’re worlds apart from the last time I saw you.
The Fire King may not be good at much else, but he’s raised his Disciple well.”
“No need to look so miserable.
For martial artists like us, life and death come with the territory.”
He was right.
That was the life of a martial artist.
The Thunderbolt Saber King had spent his life making his way through a mountain of sabers and a forest of swords, past countless threats and schemes.
Now he accepted what lay ahead with calm composure.
“I had a very long dream.
In it, I looked back on my whole life.
I even saw my friend Murong Baek as a young man again, for the first time in ages.”
“Friend, my ass.
That bastard deserved to die.”
The Thunderbolt Saber King let out a quiet laugh at Jeok Cheongang’s remark and continued.
“That’s all in the past.
Nothing to be done about it now.
No use trying to gather up spilled water.
In the end, we stopped Dark Heaven’s plot and saved more people.
That’s enough for me.”
He was famous for a temper as fiery as Jeok Cheongang’s, yet he looked at me with eyes as still as a pond.
“When I first saw you at the Star-Array Grand Banquet, I had a feeling you’d accomplish great things before long.
We could all tell you’d become a pillar of the world, protecting it alongside the Sword Saint’s Disciple.”
Of course, I’d been inexperienced back then.
I couldn’t stand shoulder to shoulder with so many powerful masters the way I could now.
The monster known as the Blood Lord had crushed me.
“But no one expected you to grow so much, so quickly.”
The threats to my life had come one after another, each greater than the last, and I’d grown at a staggering pace because of them.
Fast enough to make even those who’d watched me most closely doubt their eyes.
“That’s why I asked for you right away.
This is my last chance to put the little time and energy I have left to the best possible use.”
“...You mean...”
“They say an ordinary tiger leaves its hide behind when it dies.
The great tiger of Hebei will be different.”
At the Thunderbolt Saber King’s faint smile, I finally understood why he’d asked to see me before his own flesh and blood.
He had barely regained consciousness, and death was already at his door.
“Take it.
Everything I have left.”
The moment his calm voice rang out—
*Ding.*
**System** An emergency Quest, **Transmitting Internal Energy Across the Body**, has been created. **!!
Warning, warning!!** This Quest carries extreme risk.
Do you accept the emergency Quest?
Y / N
Through the holographic window that had appeared with the clear chime, I stared silently at the Thunderbolt Saber King’s smiling face.
Then, all at once, I spoke.
“Why...
Why did you choose me?”
His answer came without the slightest hesitation.
“Because I believe in you.”

Your Master believes in you.

chapters.title: Chapter 987
paragraphs: I still remember every moment of the day I first circulated my qi.
The qi-sea acupoint.
The energy I first encountered inside my body, in the place also known as the lower dantian, was pitiful.
Its name meant “sea of qi,” which felt almost laughable. In that cramped vessel, more like a little stream than a sea, only a handful of murky energy rippled.
That was right.
It had definitely been that way.
But...
Now it was different.
*Ding.*

**System** An emergency Quest, **Transmitting Internal Energy Across the Body**, has begun. **Transmitting Internal Energy Across the Body** carries extreme risks. If anything goes wrong while internal energy is being transferred and absorbed, it may lead to qi deviation or death.
As the System’s notification gradually faded into the distance, my consciousness sank deep into my body.
When my eyes opened within that world, an endless ocean stretched before me.
*Rooooar.*
It stretched beyond sight. And it was hot.
Instead of clear blue waves, waves of fire surged without end.
An ocean of flame, vast beyond measure.
At its center, a gigantic fire dragon lay coiled atop a reef as black as pitch.
*That’s...*
I knew instinctively the moment I saw it.
In this place, filled with nothing but flames and heat, the reef where the fire dragon had made its home stood out as something especially alien.
*The energy I received from the Heavenly Power Demon.*
How could I forget?
The Heavenly Power Demon, once a great fiend of the Demonic Cult who had shaken the whole world, had passed his internal energy to me and asked me to defeat the Western Heaven Demon Lord.

Decades of imprisonment and torture had worn him down, leaving him with far less internal energy than his old reputation suggested. Perhaps that was why Transmitting Internal Energy Across the Body had succeeded without killing me.
*Put too much power into a vessel, and you break it.*
The Heavenly Power Demon’s energy had remained inside me ever since.
That energy served as the nest of the fire dragon, the very embodiment of Scorching Yang Qi born of the Fire Gate Clan’s martial arts.
The two had coexisted well enough. They had even sustained each other. But now I instinctively understood something.
If I wanted to climb higher, I had to bring this strange relationship between two energies with different roots to an end.
*Wake up.*
The world around me responded to my focused will.
An unseen vibration swept across the ocean of flames and reached the fire dragon sleeping peacefully atop the reef.
*Rumble.*
Its massive body trembled. At last, its eyelids lifted, revealing blue-white eyes fixed directly on me.
The vertically slit eyes of a vicious beast.
But the emotion within them wasn’t anger at being woken. It was obedience to its master.
Of course.
The fire dragon and the reef were both, in the end, part of this ocean.
And the master of this vast world deep inside my body was none other than me.
So, the instant our eyes met, that tremendous concentration of Scorching Yang Qi joined with my consciousness.
*Whoosh!*
Warmth and consciousness mingled.
My vision turned blue-white. One with the fire dragon, I flung out both arms without hesitation.
No—I spread wings as vast as my body and took flight.
*Boom!*
The reef shook as though an earthquake had struck. With a shockwave, I shot into the air and drew a deep breath high above it.
*Hummm.*
The energy, compressed layer upon layer, screamed.
Appalling heat surged from deep inside my body and raced up to my throat. If it hadn’t been mine, it would have reduced me to ash long ago.
*Now.*
There was no hesitation. With the breath I finally released, pale blue flames burst forth and wrapped around the reef.
Before that hellfire, powerful enough to destroy the world, the pitch-black reef began to lose its shape and melt.
Then it was swept up by the waves of fire surging all around, rising high into the air. Having just breathed out a torrent of hellfire, I opened my mouth toward it.
*Whooosh.*
The moment I swallowed the dark-red liquid into which the reef had melted—
*Gasp...!*
My breath caught. It felt as though invisible blades were savagely carving through my insides.
Sharp pain assailed my mind before I could take any satisfaction in having quenched my thirst.
But I clenched my teeth.
I steadied my wavering mind and used all my strength to swallow back the energy surging up my throat.
So it could never regain its original form.
So it could dissolve into me anew.
My endurance and that choice were soon rewarded.
*Rumble.*
I could feel it.
Power swelling inside me.
The reef—or rather, the Heavenly Power Demon’s energy—hadn’t vanished.
I had absorbed it. In another sense, we had found a new way to coexist.
Unlike before, when it had been imperfect, now it had melted together into one. A perfect coexistence.
And with that astonishing change, something else began.
*Rrrrrumble!*
The world, red with flame, flashed.
A massive bolt of lightning split open the closed sky and pierced the ocean of flames.
*Ah.*
Before I could fully feel the change in my power, a genuine exclamation escaped me.
Yes.
It was a thunderbolt in the truest sense of the word.
The end of a long and fierce life.
It was the symbol of a giant standing at death’s door—and the final legacy he meant to leave in this world through me.
As that massive bolt of lightning finally entered deep into my body through the Great Palace Acupoint, I moved toward it as if entranced.
I followed it upward and upward, along the current joining sea to sky.
*Whooosh!*
I couldn’t hear it. And yet I seemed to hear it.
The sound of the fierce wind.
Everything I felt through the fire dragon’s massive body, which had long since come to feel like my own.
My consciousness raced into the depths, perceiving everything as reality. I had risen so high that the ocean was no longer visible, and at last I saw it.
A gigantic mountain rising as though it would pierce the sky.
I already knew what it was.
*The Middle Dantian.*
The mountain known as the Jade Hall Acupoint glittered like a jewel, just as its name suggested.
All but one part of it: the highest peak.
*Why? How come?*
The question had barely surfaced before I found the answer.
*It means I’m still not ready.*
It had been quite some time since I opened my Middle Dantian, but even my incredible pace of growth had its limits.
That peak belonged to the realm of enlightenment.
A realm only those with heaven-given talent, blood-soaked effort, and long years behind them could enter.
Even after growing stronger at a dazzling pace, I couldn’t easily reach that height.
But...
*If not now, when will I ever get another chance to try?*
I’d had countless strokes of good fortune, but heavenly fortune never came easily.
And an opportunity created by someone prepared to die was one I would never see again.
*Let’s go.*
Maybe my hesitation had vanished the moment all this began. Maybe the System’s warning had lost its meaning then, too.
I’d already swallowed the Heavenly Power Demon’s energy. I already knew what I had to do.
*Crackle. Crackle-crackle!*
The bolt of lightning kept shining, refusing to fade.
I leaped into its massive pillar of light.
*Rooooar!*
Everything turned white. Agony beyond anything I’d felt while absorbing the Heavenly Power Demon’s energy wrung every muscle in my body and burned away my consciousness.
*Gyaaaah!*
I didn’t know where I was.
I couldn’t tell whether the desperate scream ringing in my mind was mine or the fire dragon’s.
As my consciousness grew hazy, all I heard was someone’s thunderous shout.
“Hah!”
The instant Jeok Cheongang’s unmistakable shout rang out—
My rapidly sinking consciousness snapped awake.
Strength returned to my limp body. Memories of reality came back to me.
Who I was. Where I was.
And...
What I had to do for everyone who had believed in me, a callow, inadequate brat.
*Endure. And keep enduring.*
With all my strength, I bore the pain that kept tearing through my body.
I mustered the Scorching Yang Qi within the fire dragon and the Heavenly Power Demon’s energy I’d just absorbed. Drawing on every last scrap of strength, I bit into the pillar of lightning.
*Crunch. Crunch.*
Lightning flashed before my eyes. It held everything that giant had been, and now it was numbing my mind beyond the point of pain.
Luckily for me.
*Fuck, it’s not like I’ve never shit blood before.*
At some point, I started laughing like a madman.
I bit into the lightning, swallowed it, and kept going without pause, even as I nearly blacked out from the pain I’d known was coming.
Until the distant flash that had filled my vision slowly dimmed.
Until at last it vanished completely, as though it had never existed.
*Rumble.*
Suddenly, through my hazy consciousness, I realized:
The massive bolt of lightning that had connected my Middle and Lower Dantians was gone.
The thunder I could hear from somewhere was ringing out inside me.
*I did it...*
The moment I understood that Transmitting Internal Energy Across the Body had succeeded—
*Ding. Ding. Ding-ding-ding!*
Clear chimes began ringing without pause, somewhere far off in my consciousness.
But the sound hadn’t come from the ocean of the Lower Dantian, now far in the distance, or from the peak of the Middle Dantian, finally glowing like a brilliant jewel.
I raised my head and saw it.
Clouds beyond the mountain peak’s reach.
Another world hidden behind them.
*The upper dantian.*
I was thirsty. With my goal achieved, my consciousness, which had nearly unraveled to a thread, began to grow clearer.
It was thirst. Longing.
*More, more, more...!*
I wanted to grow stronger. I wanted to go farther.
I wanted to break through those white clouds, soar above them, and look down on everything.
But I had to force down that burning thirst and longing.
I was already at my limit.
Any more would be greed.
I knew what this momentary impulse would bring.
*Next time. I swear.*
With that vow, I looked down over the mountain and ocean that had become wholly mine.
For the first time, I faced the essence within the three currents of energy, now united, and the vast power they formed.
No—I became one with it.
*Ah. Ahhh.*
I shuddered and groaned.
I floundered in my fading consciousness.
Enveloped in a dazzling radiance where three lights mingled, I forgot everything around me.
No-self.
As I sank into that endless swamp of consciousness, I heard a voice like a hallucination.
“Good judgment. Just like back then.”
The voice felt unfamiliar, yet somehow familiar, as though I’d heard it before.
Then the thread of my consciousness snapped.

Having just breathed out a torrent of hellfire, I opened my mouth toward it.
*Whooosh.*
The moment I swallowed the dark-red liquid into which the reef had melted—
*Gasp...!*
My breath caught.
It felt as though invisible blades were savagely carving through my insides.
Sharp pain assailed my mind before I could take any satisfaction in having quenched my thirst.
But I clenched my teeth.
I steadied my wavering mind and used all my strength to swallow back the energy surging up my throat.
So it could never regain its original form.
So it could dissolve into me anew.
My endurance and that choice were soon rewarded.
*Rumble.*
I could feel it.
Power swelling inside me.
The reef—or rather, the Heavenly Power Demon’s energy—hadn’t vanished.
I had absorbed it.
In another sense, we had found a new way to coexist.
Unlike before, when it had been imperfect, now it had melted together into one.
A perfect coexistence.
And with that astonishing change, something else began.
*Rrrrrumble!*
The world, red with flame, flashed.
A massive bolt of lightning split open the closed sky and pierced the ocean of flames.
*Ah.*
Before I could fully feel the change in my power, a genuine exclamation escaped me.
Yes.
It was a thunderbolt in the truest sense of the word.
The end of a long and fierce life.
It was the symbol of a giant standing at death’s door—and the final legacy he meant to leave in this world through me.
As that massive bolt of lightning finally entered deep into my body through the Great Palace Acupoint, I moved toward it as if entranced.
I followed it upward and upward, along the current joining sea to sky.
*Whooosh!*
I couldn’t hear it.
And yet I seemed to hear it.
The sound of the fierce wind.
Everything I felt through the fire dragon’s massive body, which had long since come to feel like my own.
My consciousness raced into the depths, perceiving everything as reality.
I had risen so high that the ocean was no longer visible, and at last I saw it.
A gigantic mountain rising as though it would pierce the sky.
I already knew what it was.
*The Middle Dantian.*
The mountain known as the Jade Hall Acupoint glittered like a jewel, just as its name suggested.
All but one part of it: the highest peak.
*Why?
How come?*
The question had barely surfaced before I found the answer.
*It means I’m still not ready.*
It had been quite some time since I opened my Middle Dantian, but even my incredible pace of growth had its limits.
That peak belonged to the realm of enlightenment.
A realm only those with heaven-given talent, blood-soaked effort, and long years behind them could enter.
Even after growing stronger at a dazzling pace, I couldn’t easily reach that height.
But...
*If not now, when will I ever get another chance to try?*
I’d had countless strokes of good fortune, but heavenly fortune never came easily.
And an opportunity created by someone prepared to die was one I would never see again.
*Let’s go.*
Maybe my hesitation had vanished the moment all this began.
Maybe the System’s warning had lost its meaning then, too.
I’d already swallowed the Heavenly Power Demon’s energy.
I already knew what I had to do.
*Crackle.
Crackle-crackle!*
The bolt of lightning kept shining, refusing to fade.
I leaped into its massive pillar of light.
*Rooooar!*
Everything turned white.
Agony beyond anything I’d felt while absorbing the Heavenly Power Demon’s energy wrung every muscle in my body and burned away my consciousness.
*Gyaaaah!*
I didn’t know where I was.
I couldn’t tell whether the desperate scream ringing in my mind was mine or the fire dragon’s.
As my consciousness grew hazy, all I heard was someone’s thunderous shout.
“Hah!”
The instant Jeok Cheongang’s unmistakable shout rang out—
My rapidly sinking consciousness snapped awake.
Strength returned to my limp body.
Memories of reality came back to me.
Who I was.
Where I was.
And...
What I had to do for everyone who had believed in me, a callow, inadequate brat.
*Endure.
And keep enduring.*
With all my strength, I bore the pain that kept tearing through my body.
I mustered the Scorching Yang Qi within the fire dragon and the Heavenly Power Demon’s energy I’d just absorbed.
Drawing on every last scrap of strength, I bit into the pillar of lightning.
*Crunch.
Crunch.*
Lightning flashed before my eyes.
It held everything that giant had been, and now it was numbing my mind beyond the point of pain.
Luckily for me.
*Fuck, it’s not like I’ve never shit blood before.*
At some point, I started laughing like a madman.
I bit into the lightning, swallowed it, and kept going without pause, even as I nearly blacked out from the pain I’d known was coming.
Until the distant flash that had filled my vision slowly dimmed.
Until at last it vanished completely, as though it had never existed.
*Rumble.*
Suddenly, through my hazy consciousness, I realized:
The massive bolt of lightning that had connected my Middle and Lower Dantians was gone.
The thunder I could hear from somewhere was ringing out inside me.
*I did it...*
The moment I understood that Transmitting Internal Energy Across the Body had succeeded—
*Ding.
Ding.
Ding-ding-ding!*
Clear chimes began ringing without pause, somewhere far off in my consciousness.
But the sound hadn’t come from the ocean of the Lower Dantian, now far in the distance, or from the peak of the Middle Dantian, finally glowing like a brilliant jewel.
I raised my head and saw it.
Clouds beyond the mountain peak’s reach.
Another world hidden behind them.
*The upper dantian.*
I was thirsty.
With my goal achieved, my consciousness, which had nearly unraveled to a thread, began to grow clearer.
It was thirst.
Longing.
*More, more, more...!*
I wanted to grow stronger.
I wanted to go farther.
I wanted to break through those white clouds, soar above them, and look down on everything.
But I had to force down that burning thirst and longing.
I was already at my limit.
Any more would be greed.
I knew what this momentary impulse would bring.
*Next time.
I swear.*
With that vow, I looked down over the mountain and ocean that had become wholly mine.
For the first time, I faced the essence within the three currents of energy, now united, and the vast power they formed.
No—I became one with it.
*Ah.
Ahhh.*
I shuddered and groaned.
I floundered in my fading consciousness.
Enveloped in a dazzling radiance where three lights mingled, I forgot everything around me.
No-self.
As I sank into that endless swamp of consciousness, I heard a voice like a hallucination.
“Good judgment.
Just like back then.”
The voice felt unfamiliar, yet somehow familiar, as though I’d heard it before.
Then the thread of my consciousness snapped.

paragraphs: At some point, the Thunderbolt Saber King, Peng Cheolhu, had begun to laugh without a sound.

Even as the several sixty-year cycles’ worth of internal energy he’d accumulated, along with every ounce of strength in his body, melted away and vanished, the clear smile at the corners of his wrinkled mouth remained.
Just like the brilliant halo of light still brightening his view in this very moment.
*Whoooosh.*
The wind howled.
An energy unlike anything seen before swelled within it. Three lights, each a different color, drew together and mingled without pause.
And at last, they changed.
*Whoosh!*
The air turned searing hot. Through it, the Thunderbolt Saber King saw three radiant flower buds bloom.
No—what he saw was a young man seated cross-legged, slowly rising into the air.
*Yes. I suppose so.*
He was witnessing Three Flowers Gather at the Crown, the realm every martial artist in Murim dreamed of reaching. But he wasn’t surprised.
He’d walked this path himself once. And it was someone else’s present.
The Blazing Flame Divine Dragon, Jin Taekyung.
Heir to the Fire Gate Clan and successor to the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang.
The Thunderbolt Saber King knew. He believed it, too.
For that callow brat, who’d only passed twenty two years ago, the realm of Three Flowers Gather at the Crown was nothing more than a step on the way to a greater height.
Even now, Jin Taekyung was moving toward the next step.
Before long, the Thunderbolt Saber King saw that belief become reality.
*Fwoosh.*
The three flower buds suddenly caught fire.
After a fierce struggle, the Extreme Yang flames swallowed the pitch-black energy. The moment five rings formed, the Thunderbolt Saber King gave a quiet laugh.
*Beyond Three Flowers Gather at the Crown... Five Qi Returning to Origin.*
Jin Taekyung probably didn’t know exactly what those five rings meant.
But the Thunderbolt Saber King did.
No, every martial artist under Heaven knew. To set foot in the realm of Five Qi Returning to Origin was to meet the bare minimum qualification for being called a king across the vast Nine Provinces.
But the transformation didn’t end there.
*Crackle!*
Flame and lightning intertwined.
The struggle between the hellfire that had swallowed the darkness and the thunderbolt was fierce, desperate enough to leave Jin Taekyung trembling with pain as he floated in the air.
A tremendous reverberation burst from his body and spread in every direction, far beyond the pavilion.
“Hah!”
At Jeok Cheongang’s sudden shout, Jin Taekyung’s violent trembling slowly began to subside.
His face, contorted like a fiend’s by the terrible pain, took on a new expression.
Will.
It was Will: a fierce resolve to break rather than yield, to get past this wall and reach higher still.
When the Thunderbolt Saber King felt Jin Taekyung’s Will, he was finally certain.
*I made the right choice.*
A smile brighter than any before spread across his face.

He watched the internal energy he’d spent a lifetime accumulating—those long years, and the little life he had left—melt into the flames. Then he spoke, making his voice gruff despite everything he felt.
“Damn it. I’ve done nothing but good things for the Fire Gate Clan before I go.”
The old master gazed at his Disciple, enveloped in the energy that had finally become one amid the distant blaze of light, and answered.
“If you’re so sore about it, you should’ve had more kids. If you’d tried a little harder, maybe the Peng Family would’ve had a brat like him.”
“Would you listen to this senile old man? You took a monster for a Disciple by pure luck, and now you’re saying whatever you please.”
“That’s right. I was lucky.”
“Damn it. Don’t admit it!”
“Why not?”
“Because if you admit it that easily, I’ve got nothing to say.”
The Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, and the Thunderbolt Saber King, Peng Cheolhu, looked at each other and chuckled.
“Remember that time?”
“What time?”
“Just after the Great Faction War ended, I think. When we all got together for a drink to celebrate.”
“Oh, the day you mouthed off to this old man and got a bloody nose?”
The Thunderbolt Saber King frowned.
“Get it straight. We were evenly matched until then.”
“We were. For about thirty exchanges. Then you got beaten. I was clearly a cut above.”
“...Childish to the very end. There’s a reason they say people never change.”
“If a man changes, it means he’s about to die. Anyway, it was my complete victory.”
“You insufferable old bastard. Did you eat all those years through your asshole?”
Fifty years ago, they would surely have been throwing punches at each other by now.
Instead, the two old men kept smiling.
One was doing his best to hide the bitterness rising from deep within him. The other had accepted both the years long gone and the death drawing near.
Jeok Cheongang looked at Peng Cheolhu, whose hair had turned completely white, and made a show of scowling.
“You ill-mannered brat. I told you, if you’re going to treat me like an old man, you ought to count our years properly and show me the respect I’m due.”
“Damn it. The age thing again.”
“I’ve told you hundreds of times. Is your skull made of Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron? Is that why you can’t remember?”
“Enough of what I don’t want to hear. Fine, I understand. I’ll show you respect, all right?”
“Peng Family bastards, honestly... What did you just say?”
Jeok Cheongang stopped mid-sentence. At his startled expression, the Thunderbolt Saber King let out a hearty laugh.
“What’s the matter? Have you gotten so old you’ve gone deaf, Jeok hyung?”
“Tsk, tsk. What’s the point of looking young again? All those years, and nothing to show for them.”
Jeok Cheongang stared at him in silence as he clicked his tongue loudly enough to be heard. Then, all at once, he laughed aloud.
“What are you laughing at?”
“Nothing. I just lived long enough to see this day. Have you got a problem with that?”
“I always have a problem with something. But can a younger brother talk back to his hyung?”
*Younger brother.*
Why did those two simple words stir something in Jeok Cheongang’s chest? He forced his fading smile back onto his lips.
“You’ve finally come to your senses. I wondered how long you’d keep digging in your heels.”
“Now, now. Is that any way to speak to your younger brother? It seems Jeok hyung still hasn’t come to his senses.”
“Then shall I call you Peng, my younger brother, from now on?”
This time, the Thunderbolt Saber King laughed aloud. His face, covered in fine wrinkles and age spots after he’d given away everything he had, creased deeply.
“No. Better not. Hearing you say that makes me itch right down to my guts.”
“You damnable bastard. What do I have to do to satisfy you?”
“That’s much better. You’ve finally turned back into the Fire King Jeok Cheongang I know.”
At last, the Thunderbolt Saber King smiled in satisfaction. When he spoke again, his voice was gentle.
“Jeok hyung.”
Jeok Cheongang didn’t answer.
No—he couldn’t.

The sudden change in the Thunderbolt Saber King’s tone and expression, the voice that now sounded unmistakably like an old man’s—something about it lodged in Jeok Cheongang’s throat and left him speechless.
The Thunderbolt Saber King looked at him as if he understood and went on.
“You, at least... don’t change, Jeok hyung.”
“Stay in Murim as you are, just as you always have.”
So many years had passed.
The sun and moon kept changing places. The mountains and rivers changed their clothes in turn, and those born into this world with vigorous cries returned to the soil.
Yet some had not changed.
Their bodies had aged with the years, but their hearts remained steadfast.
“Looking back, I’ve been very lucky.”
Years flashed like meteors through the Thunderbolt Saber King’s fading eyes.
He had been born into the Hebei Peng Family, a power that commanded its region, and spent a childhood wanting for nothing.
In his youth, his name had spread beyond the northern lands and across the world.
And then—
“Even in that terrible war, I had friends I could fight back to back with.”
“...Yes. You did. You still do.”
Jeok Cheongang’s voice was dry. He quietly bit his lip. He was no longer smiling.
“Jeok hyung.”
“Go on. I’m listening.”
“Do you remember what I used to say all the time?”
Jeok Cheongang nodded without hesitation.
“That a man should meet his death proudly on the battlefield.”
“You remembered.”
“How could I forget? You said it several times a day.”
“I did. And every time, you threatened to rip my mouth open.”
The Thunderbolt Saber King laughed happily at the old memory. But instead of the thunderous laughter that had once boomed from him, only a faint breath came out.
“I take it back. Now that I’ve come this far... this kind of death isn’t so bad after all.”
His head kept drooping. He forced it up, straightened his bent back, and looked over Jeok Cheongang’s shoulder.
At the figure floating there, engulfed in deep light.
*Crack. Creak.*

The sound of flesh tearing came from Jin Taekyung’s body as fine tremors spread through it. The Thunderbolt Saber King watched with joy in his eyes as Jin Taekyung entered Bone Transformation—a process he himself had never experienced.
*Supreme Peak.*
He had climbed the summit and reached the utmost height: the highest place on earth, and the path closest to Heaven.
“Jeok hyung. Do you see him?”
At the Thunderbolt Saber King’s voice, trembling with emotion, Jeok Cheongang turned to look at his Disciple.
“Yes. I see him. My one and only Disciple—and the successor who inherited everything you had.”
“Is that so?”
Death had already dimmed the Thunderbolt Saber King’s eyes. He could no longer see Jeok Cheongang’s face or Jin Taekyung’s form.
And yet, in the darkness slowly approaching, he saw a radiant halo of light that would not go out.
“Th-that child...”
He struggled for breath.
Clinging to his fading consciousness, he reached toward the light shining beyond the darkness.
Toward the future he had left behind. Toward hope.
Then he cast off everything pressing down on his body and lunged toward the light.
Toward a new mountain peak that didn’t exist in this world, waiting for him.
Toward another Supreme Peak: death.
*Tap.*
His fingertips fell limply, touching nothing.
Jeok Cheongang quietly closed his eyes. A low voice slipped between his lips.
“Farewell, you Peng bastard.”
He would save the words *younger brother* for the day they met again.
That was his last promise to the Thunderbolt Saber King—no, to Peng Cheolhu.
And as the Fire King Jeok Cheongang, rather than Jeok hyung, he still had far too much left to do.
*Whoosh.*
Feeling the halo of light finally begin to fade, Jeok Cheongang opened his eyes.

chapters.title: Chapter 989
paragraphs: The Thousand-Faced Fox, Song Ho, was having another day so busy he couldn’t catch his breath.
Or, more accurately, he was supposed to be.
When he rose after less than two hours of sleep, he already had his day planned out in fifteen-minute increments.
But the moment he read the red missive brought by a Hidden Shadow Pavilion agent before sunrise, the Thousand-Faced Fox realized one thing:
Today would not go according to plan.
“Cancel the meeting already on the schedule. Instead, summon the Inner Hall’s officers within fifteen minutes.”
“I’ll make sure every one of them is notified.”
“What’s the situation in the Outer Hall?”
“They’re already on alert. The messenger eagles bound for each province are ready and waiting for your orders, Pavilion Master—”
“Send them out at once. I’ll see the Alliance Leader in the meantime.”
After giving several more orders, the Thousand-Faced Fox hurried toward his destination.
As always, Sword Saint Mae Jonghak was waiting for him, seated cross-legged.
“It’s early for bad news. You could’ve waited until sunrise, at least.”
His voice and gaze were as clear as the water at a lakeshore.
Usually, the Number One Sword Under Heaven’s composure made him seem utterly carefree. Faced with it now, the Thousand-Faced Fox spoke cautiously.
“Did you already... know?”
“I can’t say I know. I just found it hard to sleep last night.”
Mae Jonghak slowly opened his eyes and looked at the Thousand-Faced Fox.
Or, more precisely, at the red missive in his hand.
“So. Who is it this time?”
Mae Jonghak’s voice had sunk low.
Many years had passed, and much had changed. But some things remained the same.
Red missives bearing tragic news were one of them.
During the Great Faction War, whenever an important figure died or heavy casualties were reported, they had written those missives with heavy hearts.
Just like the one in the Thousand-Faced Fox’s hand now.
“Alliance Leader.”
“It’s all right. Tell me the name written in that red missive.”
The Thousand-Faced Fox hesitated, then spoke somberly.
“The Thunderbolt Saber King, who was staying with the Jin Family of Taiyuan, has finally...”
“Enough. That will do.”
Mae Jonghak waved a hand, his expression bitter.
“So it came to this, after all.”
“I’m sorry to bring you such news.”
“You? No. If someone must be blamed, it should be me—the Alliance Leader.”
The Thousand-Faced Fox bowed his head without a word.

The two men had known each other for decades: first as promising young martial artists of the Nine Sects and One Gang and the Five Great Families, then as comrades who had joined forces to weather the war.
For now, he needed to give Mae Jonghak time to receive the news as the dead man’s friend, not as the Alliance Leader. Fortunately, the silence did not last long.
“How did Senior Peng pass?”
“They say he was smiling until the end. He knew he had little time left, so he passed on everything he had through Transmitting Internal Energy Across the Body.”
The astonishing news left out one crucial detail: to whom.
But Mae Jonghak didn’t need to ask. Before the Thousand-Faced Fox had finished speaking, a name had already come to mind.
“Jin Taekyung. It must have been that boy.”
“Yes. It was an extremely dangerous attempt, but I’m told the technique succeeded.”
Mae Jonghak nodded quietly.
Though he’d spent only a short time with Jin Taekyung, he’d had a vague sense that the transfer would succeed.
“That boy could certainly pull it off. There’s no telling how deep his abilities run.”
The Thousand-Faced Fox’s next report, however, drew a disbelieving laugh even from Mae Jonghak.
“Bone Transformation?”
The Heavenly Martial Physique was something one was born with. Bone Transformation, by contrast, completely rebuilt the body through immense internal energy and enlightenment.
Even a white-haired old man on the verge of death could regain his youth and make remarkable gains in martial arts through Bone Transformation.
And yet that fortune, coveted by all, had come to a young man around twenty.
Even the Thousand-Faced Fox, who had read the report with his own eyes, plainly struggled to believe it.
“Is this truly... possible?”
“You don’t seem convinced.”
“I doubt most people would be.”
“Why do you think it’s impossible?”
“In the entire thousand-year history of Murim, how many have experienced Bone Transformation? As far as I know, fewer than twenty.”
“You have a point. But there’s something you’re overlooking.”
“What is it?”
Mae Jonghak spread one hand instead of answering.
“Five.”
“What does that—”
“Of those fewer than twenty, five have appeared in this age alone.”
“No—now there’ll be six.”
The Martial God and the Three Saints.
The Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, and his Disciple, the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon, Jin Taekyung.
Mae Jonghak raised another finger as he named them, then continued calmly.
“Isn’t it strange? Only around twenty people have undergone Bone Transformation in the last thousand years, yet the orthodox Murim alone already has six.”
“That’s...”
“You’ve felt it yourself, I’m sure. You just can’t easily accept it out loud.”
Mae Jonghak uncrossed his legs and stood.
He looked so ordinary that the Thousand-Faced Fox might have passed him anywhere without a second glance. But the eyes meeting his were clear as glass.
“We live in a truly strange age. The boundaries of common sense collapsed long ago, and a vast, unimaginable shadow has fallen over the world.”
More than fifty years ago, two supreme figures had appeared in the same age: the Martial God and the Heavenly Demon.
And that was hardly all.
Dozens of Supreme Peak masters from the orthodox, unorthodox, and Demonic factions had gathered around them, and a battle had begun between superhumans wielding unprecedented power.
The Three Saints and the Ten Kings. Great fiends of the Demonic Cult and the unorthodox faction, with power enough to shake heaven and earth.
And...
“Now Dark Heaven has appeared, surpassing even the Demonic Cult of that era by far.”
Does the age make the people, or do the people make the age?
The question had inspired countless debates, but no one had found a clear answer. Sword Saint Mae Jonghak was no exception.
Yet deep down, he knew the age he lived in was more than a mere time of chaos.
He sensed something hidden behind the conflict between superhumans—whether they had been born of this chaotic age or were bringing it into being.
“Supernatural powers we cannot understand. Monsters in horrific forms. And at the center of it all, someone called the Lord of Heaven.”
His gaze deepened as he murmured, almost to himself.
“Sometimes I wonder if all of this is a scheme devised by someone beyond our imagining.”
Mae Jonghak suddenly turned to look out the window.
White snowflakes drifted slowly down, so thick they obscured the sunlight spreading from the distant east.
Snow in early autumn. A tremendous snowfall, at that.
In Henan’s warm climate, such a thing was not merely rare—it had been unheard of. Yet it had begun happening several months ago.
And not only in Henan. It was happening across the world.
The changes were not confined to the ground, either.
The sky that had always hung above them—the heavenly patterns whose change Dharma King Hong Dao had long ago foreseen—was changing rapidly.
“Can you make sense of any of this?”
At Mae Jonghak’s question, the Thousand-Faced Fox, Song Ho, bit his lip without a word.
Cold sweat had soaked his back.
“I—I can’t. I can’t even begin to guess what’s about to happen.”
His voice trembled.

Even a man who had served the Martial God at close quarters and fought the hundred thousand followers of the Demonic Path led by the Heavenly Demon could not stay calm when he thought of what lay ahead.
It was as though...
*Something beyond the bounds of the human world.*
The words hovered on the tip of his tongue. The Thousand-Faced Fox could not bring himself to say them, so he swallowed them instead.
He couldn’t believe it.
No—he didn’t want to believe it.
Mae Jonghak watched the Thousand-Faced Fox’s agitation with clear eyes.
“Pavilion Master Song. May I say one thing to you as your superior and the Alliance Leader?”
“Please.”
“Admit that you’re afraid. Accept it.”
“Be more afraid than anyone else. Always be on guard against our enemies and distrust them. You and I have no choice. We’re in positions where we have to.”
The Thousand-Faced Fox understood the meaning behind Mae Jonghak’s words at once.
“I’ll take your words to heart, Alliance Leader.”
“Thank you. You’re a coolheaded, intelligent man. One of the most... no, not *the* most, but certainly among the ten most intelligent people I’ve known.”
The Thousand-Faced Fox let out a dry chuckle.
“So there are quite a few ahead of me.”
“I have to get the numbers right. Try not to be offended.”
“I won’t take that part to heart.”
“Good news. You already have more than enough pressing matters on your mind.”
“Of course. Then I’ll take my leave.”
Mae Jonghak smiled faintly but did not stop the Thousand-Faced Fox as he hurried away, moving as briskly as he had when he arrived.
Once he was alone, Mae Jonghak slowly read the red missive left behind. Then he murmured under his breath.
“So I’m saying goodbye to someone again.”
Beyond their friendship, the Thunderbolt Saber King’s death was a tremendous loss to the orthodox Murim as a whole.
Half of the Ten Kings had fallen over the long years. Of the five who remained, another was gone.
Perhaps the trace left by that giant’s final step could ease the grief of his passing, if only a little.
“The Blazing Flame Divine Dragon, Jin Taekyung.”
Mae Jonghak quietly spoke the name that had lingered in his mind.
A great star, the Thunderbolt Saber King, had fallen, and a new star had risen to fill the void.
No—he had already been shining brightly before this.
As if to prove his title, Divine Dragon.
*Before long, two dragons will finally ascend to the heavens.*
Mae Jonghak did not doubt it for a moment.
Jin Taekyung, now a giant of Murim, and the last successor Mae Jonghak had raised like his own grandson would stand at the center of this strange age.
Thinking of Cheongpung, who must by now have finally heard the news from Shanxi Province even where he was so far away, Mae Jonghak poured internal energy into the missive in his hand.
*Fwoosh. Crackle.*
The flames of Samadhi True Fire tinted Mae Jonghak’s clear eyes red.

chapters.title: Chapter 990
paragraphs: The Thunderbolt Saber King, Peng Cheolhu.
News that the Grand Family Head of the Hebei Peng Family—yet another giant born of the Great Faction War—had fallen spread like a raging wildfire.
“I thought he, at least, would hold firm... And yet it’s come to this.”
“Even so, who could’ve imagined the Saber King would meet such a pointless end?”
“Pointless? Don’t ever say that in front of me again. Great Hero Peng held fast to his chivalrous spirit until the very end.”
“Enough. You think he said that because he didn’t know? He’s just heartbroken.”
“I know. Damn it, I know.”
The martial artists who received the unexpected and tragic news could not hide their grief.
To them, the title of one of the Ten Kings carried a meaning unlike any other.
Yet Hong Dao, the Dharma King who had earned everyone’s respect, was gone.
So was Tang Taesang, the Poison King who had struck fear into countless members of the Demonic Cult.
And now even the Thunderbolt Saber King—the man who, apart from the overwhelming presence of the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, had been all but the foremost of the Ten Kings—had met his death.
None of them had died of old age or illness.
“Don’t forget. They died honorably, fighting for what was right. Avenge them—that duty falls to us now.”
The old masters who had symbolized the orthodox Murim and stood for chivalry were dying one after another.
The martial artists of Murim layered anger over their grief.
To avenge those they had lost.
To defeat the new enemy, which had emerged for the first time since the Demonic Cult and revealed a power more threatening than ever.
“Who will stand against Dark Heaven!”
“Take up your swords! For the Nine Provinces, for justice and chivalry—rise up and fight those fiends!”
Rousing shouts rang out on streets everywhere. They had become an everyday occurrence.

Learning from the Murong Family’s example, Sect Leaders and Family Heads of various factions met often and put old grudges behind them. Young people, their blood burning with fervor, swung weapons they had never so much as bloodied until their palms split.
Even a stone leaves a mark when it moves. How much greater the mark left by a mountain?

The bloody battle fought across a narrow gorge in Shanxi Province—the incident that came to be known as the Eight Heavens Blood Calamity—and the death of the Thunderbolt Saber King had been the final sparks.

Dark Heaven had stirred up bloodshed across the land without ever revealing its full strength. Those who feared it now understood, as did the martial artists caught between the orthodox and unorthodox factions who had once been reluctant to oppose it.
The razor-sharp blade in Dark Heaven’s hand was aimed not only at the orthodox Murim, but at the entire world.
And the repercussions had long since spread far beyond Murim’s borders.
“So, who are you, and where are you from?”
“I’m Jang-pal, from Jeong Family Village.”
“Jang-pal? If you’re from Jeong Family Village, why is your surname Jang?”
“Pardon?”
“Why Jang-pal?”
“Oh, well...”
“Well, what?”
“My father’s from somewhere else.”
“Somewhere else, huh? So he married into the family and settled in Jeong Family Village.”
“Yes, yes. That’s right.”
“How old are you?”
“I turned twenty this year.”
The low-ranking official assigned to recruit soldiers looked the applicant up and down. Young man? The fellow standing before him ought to have been called a boy.
“Twenty?”
“Yes, sir!”
“I see. Then what is your mother’s full name?”
“What?”
“The more we talk, the more familiar you look. I might know your family. If I do, I could send you somewhere you’d have a good chance to earn military merit.”
At the official’s coaxing tone, the boy’s eyes lit up.
“Y-you really mean it?”
“Of course. So, what’s your mother’s name?”
The boy hesitated, but not for long.
He might not have his family’s permission, but his sense of chivalry and his dreams of making his mark on the world had never burned brighter.
If his parents were acquainted with the official in front of him, this was the perfect chance to be posted to a good battlefield, earn brilliant merit, and become a young general.
*Me too. I’ll be like him one day.*
He had already made up his mind.
Thinking of the idol he had never once seen in person, the boy found his courage. He gripped the bamboo spear he had clumsily whittled himself and opened his mouth.
“Th-the second daughter of the Oh family from the house by the persimmon tree. She said people nearby would know her...”
“Go home.”
“What?”
“Your father’s a Jeong, your mother’s an Oh, so why do you live in Jeong Family Village?”
“What, still got something to say?”
The official glared at him as though he already knew everything. The boy stiffened, then barely managed to force out a reply.
“Actually, my whole family came from somewhere else...”
“What are you waiting for? Drag this brat out!”
“Gah, sir! No! You can’t! You’ll really regret turning me away!”
The boy’s eyes widened with fierce determination. Deeply moved by the sight, the official gave an order to the guards holding him by both arms.
“Give him three swats on the rear and toss him out. Twenty, my ass. You little brat—first you lie, and then you glare at an adult?”
“Siiir!”
His desperate cries changed nothing.

Ever since the Emperor’s proclamation had spread throughout the land, government offices in every province had been packed with people who couldn’t contain their dreams of making a name for themselves or the hot blood in their veins.
The official was in danger of dying from overwork before Dark Heaven ever got to him. He’d had his fill of boys lying about their age to enlist.
“Give him two more!”
“Nooo!”
“Yes!”

In the end, the guards gave the boy a sound kick to the rear and drove him out. The applicants, whose line stretched all the way outside the government office, watched him go and murmured among themselves.
“He looks younger than my little brother.”
“Still, the kid’s got spirit. Shame his head’s a complete rock.”
“But where did he say he was from again?”
“Doesn’t matter. He obviously made it up.”
“No, I still need to know.”
“Why are you so hung up on it?”
“I made mine up too.”
“I can’t have the place name overlapping by accident. They’ll catch me, and I’ll end up like him.”
“...How old are you, by the way?”
“Sixteen.”
“Cut the crap. You’ve got the face of a grizzled veteran.”
“Thank you, hyung. Looks like I’ll get through just fine. And please keep this a secret.”
“...Wait, you weren’t joking?”
While everyone else was still reeling, the applicant with the weathered face called to the boy as he staggered to his feet.
“How old are you?”
The boy, staring blankly at the government office, answered.
“Sixteen.”
“Same as me. Since we’ve met, let’s drop the formalities.”
“Not even a stray dog would believe that. I’m in a lousy enough mood already.”
“I’m serious.”
“I’m not falling for... it, sir.”
“Anyway, where’d you get that spear?”
The boy fidgeted before answering.
“I whittled it myself...”
“Don’t people our age usually use swords? Like me.”
The boy’s face twisted at once.
“Who says that? The spear is the king of all weapons.”
“There, you’re talking to me normally now. And I never said swords were the best. I just said most people use them.”
“Oh.”
“Seeing you get worked up over weapons tells me one thing. You came here because you want to be like ‘that person,’ didn’t you?”
The boy hesitated, then answered in a much softer voice.
“Show him some respect.”
“What?”
“Don’t call him ‘that person.’ Speak of him with respect.”
His dejected look had vanished.
As if nothing had happened, he seemed to have forgotten he’d just been thrown out of the government office. His eyes brightened as he continued.
“Blazing Flame Divine Dragon Jin Taekyung. I’m going to be like him. I will!”
Everyone had a goal they wanted to reach.
For the boy, Jin Taekyung was that goal.
A young hero of the martial world, watched by the entire land, and a noble marquis personally appointed by the Son of Heaven.
He admired him. Respected him.
When he’d strode here so confidently, he’d been full of ambition. Before long, he’d thought, he would stand shoulder to shoulder with Jin Taekyung.
Reality, of course, had kicked him in the rear and thrown him out.
“Damn it.”
The boy lowered his head gloomily.
Then a strange voice suddenly rang out from somewhere.
“Wow! That’s so cool!”
The boy looked up and blinked at the speaker. Everyone waiting outside the government office did the same.
*Who’s that?*
*When did he show up? I don’t think he was here a moment ago.*
*Huh. Or was he?*
*Now that I think about it, maybe he was here the whole time...*
They exchanged bewildered glances. But before anyone could make sense of it, the young man who had suddenly appeared before them was smiling brightly at the boy.
“My grandpa told me— No, someone told me it’s good to have a goal you want to achieve!”
“Y-yes?”
The boy stared at the young man, bewildered.
Perhaps it was the long robe caked in dust. The young man looked more than ordinary—he looked downright shabby.
Maybe that was why the shock of his sudden appearance and his attempt to strike up a conversation soon gave way to an inexplicable sense of familiarity. The boy felt it, and so did everyone else.
It was like... like...
Right.
*That one slow older guy every neighborhood seems to have.*
For once, everyone was thinking the same thing. How could they not?
Just look at that spotless, pure-white smile.
There wasn’t a speck of malice in his eyes. They were clearer than a stream, and then he grabbed the boy’s hand and shook it over and over—the way a little kid might.
“That’s so cool! You’re determined to become like the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon. That’s amazing!”
With both hands trapped in the young man’s grip, the wide-eyed boy finally came back to his senses when his shoulders began to ache.
“P-please let go.”
“Oh, sorry. I got excited. Did I hurt you?”
You couldn’t spit in a smiling face. Seeing how genuinely worried the young man looked, the boy couldn’t bring himself to complain.
“...No, I’m fine. But who exactly are you?”
“Just a passing hero who wants to save the world, like you, Young Hero!”
He puffed out his chest and declared it proudly. The boy and everyone else reached the same conclusion.
*Yep. Definitely slow.*
And, proving their suspicions, the young man kept babbling about whatever came to mind, oblivious to the strange atmosphere.
“But, Young Hero, if you want to become like the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon, why come to the government office? Wouldn’t it be better to go straight to the Jin Family of Taiyuan?”
“Oh, it’s just so far away. I’ve never been more than a hundred li from home in my life. How could I...?”
“It’s far, but not *that* far.”
“Not that far? From here in Qinghai to Shanxi?”
“It goes by faster than you’d think. As long as you keep running hard and don’t give up.”
Snickers broke out around them.

The trip would be grueling and mind-numbingly dull.
If even people who made their living on the road felt that way, what about those who lived in Qinghai, on the far western edge of the realm?
It was the sort of nonsense only a fool would say.
But to a boy whose own impossible dream had drawn laughter, the young man’s words sounded different.
“Just keep at it and don’t give up?”
“Right! And even if the Jin Family of Taiyuan is too far away, there are other options. For example...”
“Do you mean the Kunlun Sect?”
“Oh, you know about it?”
“Yes. I’m from around here, of course I do. And I know I’m too old to join the Kunlun Sect.”
The boy sighed deeply before going on.
“But I don’t want to join the Black Dragon Demon Gate. I know it belongs to the Murim Alliance, but its roots are still in the unorthodox faction. There are some unpleasant rumors about it, too.”
“Hmm. What about the other sects...?”

“The details are different, but it’s much the same with them. I’d rather join the military, learn strategy, and someday become a general leading an army. That might bring me a little closer to his fame.”
After pouring all that out, the boy gave a self-mocking laugh.
What was the point of telling a complete stranger—one who seemed none too bright—all this?
“I should go. Maybe I’ll see you again sometime.”
“Hey, wait.”
The boy kept trudging off despite the young man calling after him.
As the young man watched him go with a dejected expression, a round face popped up beside him.
“Hyung, what are you doing here? I’ve been looking all over for you.”

“Sorry. I was only going to be gone for a little while.”

“I had a reason.”
“Then tell me.”

“Hehe. Did I ever tell you? When my Benefactor first saw me, the candied hawthorn skewers—”
“Shut up. Please.”

sentences.text: The Thunderbolt Saber King, Peng Cheolhu.
News that the Grand Family Head of the Hebei Peng Family—yet another giant born of the Great Faction War—had fallen spread like a raging wildfire.
“I thought he, at least, would hold firm...
And yet it’s come to this.”
“Even so, who could’ve imagined the Saber King would meet such a pointless end?”
“Pointless?
Don’t ever say that in front of me again.
Great Hero Peng held fast to his chivalrous spirit until the very end.”
“Enough.
You think he said that because he didn’t know?
He’s just heartbroken.”
“I know.
Damn it, I know.”
The martial artists who received the unexpected and tragic news could not hide their grief.
To them, the title of one of the Ten Kings carried a meaning unlike any other.
Yet Hong Dao, the Dharma King who had earned everyone’s respect, was gone.
So was Tang Taesang, the Poison King who had struck fear into countless members of the Demonic Cult.
And now even the Thunderbolt Saber King—the man who, apart from the overwhelming presence of the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, had been all but the foremost of the Ten Kings—had met his death.
None of them had died of old age or illness.
“Don’t forget.
They died honorably, fighting for what was right.
Avenge them—that duty falls to us now.”
The old masters who had symbolized the orthodox Murim and stood for chivalry were dying one after another.
The martial artists of Murim layered anger over their grief.
To avenge those they had lost.
To defeat the new enemy, which had emerged for the first time since the Demonic Cult and revealed a power more threatening than ever.
“Who will stand against Dark Heaven!”
“Take up your swords!
For the Nine Provinces, for justice and chivalry—rise up and fight those fiends!”
Rousing shouts rang out on streets everywhere.
They had become an everyday occurrence.
Learning from the Murong Family’s example, Sect Leaders and Family Heads of various factions met often and put old grudges behind them.
Young people, their blood burning with fervor, swung weapons they had never so much as bloodied until their palms split.
Even a stone leaves a mark when it moves.
How much greater the mark left by a mountain?

The bloody battle fought across a narrow gorge in Shanxi Province—the incident that came to be known as the Eight Heavens Blood Calamity—and the death of the Thunderbolt Saber King had been the final sparks.
Dark Heaven had stirred up bloodshed across the land without ever revealing its full strength.
Those who feared it now understood, as did the martial artists caught between the orthodox and unorthodox factions who had once been reluctant to oppose it.
The razor-sharp blade in Dark Heaven’s hand was aimed not only at the orthodox Murim, but at the entire world.
And the repercussions had long since spread far beyond Murim’s borders.
“So, who are you, and where are you from?”
“I’m Jang-pal, from Jeong Family Village.”
“Jang-pal?
If you’re from Jeong Family Village, why is your surname Jang?”
“Pardon?”
“Why Jang-pal?”
“Oh, well...”
“Well, what?”
“My father’s from somewhere else.”
“Somewhere else, huh?
So he married into the family and settled in Jeong Family Village.”
“Yes, yes.
That’s right.”
“How old are you?”
“I turned twenty this year.”
The low-ranking official assigned to recruit soldiers looked the applicant up and down.
Young man?
The fellow standing before him ought to have been called a boy.
“Twenty?”
“Yes, sir!”
“I see.
Then what is your mother’s full name?”
“What?”
“The more we talk, the more familiar you look.
I might know your family.
If I do, I could send you somewhere you’d have a good chance to earn military merit.”
At the official’s coaxing tone, the boy’s eyes lit up.
“Y-you really mean it?”
“Of course.
So, what’s your mother’s name?”
The boy hesitated, but not for long.
He might not have his family’s permission, but his sense of chivalry and his dreams of making his mark on the world had never burned brighter.
If his parents were acquainted with the official in front of him, this was the perfect chance to be posted to a good battlefield, earn brilliant merit, and become a young general.
*Me too.
I’ll be like him one day.*
He had already made up his mind.
Thinking of the idol he had never once seen in person, the boy found his courage.
He gripped the bamboo spear he had clumsily whittled himself and opened his mouth.
“Th-the second daughter of the Oh family from the house by the persimmon tree.
She said people nearby would know her...”
“Go home.”
“What?”
“Your father’s a Jeong, your mother’s an Oh, so why do you live in Jeong Family Village?”
“What, still got something to say?”
The official glared at him as though he already knew everything.
The boy stiffened, then barely managed to force out a reply.
“Actually, my whole family came from somewhere else...”
“What are you waiting for?
Drag this brat out!”
“Gah, sir!
No!
You can’t!
You’ll really regret turning me away!”
The boy’s eyes widened with fierce determination.
Deeply moved by the sight, the official gave an order to the guards holding him by both arms.
“Give him three swats on the rear and toss him out.
Twenty, my ass.
You little brat—first you lie, and then you glare at an adult?”
“Siiir!”
His desperate cries changed nothing.

Ever since the Emperor’s proclamation had spread throughout the land, government offices in every province had been packed with people who couldn’t contain their dreams of making a name for themselves or the hot blood in their veins.
The official was in danger of dying from overwork before Dark Heaven ever got to him.
He’d had his fill of boys lying about their age to enlist.
“Give him two more!”
“Nooo!”
“Yes!”
In the end, the guards gave the boy a sound kick to the rear and drove him out.
The applicants, whose line stretched all the way outside the government office, watched him go and murmured among themselves.
“He looks younger than my little brother.”
“Still, the kid’s got spirit.
Shame his head’s a complete rock.”
“But where did he say he was from again?”
“Doesn’t matter.
He obviously made it up.”
“No, I still need to know.”
“Why are you so hung up on it?”
“I made mine up too.”
“I can’t have the place name overlapping by accident.
They’ll catch me, and I’ll end up like him.”
“...How old are you, by the way?”
“Sixteen.”
“Cut the crap.
You’ve got the face of a grizzled veteran.”
“Thank you, hyung.
Looks like I’ll get through just fine.
And please keep this a secret.”
“...Wait, you weren’t joking?”
While everyone else was still reeling, the applicant with the weathered face called to the boy as he staggered to his feet.
“How old are you?”
The boy, staring blankly at the government office, answered.
“Sixteen.”
“Same as me.
Since we’ve met, let’s drop the formalities.”
“Not even a stray dog would believe that.
I’m in a lousy enough mood already.”
“I’m serious.”
“I’m not falling for... it, sir.”
“Anyway, where’d you get that spear?”
The boy fidgeted before answering.
“I whittled it myself...”
“Don’t people our age usually use swords?
Like me.”
The boy’s face twisted at once.
“Who says that?
The spear is the king of all weapons.”
“There, you’re talking to me normally now.
And I never said swords were the best.
I just said most people use them.”
“Oh.”
“Seeing you get worked up over weapons tells me one thing.
You came here because you want to be like ‘that person,’ didn’t you?”
The boy hesitated, then answered in a much softer voice.
“Show him some respect.”
“What?”
“Don’t call him ‘that person.’ Speak of him with respect.”
His dejected look had vanished.
As if nothing had happened, he seemed to have forgotten he’d just been thrown out of the government office.
His eyes brightened as he continued.
“Blazing Flame Divine Dragon Jin Taekyung.
I’m going to be like him.
I will!”
Everyone had a goal they wanted to reach.
For the boy, Jin Taekyung was that goal.
A young hero of the martial world, watched by the entire land, and a noble marquis personally appointed by the Son of Heaven.
