chapters.title: Chapter 991
paragraphs: Whenever I lost consciousness or fell into a deep sleep, I found myself caught up in some kind of dream. It was nothing unusual anymore.
Someone once said dreams were a window into the mind. Worries I hadn’t managed to shake and memories that still lingered would mix together and surface as the illusion we called a dream.
Everything in this world had a cause or a reason. Dreams were no different.
Right.
That had to be true.
At least, as far as I knew.
But then why...
*Why am I having this dream?*
I blinked slowly. My vision was a blur.
Everything was hazy.
Unlike my other dreams, which had been horrifyingly vivid, I couldn’t even make out the illusions around me.
Then someone spoke, and I finally understood why I felt so groggy.
“Looks like you’re awfully sleepy, little guy.”
Sleepy.
As the realization sank in, I lifted my head.
No—*my head lifted* might be more accurate.
The blinking of my eyes, the movement of my head, even the voice slipping between my lips now—none of it was under my control.
“Yeah. I’m sleepy.”
The voice sounded muffled, as though I were underwater, but one thing was clear.
I was a child.
Young enough that hearing myself whine didn’t feel strange at all.
That answered one question, but another took its place.
Who was the unfamiliar man indulging the child’s whining?
*I’ve never heard his voice before.*
A voice wasn’t an ID card. I couldn’t expect to recognize someone the instant I heard him. Still, anyone who appeared in my dreams ought to be familiar to me.
But everything here was strange. The voice coming through the haze. The scene playing out slowly, like a TV screen full of static.
Then I heard the child speak again through lips that weren’t mine, and I understood where that strangeness came from.
“Dad. Can I go to sleep?”
If I’d been able to speak of my own accord, I would have groaned.
What I’d just realized was that startling—and that hard to understand.
*Dad?*
No. That couldn’t be.
I could turn the oldest drawer of my memories upside down and shake it, and I still wouldn’t find a memory like this.
The faint memory I had of my father’s voice sounded nothing like the man I was hearing now.
Which meant this was—
*Not my memory.*
Just then, an inexplicable chill ran down my spine.
Then the unfamiliar man the child had called Dad spoke close to my ear.
“Have a good dream, my son.”
A warm hand stroked my hair. His voice was gentle.
As my vision plunged into darkness, the man’s final word echoed faintly.
It was faint, but I’d heard it clearly.
A father speaking to his son. Calling him by name.
And at that moment, my thoughts ground to a halt with the shock of something I’d never expected.
*Fwoosh.*
Light poured down from beyond the pitch-black darkness, wrapping around the child lost in deep sleep.
No—around me.
If someone asked me what I usually saw first when I regained consciousness, I’d say the ceiling.
Or Hyuk Mujin, snoring in a corner under the pretense of standing guard. Or Jeok Cheongang’s face as he waited by my side for me to wake.
This time, it was none of those.
“Hah... hah...”
I sprang upright and gasped for breath.
Was this what it felt like to be on the verge of suffocating?
My newly regained vision wavered like melting candle wax. Voices from every direction thundered in my ears.
“Medicine King...! Come here! Hurry!”
“...tain, Captain!”
“What the hell...!”
Was I still dreaming? Or was this real?
I couldn’t tell. I kept batting away the hands reaching for me, acting on instinct through the confusion.
Then someone seized my shoulder.
Even in the middle of all that, I could feel the strength in that hand with perfect clarity.
It hurt a little, but an unfamiliar warmth came through that hand, too.
*Shaa...*
My rigid body slowly relaxed.
Only then did I realize whose energy was flowing along the acupoint pathways known to just two people in this vast world—the Extreme Yang qi flowing through me.
“...Old Master.”
I let the words out with the breath I’d been holding. A voice I knew all too well answered.
“Stay just as you are for a moment. Just a moment.”
I closed my eyes as Jeok Cheongang told me to.
I reminded myself that this place I was in was real, not an illusion, and slowly calmed my heart, which was pounding without pause.
How much time passed like that?
After a while, I opened my eyes to a world that was quiet and clear.
And to a familiar face watching me with concern.
“You fool. Are you finally coming around?”
I hesitated before answering his abrupt question.
“More or less.”
“So not quite.”
“Could you hit me hard once?”
“What?”
“Just once. Don’t hold back at all. Put your whole heart into it.”
“Please.”
At my solemn request, Jeok Cheongang sighed and raised his fist.
“Fine.”
*Whoosh.*
White flames sprang up around his tightly clenched fist.
As I watched him prepare to fire off a move from the Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist without further discussion, I spoke calmly.
“Wow, that’s hot.”
“What kind of nonsense is that? The Fire Gate Clan’s martial arts have always been hot.”
“If I can feel the heat, I think I’ve definitely come to my senses.”
Jeok Cheongang shook his head.
“Doesn’t look like it to me.”
“On second thought, I think I’m all right.”
“You said to put my whole heart into it.”
“Not to this extent.”
“Weren’t you the one who asked?”
“If you were going to take me *that* seriously, you should’ve refused three times first. Isn’t that only polite?”
“You lunatic. Do you think I’m Zhuge Cheongang? Quit flapping that mouth and brace yourself.”
Despite his words, Jeok Cheongang lowered his fist. He flicked his hand, and a water bottle on the bedside table shot toward me.
“What are you waiting for? Drink.”
“Thank you.”
I drained the full bottle without stopping for breath.
The cold water ran down my parched throat. At last, I felt like I could breathe again.
“Whew.”
“Well? Can you tell whether you’re dreaming or awake now?”
“More or less.”
At the same answer I’d given before, Jeok Cheongang clenched his fist again.
“And now?”
“...Wow, I’m awake! Definitely awake! The whole world is beautiful! I’m so happy to be alive!”
“Good. You’re finally back to the reckless little brat I know.”
“Was I not a moment ago?”
“Do you really have to ask? You woke up and immediately started thrashing around like you couldn’t tell up from down, so I sent everyone else out.”
“Hmm.”
Now that I thought about it, that did sound familiar.
I’d been overwhelmed with confusion and had instinctively fought off the hands trying to hold me.
Besides, the proof was right in front of me.
“What a mess.”
I muttered as I looked at the fragments scattered everywhere, their original forms lost. Jeok Cheongang nodded emphatically in agreement.
“A hell of a mess.”
“Did I do this, too?”
“Half right, half wrong.”
“What do you mean...?”
“Your eldest brother was the one who made a scene. Built like a mountain, bawling his eyes out and insisting he couldn’t leave. I had no choice but to deal with him myself.”
I stared at Jeok Cheongang, eyes wide.
“Did you kill him?”
“Want me to kill you first?”
“No. I’m joking.”
“I’m not.”
“Oh.”
A long time ago, I would’ve clutched my ass like it came with built-in dynamite and started counting down. Not anymore.
I gave a quiet laugh instead of answering. Jeok Cheongang clicked his tongue.
“Damn it. Now you really do think I’m worth less than dirt.”
“Come on, you’re sulking again. You know that’s not true.”
“Know what, my ass. More importantly... what caused this?”
The question came with a brief pause, his voice trailing off.
I opened my mouth, feeling the sweat that had soaked my back.
“It was just a dream.”
“What sort of nightmare?”
“No, it wasn’t exactly a nightmare... I don’t know. It was a strange dream. I can’t really describe it.”
Even as I answered, an odd feeling crept over me. I frowned.
*What is it?*
It felt strangely familiar.
But the sudden sense of déjà vu vanished when Jeok Cheongang spoke again, his voice grave.
“Tell me more. That nightmare could be a trace of the Heart Demon lurking inside you.”
I pushed aside my brief hesitation and answered.
“I don’t think so. It was a memory.”
“An unhappy memory can leave a trace of the Heart Demon, too. I’ve seen people trapped by their past until it destroyed them.”
I knew what Jeok Cheongang was worried about.
In modern terms, it was something like trauma.
For a Murim martial artist to break past their limits and reach the highest realms, powerful internal energy and martial arts weren’t enough.
They also needed the mental enlightenment gained through cultivating the mind.
Whether their path was good or evil, they had to reach an understanding of their own to keep walking it.
And for those who had begun that training, an unhealed illness of the mind could be devastating.
*Like Old Master suffering from the infirmities of old age after losing Jopil. No—Jangcheon.*
So Jeok Cheongang’s concern wasn’t an overreaction.
The world knew the Fire King Jeok Cheongang for a temper like hellfire. But inside him lay the caution and wisdom honed over many long years.
This time, though, I could answer him without hesitation.
“It’s not the Heart Demon.”
Jeok Cheongang’s expression hardened. I met his gaze and slowly continued.
“Because the memory I saw in the dream wasn’t mine to begin with.”
“What do you mean, it wasn’t yours?”
I swallowed a trembling breath.
And I remembered the man’s voice, faintly reaching the child as he fell into a deep sleep in that hazy dream.
No—the voice of another father.
“Have a good dream, my son... Taekyung.”
It was my memory, and at the same time, the memory of someone I could only call *you*.
Jin Taekyung, Third Young Master of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
The Shame of the Family, and the original owner of this body.

Still, anyone who appeared in my dreams ought to be familiar to me.
But everything here was strange.
The voice coming through the haze.
The scene playing out slowly, like a TV screen full of static.
Then I heard the child speak again through lips that weren’t mine, and I understood where that strangeness came from.
“Dad.
Can I go to sleep?”
If I’d been able to speak of my own accord, I would have groaned.
What I’d just realized was that startling—and that hard to understand.
*Dad?*
No.
That couldn’t be.
I could turn the oldest drawer of my memories upside down and shake it, and I still wouldn’t find a memory like this.
The faint memory I had of my father’s voice sounded nothing like the man I was hearing now.
Which meant this was—
*Not my memory.*
Just then, an inexplicable chill ran down my spine.
Then the unfamiliar man the child had called Dad spoke close to my ear.
“Have a good dream, my son.”
A warm hand stroked my hair.
His voice was gentle.
As my vision plunged into darkness, the man’s final word echoed faintly.
It was faint, but I’d heard it clearly.
A father speaking to his son.
Calling him by name.
And at that moment, my thoughts ground to a halt with the shock of something I’d never expected.
*Fwoosh.*
Light poured down from beyond the pitch-black darkness, wrapping around the child lost in deep sleep.
No—around me.
If someone asked me what I usually saw first when I regained consciousness, I’d say the ceiling.
Or Hyuk Mujin, snoring in a corner under the pretense of standing guard.
Or Jeok Cheongang’s face as he waited by my side for me to wake.
This time, it was none of those.
“Hah... hah...”
I sprang upright and gasped for breath.
Was this what it felt like to be on the verge of suffocating?
My newly regained vision wavered like melting candle wax.
Voices from every direction thundered in my ears.
“Medicine King...!
Come here!
Hurry!”
“...tain, Captain!”
“What the hell...!”
Was I still dreaming?
Or was this real?
I couldn’t tell.
I kept batting away the hands reaching for me, acting on instinct through the confusion.
Then someone seized my shoulder.
Even in the middle of all that, I could feel the strength in that hand with perfect clarity.
It hurt a little, but an unfamiliar warmth came through that hand, too.
*Shaa...*
My rigid body slowly relaxed.
Only then did I realize whose energy was flowing along the acupoint pathways known to just two people in this vast world—the Extreme Yang qi flowing through me.
“...Old Master.”
I let the words out with the breath I’d been holding.
A voice I knew all too well answered.
“Stay just as you are for a moment.
Just a moment.”
I closed my eyes as Jeok Cheongang told me to.
I reminded myself that this place I was in was real, not an illusion, and slowly calmed my heart, which was pounding without pause.
How much time passed like that?
After a while, I opened my eyes to a world that was quiet and clear.
And to a familiar face watching me with concern.
“You fool.
Are you finally coming around?”
I hesitated before answering his abrupt question.
“More or less.”
“So not quite.”
“Could you hit me hard once?”
“What?”
“Just once.
Don’t hold back at all.
Put your whole heart into it.”
“Please.”
At my solemn request, Jeok Cheongang sighed and raised his fist.
“Fine.”
*Whoosh.*
White flames sprang up around his tightly clenched fist.
As I watched him prepare to fire off a move from the Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist without further discussion, I spoke calmly.
“Wow, that’s hot.”
“What kind of nonsense is that?
The Fire Gate Clan’s martial arts have always been hot.”
“If I can feel the heat, I think I’ve definitely come to my senses.”
Jeok Cheongang shook his head.
“Doesn’t look like it to me.”
“On second thought, I think I’m all right.”
“You said to put my whole heart into it.”
“Not to this extent.”
“Weren’t you the one who asked?”
“If you were going to take me *that* seriously, you should’ve refused three times first.
Isn’t that only polite?”
“You lunatic.
Do you think I’m Zhuge Cheongang?
Quit flapping that mouth and brace yourself.”
Despite his words, Jeok Cheongang lowered his fist.
He flicked his hand, and a water bottle on the bedside table shot toward me.
“What are you waiting for?
Drink.”
“Thank you.”
I drained the full bottle without stopping for breath.
The cold water ran down my parched throat.
At last, I felt like I could breathe again.
“Whew.”
“Well?
Can you tell whether you’re dreaming or awake now?”
“More or less.”
At the same answer I’d given before, Jeok Cheongang clenched his fist again.
“And now?”
“...Wow, I’m awake!
Definitely awake!
The whole world is beautiful!
I’m so happy to be alive!”
“Good.
You’re finally back to the reckless little brat I know.”
“Was I not a moment ago?”
“Do you really have to ask?
You woke up and immediately started thrashing around like you couldn’t tell up from down, so I sent everyone else out.”
“Hmm.”
Now that I thought about it, that did sound familiar.
I’d been overwhelmed with confusion and had instinctively fought off the hands trying to hold me.
Besides, the proof was right in front of me.
“What a mess.”
I muttered as I looked at the fragments scattered everywhere, their original forms lost.
Jeok Cheongang nodded emphatically in agreement.
“A hell of a mess.”
“Did I do this, too?”
“Half right, half wrong.”
“What do you mean...?”
“Your eldest brother was the one who made a scene.
Built like a mountain, bawling his eyes out and insisting he couldn’t leave.
I had no choice but to deal with him myself.”
I stared at Jeok Cheongang, eyes wide.
“Did you kill him?”
“Want me to kill you first?”
“No.
I’m joking.”
“I’m not.”
“Oh.”
A long time ago, I would’ve clutched my ass like it came with built-in dynamite and started counting down.
Not anymore.
I gave a quiet laugh instead of answering.
Jeok Cheongang clicked his tongue.
“Damn it.
Now you really do think I’m worth less than dirt.”
“Come on, you’re sulking again.
You know that’s not true.”
“Know what, my ass.
More importantly... what caused this?”
The question came with a brief pause, his voice trailing off.
I opened my mouth, feeling the sweat that had soaked my back.
“It was just a dream.”
“What sort of nightmare?”
“No, it wasn’t exactly a nightmare...
I don’t know.
It was a strange dream.
I can’t really describe it.”
Even as I answered, an odd feeling crept over me.
I frowned.
*What is it?*
It felt strangely familiar.
But the sudden sense of déjà vu vanished when Jeok Cheongang spoke again, his voice grave.
“Tell me more.
That nightmare could be a trace of the Heart Demon lurking inside you.”
I pushed aside my brief hesitation and answered.
“I don’t think so.
It was a memory.”
“An unhappy memory can leave a trace of the Heart Demon, too.
I’ve seen people trapped by their past until it destroyed them.”
I knew what Jeok Cheongang was worried about.
In modern terms, it was something like trauma.
For a Murim martial artist to break past their limits and reach the highest realms, powerful internal energy and martial arts weren’t enough.
They also needed the mental enlightenment gained through cultivating the mind.
Whether their path was good or evil, they had to reach an understanding of their own to keep walking it.
And for those who had begun that training, an unhealed illness of the mind could be devastating.
*Like Old Master suffering from the infirmities of old age after losing Jopil.
No—Jangcheon.*
So Jeok Cheongang’s concern wasn’t an overreaction.
The world knew the Fire King Jeok Cheongang for a temper like hellfire.
But inside him lay the caution and wisdom honed over many long years.
This time, though, I could answer him without hesitation.
“It’s not the Heart Demon.”
Jeok Cheongang’s expression hardened.
I met his gaze and slowly continued.
“Because the memory I saw in the dream wasn’t mine to begin with.”
“What do you mean, it wasn’t yours?”
I swallowed a trembling breath.
And I remembered the man’s voice, faintly reaching the child as he fell into a deep sleep in that hazy dream.
No—the voice of another father.
“Have a good dream, my son...
Taekyung.”
It was my memory, and at the same time, the memory of someone I could only call *you*.
Jin Taekyung, Third Young Master of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
The Shame of the Family, and the original owner of this body.

chapters.title: Chapter 992
paragraphs: The fact that Jeok Cheongang was the only person left in the room was a huge relief.
He already knew the truth about me, and he hadn’t dismissed the words I’d spoken in a trembling voice as the ramblings of a lunatic.
“...So that was the last of it?”
“Yes. After I woke up, well, you know the rest, Old Master.”
Was it the shock of finally facing the truth?
Or had something actually changed inside me?
I didn’t know the exact reason, but I’d been left to flounder alone in a state of utter confusion.
No—maybe I still was.
“Damn it. That’s downright bizarre.”
Jeok Cheongang muttered the words like a groan, then studied me cautiously.
“What is it?”
“No, well... Has anything changed?”
“Changed? Of course.”
“What?”
He cried out in alarm.
Cold sweat still clung unpleasantly to my skin. Apart from that, I could feel power surging through my whole body.
“Well, my mood’s in the gutter, but I feel great physically.”
Jeok Cheongang swallowed.
“A-and?”
“That’s it.”
“...That’s all?”
“Yes.”
He gave me a flat look, then sighed.
“Fine. In a situation like this, that’s probably for the best.”
I agreed, though I kept it to myself. I felt awful, but nothing had actually happened to me.
The bigger problem was what this inexplicable phenomenon meant.
“Just to be safe, let me ask you something. Has anything like this ever happened before?”
“No. Not once, from the beginning until now.”
I answered firmly, then added, “That’s what makes it so strange. If this is a sign of something to come...”
“Don’t say that. Words have a way of coming true. Keep that rotten-luck talk to yourself.”
“Seeds can sprout without anyone watering them. It’s a hundred times better to predict what we can and prepare for it.”
“...Even in a situation like this, you’ve got a silver tongue.”
Jeok Cheongang said it with a sour expression, but he didn’t exactly argue with me.
With far more years behind him than I had, he must already have known it deep down.
What was going to happen would happen, one way or another.
And this wasn’t just a coincidence.

“If your consciousness and Jin Taekyung’s had been mixed together from the beginning... Damn it. I don’t know what to call him. Fine, if your consciousness and that good-for-nothing’s had been mixed together, wouldn’t that make sense?”
After a brief silence, I considered his question, then shook my head.
“I don’t think so. No, I’m sure that’s not it.”
“What makes you say that?”
“I had no memories at all when I first arrived. If our consciousnesses had merged, as you say, then at least some tiny memory should’ve remained. That’s the only way it would add up.”
I still remembered that time clearly.
When I first opened my eyes in the pleasure house, I didn’t even know Murim was another world rather than a virtual reality game.
I spoke with Wolhwa without knowing exactly who I was or where I was. That conversation was how I managed to learn even the bare minimum.
*And even that was so basic I had to lie to Jin Wikyung and tell him my memories were jumbled.*
If even the tiniest fragment of a memory had remained, I could’ve adjusted to this strange world much faster.
You know how it goes in web novels. The protagonist gets hit with a splitting headache, and a flood of memories comes rushing in.
But reality and fiction were worlds apart.
All I’d been given when I first set foot here was the same three-syllable name I’d had in the modern world.
And a body half-rotted from drink and women.
Now that I thought about it, that pissed me the fuck off.
Anyway, my conclusion was simple.
My consciousness and that of this world’s Jin Taekyung, who’d been nothing but a good-for-nothing, were completely separate.
No—they *had been* separate.
At least until today, before I had that strange dream.
“You’re so certain, so I’ll take your word for it for now. But the fact that the good-for-nothing’s memories appeared, even if only in a dream...”
His words trailed off.
Jeok Cheongang held my gaze, his expression grave. At last, he continued.
“Maybe some part of that good-for-nothing’s consciousness was inside you from the beginning.”
A groan escaped me before I could stop it.
It was one of the theories I’d been considering myself, but hearing someone else say it gave it a whole different weight.
*Damn it. What is this, one house with two families?*
There had been a time when I’d wondered about this, too.
It was after I’d spent a while living as Jin Taekyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan—more precisely, after I realized this strange world wasn’t a game but another reality.
Two worlds.
Two people who’d lived different lives under the same name.
Even if my head were made of Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron, it would’ve been only natural to wonder about it at least once.
If this body wasn’t a game character...
Then what had happened to its original owner?
His body was still here, so where was that good-for-nothing’s soul?
But at some point, I’d had to stop dwelling on it. Crises kept coming at me, one after another. I couldn’t afford to cling to a question I had no way to answer.
I’d simply assumed he’d disappeared the moment I took over this body.
Maybe whoever had made the piece-of-junk capsule that brought me here had thought that was the better outcome, too.
*But that wasn’t what happened?*
For once, I didn’t know what to say.
I rubbed my stomach, wearing an expression I couldn’t have described if I’d tried.
Jeok Cheongang watched me in silence until he finally spoke.
“I understand you’re feeling conflicted, but what the hell are you rubbing your stomach for? It’s not like you’re pregnant. You’re a hairy man, for crying out loud.”
“...I did it without thinking. Why do you have to put it like that?”
Was this the danger of media?
The moment I thought there might be something inside me, my hand had gone to my stomach on instinct.
*Must be a side effect of watching too many commercials about babies and toddlers,* I muttered to myself. Then I quietly moved my hand from my stomach to my chest and looked at Jeok Cheongang.
“Did something land on your chest, too? Are you all worked up, huh? Burning up with rage?”
“...I was just trying it out.”
“Fine, let’s say so. You went from your stomach to your chest. Where were you planning to touch next?”
“My head.”
Jeok Cheongang answered without hesitation.
“Don’t. You’ll look like an idiot.”
“Yes, sir.”
I was already starting to regret it. I snatched my hand back, and Jeok Cheongang let out a deep sigh.
“What’s wrong?”
“Seeing the way you carry on makes me worry.”
“About what?”
“From what I’ve heard, that good-for-nothing was a complete idiot. If he suddenly took over your body one day, I might not even notice.”
“Ah, because I’m just as much of an idiot?”
“Exactly. Nothing to add, nothing to take away.”
“Come on, that’s a little harsh. You’re hurting my feelings.”
“What are you going to do if your feelings are hurt? What can you even do? Hm? You...”
“Hey, why are you getting worked up all of a sudden? Calm down. Take it easy.”
Thankfully, Jeok Cheongang came to his senses at the last moment. He spoke calmly, as though nothing had happened.
“Anyway, keep discussing this with me. Do you understand?”
“I was planning to. Who else could I talk to about something like this, if not you?”
It wasn’t a choice. It was a necessity.
If I told people and even one word got out, I’d go from Divine Dragon to Mad Dragon in no time.

Jeok Cheongang believed me because of what he’d seen and experienced himself. But if the truth about me became known throughout the world, the orthodox faction’s chivalrous heroes would take numbers and line up to tear me apart for using unprecedented dark arts.
Who knew? Maybe I’d become the Lord of Heaven’s classmate as a public enemy of Murim.
But in response to my obvious answer, Jeok Cheongang shook his head.
“No. There’s one more person besides me. Have you already forgotten?”
“Who... Oh.”
I’d asked on instinct. Now I clicked my tongue.
Right. There was someone else.
Someone who wasn’t close enough for me to have a deep conversation with about something like this, but who was still somewhat near the truth.
*That’s right. The Bow Saint.*
I was still a little wary of her.
No—not a little. Very.
*I have no idea what she’s thinking.*
The distance between us never seemed to shrink.
Even when we’d had several chances to talk at length while staying in the Imperial Palace, we’d never crossed the line she’d drawn.
An invisible wall stood between the Bow Saint and me.
No, she seemed to treat everyone that way. Whenever anyone tried to break through that wall and get closer, she quietly withdrew.
Like magnets with the same pole facing each other.
As if that were the answer.
*But the Bow Saint might know something. She knows at least part of the truth.*
She’d believed the outlandish contents of a letter and spent decades wandering the world in search of me—or, more precisely, the “chosen one.”

Aside from Jeok Cheongang, who was standing right in front of me, and the mysterious absolute being known as the Martial God, whose very survival was uncertain, the Bow Saint was unquestionably the right person to ask.
Of course, first she’d have to agree to talk.
“Old Master. Then, by any chance...”
Before I could finish, Jeok Cheongang guessed what I was about to say and shook his head.
“Meeting the Bow Saint right now isn’t possible. She still hasn’t returned from Hebei.”
“Hebei...”
“The situation hasn’t fully settled down. Even the Family Head of the Peng Family hasn’t been able to return yet, so it’ll probably take a little longer.”
Hebei. The Peng Family.
At the sound of those two words, something stirred in a corner of my chest.
Someone came to mind—someone who’d done his best for everyone until the very last moment of his life, then left.
“The Thunderbolt Saber King... Is he...?”
I had to force the question out.
“He’s gone,” Jeok Cheongang answered. Then he added, “He was smiling. So brightly I could hardly stand to look at him.”
“That’s enough. That’s all that matters.”
I nodded quietly instead of answering.
Then Jeok Cheongang left, and silence settled into the space he’d occupied.
A quiet that had finally come at long last—one I hadn’t felt in a very long time.
*Open System window.*
Ding.
A clear chime shattered the silence.

Then he added, “He was smiling.
So brightly I could hardly stand to look at him.”
“That’s enough.
That’s all that matters.”
I nodded quietly instead of answering.
Then Jeok Cheongang left, and silence settled into the space he’d occupied.
A quiet that had finally come at long last—one I hadn’t felt in a very long time.
*Open System window.*
Ding.
A clear chime shattered the silence.

chapters.title: Chapter 993
paragraphs: *Open System window.*
The moment I muttered that short command in my mind—
Ding. Ding. Diiiing!
A familiar, clear chime rang out, and countless holographic windows poured from the air as if a dam had burst.

**System** Sudden Quest, **Transmitting Internal Energy Across the Body**, completed successfully! Quest rewards have been issued! Your **internal energy** has increased dramatically! You have gained a large amount of **EXP**! You have received 20 bonus stat points! Level up! **Transmitting Internal Energy Across the Body** is a technique with such a low chance of success that no martial artist dares attempt it anymore. We commend your patience and audacity in succeeding at the process twice. You have earned the rare achievement **You Did That Twice. You Did That Twice.** Achievement rewards have been issued! You have gained a large amount of **EXP**! Your **Endurance** has increased dramatically!
The first things that caught my eye were the System messages announcing the completed Quest and earned achievement.
I’d only leveled up once, but the stat increase from successfully completing Transmitting Internal Energy Across the Body was enormous.
I skimmed the messages, then erased a dozen or so with a single wave of my hand. There were still more holographic windows I needed to check.

**System** Successfully absorbed the internal energy of the **Heavenly Power Demon**! Successfully absorbed the internal energy of the **Thunderbolt Saber King**! The nature of **Scorching Yang Qi** is changing. The new flame born deep within your body will burn fiercer and hotter than ever! He who conquers the great sea will look down upon the world, but he who climbs the peak closest to heaven will look down even upon the great sea. Congratulations! Your **Middle Dantian** has been fully opened! You have reached the **Supreme Peak** realm! Sudden Quest, **Bone Transformation**, has begun. You cannot refuse this Quest! Sudden Quest, **Bone Transformation**, completed successfully! You can now draw in and release qi with great freedom. Your Muscles and Bones, now perfect in themselves, even reject impure qi! You have earned the great achievement **Full-Body Plastic Surgery**! Quest and achievement rewards have been issued! All attributes have increased significantly! Open the **Status Window** to check the details. You have received 30 bonus stat points! You have gained a large amount of **EXP** and **Fame**! Level up!
As I read through the holographic windows pouring out one after another, only one thought came to mind.
*This is insane.*
Of course, I’d expected massive rewards.
The Thunderbolt Saber King, Peng Cheolhu.
The power that giant, who’d defined an entire era, had passed on to me at the cost of what little life he had left was just as pure as it was immense.
Even so, the rewards listed by the System went far beyond what I’d expected.
Two level-ups, a huge number of bonus points on top of that, and a boost to all my attributes.
*I’ll have to check the details to see just how much my attributes increased, but even so, if I add all this together...*
It wouldn’t be an exaggeration to say I’d gained more than ten levels in one go.
No, in practice, it was even better than that.
The stronger I got, the farther away my next level-up seemed. The EXP required rose exponentially with each level, but the huge number of stat points I’d just received as a reward was pure bonus.
*I’m in debt. Deep in debt.*
Even with all those incredible rewards, I felt conflicted.
Caught between joy and bitterness, I remembered the Thunderbolt Saber King smiling brightly as he said he would pass everything he had on to me.

And with him, I remembered all the victims who’d fallen at Eight Spring Gorge that day, when the chrysanthemums covering the mountain had turned red and the bodies of people and horses had piled up like mountains.
I etched one thing deep in my heart: these enormous rewards had been paid for with the lives of the dead.
*I’ll repay this debt... no matter what.*
I’d never been well-off, and debt had always been a miserable thing to me. But not this time.
I was looking toward the same place they were.
The day I finally paid it all back, the peace everyone wanted would arrive.
And to make that happen, I had to endure and overcome whatever hardships came my way.
I couldn’t collapse under my grief or settle for where I was. I had to keep moving higher, with no thought of giving up.
Toward the place I’d glimpsed while completing Transmitting Internal Energy Across the Body, hidden behind thick, billowing clouds.
Toward the sky above the summit.
*Right. The upper dantian.*
Of course, I knew it wouldn’t be easy.
I couldn’t even be sure whether the Three Saints, the greatest masters in the Central Plains, or Jeok Cheongang, who stood shoulder to shoulder with them, had opened their upper dantian.
*No, even if they’ve already reached that stage, there must still be differences between them.*
Everything had its proper order.
I’d widened a narrow stream into a vast sea. Now I had to climb a mountain peak that rose as if it would pierce the clouds.
Until now, I’d grown at a terrifying pace thanks to the System I’d gained by chance and countless fortuitous encounters. But even I had been stopped by the clouds.
I still couldn’t reach the absolute beings who looked down on the lower world from above them.
*What if I’d ridden that momentum and kept pushing forward back then?*
A pang of regret struck me.
But I already knew the answer.
*I would’ve failed. And the odds would’ve been very high.*
Trying to break through to the upper dantian in those circumstances wouldn’t have been a challenge. It would’ve been a gamble.
Even I, despite having fully opened my Middle Dantian and feeling an intense surge of elation, had instinctively understood the difference between courage and recklessness—and pulled back.
The more I thought about it, the more indescribably frustrating it felt. But looking at it objectively, it had been a very good decision...
*Wait.*
What was this feeling?
I furrowed my brow and thought back to the excruciating process of Transmitting Internal Energy Across the Body, then to the strange dream born of memories that weren’t mine.
But that wasn’t all.
The inexplicable déjà vu sweeping through me pointed to the trace of a memory worn away somewhere between the two.
“Decision. A good decision... I’m sure I heard that somewhere.”
My lips moved on their own. The voice that came out sounded unfamiliar, as though it belonged to someone else.
How much time passed?
I stared blankly into empty air, muttering the same words over and over like a man in a trance. At last, I recovered part of the memory I’d forgotten.
*Someone definitely said something like that. Not in reality, but inside my consciousness.*
My eyes stung. I’d forgotten even to blink.
After turning the thought over for so long, my head felt hot.
No—an invisible little awl was slowly burrowing into my mind.
A headache slowly spread through me.
But even as the pain made me wince, I kept searching my memory. I groped through the darkness for a tiny fragment hidden behind larger memories.
And finally—
I remembered.
I remembered realizing it wasn’t time yet and turning away from the upper dantian beyond the clouds.
Then, as I slipped into the world of No-self, someone’s words echoed faintly in my ear.
*That was a good decision. Just like back then.*
My eyes flew wide open.
Because I’d realized who the voice belonged to?
No.
Because an immense pain had suddenly struck me.
Hk.
I sucked in a breath on instinct. Clenching my teeth wasn’t enough; I squeezed my eyes shut, too.

The headache that had been slowly burrowing into my mind like an invisible awl had grown as huge as the long acupuncture needle the Medicine King Hall Master carried around like a prized weapon. Now it was tearing through my head.
*What the hell is this...!*
With my vision gone white, I flailed my limbs like someone on the verge of drowning.
Even then, I couldn’t let go of the one question still unanswered in my mind.
Who did that voice, which had rung out like a hallucination at the last moment, belong to?
Who could speak to me in a space inside my mind rather than in the real world?
*How? How could they do that?*
There was one thing I could be sure of.
The voice I’d heard belonged neither to Jeok Cheongang nor, least of all, to the Thunderbolt Saber King.
And aside from those two old martial-world veterans, no one else could have communicated with me then.
*Then who was it?*
I genuinely wanted to know. Even as it felt like my head was splitting open, I wanted to know.
Who owned that voice, and how had they approached me and whispered without any of us noticing?
At the same time, I wanted to ask:
How did you know me?
*Just like back then... That’s what they said. I’m sure of it.*
There was no doubt.
I didn’t know them, but they knew me.
I couldn’t say when or where we’d met, but today wasn’t the first time we’d encountered each other.
But...
*Why can’t I remember anything? Why?*
I remembered only what they’d said. I couldn’t distinguish the pitch or depth of their voice, or even their gender.
I couldn’t guess whether they were a woman or a man—or, if they were a man, how old they might be.
All I could vaguely recall was the sensation of that moment, dredged up at the cost of enduring that terrible headache.
*A strange familiarity.*
The voice seemed as unfamiliar as something I’d never heard before, yet faintly, peculiarly familiar.
And that was all I could recover.
Whoosh!
A flash of light exploded. The whiteness in my vision slowly receded, and my blurred sight began to come back into focus.
I let out the breath I’d been holding and realized that the pain, which had seemed as though it would go on forever, had finally ended.
And with it, the memory I’d been allowed to recover had reached its limit.
*Damn it.*
I stared silently at my fingertips, still trembling from the pain, then curled them into a tight fist.
Crunch.
The skin of my palm, now almost like iron after Bone Transformation, pressed taut against my sharp fingernails.
Perhaps it was the strange turmoil of my emotions.
At that very moment, the vast qi sleeping inside my body began to boil—
Ding.

**System** A new Quest, **Unknown Voice**, has been created. You cannot choose whether to accept this Quest. The Quest will proceed by force. Would you like to check the newly updated Quest information?
Unknown Voice.
I stared at the Quest title on the holographic window, then parted my tightly shut lips.
“Yes.”

chapters.title: Chapter 994
paragraphs: The System often—maybe even pretty frequently—sprang clues on me in the form of Quests without making clear what they meant.
Just like now.

**System Quest Unknown Voice** At some point, you became aware of the voice of someone whose identity you cannot determine. This may or may not be the first time this has happened, but one thing is certain. In the not-too-distant future, you may come face-to-face with the owner of that voice. May that meeting not be an unhappy one. **Grade:** None **Restriction:** Jin Taekyung **Objective:** Continue to survive (In progress) **Reward:** ??? **Failure:** ???
The moment I saw the translucent holographic window, only one thought came to mind.
*Here we fucking go again.*
What, would the screen go blue if it gave me a straight answer?
The whole description was vague, as if someone had hidden it in fog.
This wasn’t the first time I’d received a Quest like this, of course. That didn’t make it any easier to get used to.
But at the same time—
*It’s something I have to go through.*
As I knew from experience, the System wasn’t an answer sheet.
It was more like a signpost, pointing me in a direction and telling me what lay ahead.
Depending on my choices, the arrows on that sign might change. Sometimes, like now, I had to figure out what they meant.
So I read the words in the holographic window again and again, trying to work out what those Twenty Questions-style clues were hiding.
The last two sentences of the Quest description, in particular, caught my eye.
*I might meet the owner of that unknown voice? And in the not-too-distant future?*
Not too distant, huh.
Time was relative, so that was a pretty vague way to put it.
A year could feel long and distant to a little kid with a runny nose, but to a white-haired old man, it might pass in the blink of an eye.
I couldn’t guess how much time the System meant by “not too distant.”
A few days. A few months. Or... No. Even the System couldn’t be so shameless as to lump years together under that phrase.
*Days would be too soon, and years would be too long. A few months seems like the reasonable guess.*
Then what was that last line about the meeting not being unhappy?
And who on earth was the owner of that unknown voice—the person at the heart of this riddle of a Quest?
*Someone who could approach without me, the Thunderbolt Saber King, or even the Old Master noticing. Someone who could intrude into my own inner world.*
While Transmitting Internal Energy Across the Body was underway, the Thunderbolt Saber King and I had our hands full giving and receiving energy. But Jeok Cheongang was different.
He’d stood guard throughout that dangerous technique, every sense strained to its limit.
For someone to evade his notice and speak to me should have been impossible. He was a Supreme Peak master who now stood shoulder to shoulder with the Three Saints, beyond even the Ten Kings.
Well, strictly speaking, it wasn’t *completely* impossible.
*If they were the greatest assassin of all time, with a concealment technique unlike anything ever seen before—or a master at least two moves ahead of the Old Master...*
As far as I knew, only two people in the world could meet those minimum requirements.
The first was undoubtedly the greatest assassin of all time, but I couldn’t be sure they had any reason to do this—or that they could pull it off.
The other one was different.
A wonder of the world itself.
The sky looking down over this vast land alone. A being who, though human, had come to be called a god.
“...The Martial God?”
The two syllables slipped from my lips before I realized it. A shiver ran down my spine.
The Martial God. The Martial God himself?
*That can’t be right.*
It had been half a century since the Martial God disappeared.
He’d vanished as suddenly as he’d first appeared, and no one under heaven knew where he was now.
No one could even say for sure whether he was alive or dead.
Not even the Bow Saint, who’d found me through the letter he’d left behind.
And now he’d suddenly reveal his presence like this?
*No way.*
But realistically, the Martial God was the only person capable of what had happened today.
As far as I knew, he alone was an overwhelming presence beyond even the superhumans known as the Three Saints.
And perhaps I knew more about the truth hidden behind the Martial God than anyone else under heaven.
*If my guess is right...*
A thought flashed through my mind, and my heart began to pound.
I remembered the first deep conversation I’d had with the Bow Saint at the Imperial Palace. Amid the hectic days that followed, there had been one name I could only turn over in the back of my mind.
Now it filled my thoughts.
*Cheon Taemin.*
Another absolute being, existing beyond a distant space.
Just as the Martial God had fought the Heavenly Demon and restored peace, Cheon Taemin was a hero who’d saved humanity from the demon known as the Demon King Asmodeus.
I could still see him clearly in the Ares Guild’s restricted area, unconscious as if in a deep sleep, attached to a life-support system that combined Magic and science.
Over that image, I could faintly hear a woman’s voice.
“He left a message for the chosen one.”
“A message? What does that mean?”
“Divine strength. He said the chosen one should overcome the crisis with that divine strength and a Will like steel. Just as...”
That day, the Bow Saint had watched me with a deep, solemn gaze.
Then her voice had echoed faintly in my ears, like a distant refrain.
“Just as you did.”
I still remembered the shock I’d felt in that moment.
No—I’d remember it until the day I died.
I’d vaguely entertained the thought before, only to laugh at myself and shake my head. Then an unexpected piece of the puzzle had fallen into place.
Divine strength.
A strange power possessed only by the chosen one.
The supernatural ability that belonged to me now—and had belonged to the Martial God in the past.
If the message the Martial God had left the Bow Saint meant what I thought it did, it could mean only one thing.
*System user. Player.*
That was probably the Martial God’s true identity.

The truth hidden behind an unparalleled hero the likes of whom had never been seen before, and would never be seen again: a man who’d appeared out of nowhere, saved a world in turmoil, then disappeared.
But if that theory was true...
*Cheon Taemin and the Martial God can’t possibly be the same person.*
According to the capsule’s user manual, the System was a power granted to only one person.
The moment my thoughts reached that point, a headache struck.
Two heroes in different worlds.

Their actions were astonishingly alike. The more I learned about them, the more I found myself wondering whether Cheon Taemin or the Martial God might have had the same ability as me. Whether the two of them might even be the same person.
But now I didn’t know what to think.
What connection existed between the Martial God and Cheon Taemin? If they were two entirely different people, what truth were they hiding?
There was one thing I did know: how to resolve at least some of my doubts—and the headache still stabbing at my mind like a needle.
*I’m going back. Right now.*
That’s right.
The answer didn’t have to be found in just one place.
The modern world and Murim. In these two worlds connected by a power I couldn’t begin to explain, I had to find a clear answer to my question.
And right now was the perfect time.
I’d completed the important Quest concerning the crisis in Shanxi Province, and the Logout function it had blocked was available again.
*One month. Maybe two. That should be enough.*
Learning more about Cheon Taemin wasn’t my only reason to go back.
I also had to deal with the fallout from the Doppelganger incident, which had happened right before I last Logged In.
On top of that, the ominous words it had left behind before its Erasure hinted at more trouble to come. Even through the frantic days in Murim, they’d bothered me like a fish bone stuck in my throat.
*I’ll find out when I get back. Why the Doppelganger said those things. What it went that far for.*
Now that I’d made up my mind, there was no hesitation. I lay straight on the bed and pulled the covers up to my neck.
Even if I spent a couple of months in the modern world, only about three shichen would pass in Murim.

I didn’t know whose presence was hurrying toward me from somewhere far beyond the window, but by the time they reached my room, all they’d find was me already gone to the modern world—or rather, fast asleep.
*Logout.*
I slowly closed my eyes and gave the familiar command. The next moment, I realized something.
Some things in this world didn’t go the way you expected.
Bip-bip-bip!

**System** Logout failed! The System has rejected your Logout command! Error! Error! Due to a System error, the Logout function has been temporarily disabled! Unknown error! Temporary Maintenance has begun!
...What?
My eyes flew open, even though I hadn’t meant to open them.
But the System’s voice in my ears hadn’t changed. Neither had the dozens of error messages floating in the air. Confusion seized me.
*Logout rejected? Why on earth?*
This had never happened before.
No—it had, but only when I was in the middle of an important Quest. Even then, it hadn’t happened like this.
*System error? Temporary Maintenance?*
An update, sure. But I’d never heard of anything like this.
An error in the System, which had always been absolute? How could that be possible?
“What the...!”
A groan escaped me. I bit down hard and shouted over and over in my mind.
*Logout! Logout!*
But nothing changed.
Nothing at all.
The holographic windows that poured out with every command showed only the words “System error.” Faced with this unbelievable reality, all I could do was stare blankly and take it in.

sentences.text: The System often—maybe even pretty frequently—sprang clues on me in the form of Quests without making clear what they meant.
Just like now.
**System Quest Unknown Voice** At some point, you became aware of the voice of someone whose identity you cannot determine.
This may or may not be the first time this has happened, but one thing is certain.
In the not-too-distant future, you may come face-to-face with the owner of that voice.
May that meeting not be an unhappy one. **Grade:** None **Restriction:** Jin Taekyung **Objective:** Continue to survive (In progress) **Reward:** ??? **Failure:** ???
The moment I saw the translucent holographic window, only one thought came to mind.
*Here we fucking go again.*
What, would the screen go blue if it gave me a straight answer?
The whole description was vague, as if someone had hidden it in fog.
This wasn’t the first time I’d received a Quest like this, of course.
That didn’t make it any easier to get used to.
But at the same time—
*It’s something I have to go through.*
As I knew from experience, the System wasn’t an answer sheet.
It was more like a signpost, pointing me in a direction and telling me what lay ahead.
Depending on my choices, the arrows on that sign might change.
Sometimes, like now, I had to figure out what they meant.
So I read the words in the holographic window again and again, trying to work out what those Twenty Questions-style clues were hiding.
The last two sentences of the Quest description, in particular, caught my eye.
*I might meet the owner of that unknown voice?
And in the not-too-distant future?*
Not too distant, huh.
Time was relative, so that was a pretty vague way to put it.
A year could feel long and distant to a little kid with a runny nose, but to a white-haired old man, it might pass in the blink of an eye.
I couldn’t guess how much time the System meant by “not too distant.”
A few days.
A few months.
Or...
No.
Even the System couldn’t be so shameless as to lump years together under that phrase.
*Days would be too soon, and years would be too long.
A few months seems like the reasonable guess.*
Then what was that last line about the meeting not being unhappy?
And who on earth was the owner of that unknown voice—the person at the heart of this riddle of a Quest?
*Someone who could approach without me, the Thunderbolt Saber King, or even the Old Master noticing.
Someone who could intrude into my own inner world.*
While Transmitting Internal Energy Across the Body was underway, the Thunderbolt Saber King and I had our hands full giving and receiving energy.
But Jeok Cheongang was different.
He’d stood guard throughout that dangerous technique, every sense strained to its limit.
For someone to evade his notice and speak to me should have been impossible.
He was a Supreme Peak master who now stood shoulder to shoulder with the Three Saints, beyond even the Ten Kings.
Well, strictly speaking, it wasn’t *completely* impossible.
*If they were the greatest assassin of all time, with a concealment technique unlike anything ever seen before—or a master at least two moves ahead of the Old Master...*
As far as I knew, only two people in the world could meet those minimum requirements.
The first was undoubtedly the greatest assassin of all time, but I couldn’t be sure they had any reason to do this—or that they could pull it off.
The other one was different.
A wonder of the world itself.
The sky looking down over this vast land alone.
A being who, though human, had come to be called a god.
“...The Martial God?”
The two syllables slipped from my lips before I realized it.
A shiver ran down my spine.
The Martial God.
The Martial God himself?
*That can’t be right.*
It had been half a century since the Martial God disappeared.
He’d vanished as suddenly as he’d first appeared, and no one under heaven knew where he was now.
No one could even say for sure whether he was alive or dead.
Not even the Bow Saint, who’d found me through the letter he’d left behind.
And now he’d suddenly reveal his presence like this?
*No way.*
But realistically, the Martial God was the only person capable of what had happened today.
As far as I knew, he alone was an overwhelming presence beyond even the superhumans known as the Three Saints.
And perhaps I knew more about the truth hidden behind the Martial God than anyone else under heaven.
*If my guess is right...*
A thought flashed through my mind, and my heart began to pound.
I remembered the first deep conversation I’d had with the Bow Saint at the Imperial Palace.
Amid the hectic days that followed, there had been one name I could only turn over in the back of my mind.
Now it filled my thoughts.
*Cheon Taemin.*
Another absolute being, existing beyond a distant space.
Just as the Martial God had fought the Heavenly Demon and restored peace, Cheon Taemin was a hero who’d saved humanity from the demon known as the Demon King Asmodeus.
I could still see him clearly in the Ares Guild’s restricted area, unconscious as if in a deep sleep, attached to a life-support system that combined Magic and science.
Over that image, I could faintly hear a woman’s voice.
“He left a message for the chosen one.”
“A message?
What does that mean?”
“Divine strength.
He said the chosen one should overcome the crisis with that divine strength and a Will like steel.
Just as...”
That day, the Bow Saint had watched me with a deep, solemn gaze.
Then her voice had echoed faintly in my ears, like a distant refrain.
“Just as you did.”
I still remembered the shock I’d felt in that moment.
No—I’d remember it until the day I died.
I’d vaguely entertained the thought before, only to laugh at myself and shake my head.
Then an unexpected piece of the puzzle had fallen into place.
Divine strength.
A strange power possessed only by the chosen one.
The supernatural ability that belonged to me now—and had belonged to the Martial God in the past.
If the message the Martial God had left the Bow Saint meant what I thought it did, it could mean only one thing.
*System user.
Player.*
That was probably the Martial God’s true identity.

The truth hidden behind an unparalleled hero the likes of whom had never been seen before, and would never be seen again: a man who’d appeared out of nowhere, saved a world in turmoil, then disappeared.
But if that theory was true...
*Cheon Taemin and the Martial God can’t possibly be the same person.*
According to the capsule’s user manual, the System was a power granted to only one person.
The moment my thoughts reached that point, a headache struck.
Two heroes in different worlds.
Their actions were astonishingly alike.
The more I learned about them, the more I found myself wondering whether Cheon Taemin or the Martial God might have had the same ability as me.
Whether the two of them might even be the same person.
But now I didn’t know what to think.
What connection existed between the Martial God and Cheon Taemin?
If they were two entirely different people, what truth were they hiding?
There was one thing I did know: how to resolve at least some of my doubts—and the headache still stabbing at my mind like a needle.
*I’m going back.
Right now.*
That’s right.
The answer didn’t have to be found in just one place.
The modern world and Murim.
In these two worlds connected by a power I couldn’t begin to explain, I had to find a clear answer to my question.
And right now was the perfect time.
I’d completed the important Quest concerning the crisis in Shanxi Province, and the Logout function it had blocked was available again.
*One month.
Maybe two.
That should be enough.*
Learning more about Cheon Taemin wasn’t my only reason to go back.
I also had to deal with the fallout from the Doppelganger incident, which had happened right before I last Logged In.
On top of that, the ominous words it had left behind before its Erasure hinted at more trouble to come.
Even through the frantic days in Murim, they’d bothered me like a fish bone stuck in my throat.
*I’ll find out when I get back.
Why the Doppelganger said those things.
What it went that far for.*
Now that I’d made up my mind, there was no hesitation.
I lay straight on the bed and pulled the covers up to my neck.
Even if I spent a couple of months in the modern world, only about three shichen would pass in Murim.

I didn’t know whose presence was hurrying toward me from somewhere far beyond the window, but by the time they reached my room, all they’d find was me already gone to the modern world—or rather, fast asleep.
*Logout.*
I slowly closed my eyes and gave the familiar command.
The next moment, I realized something.
Some things in this world didn’t go the way you expected.
Bip-bip-bip!
**System** Logout failed!
The System has rejected your Logout command!
Error!
Error!
Due to a System error, the Logout function has been temporarily disabled!
Unknown error!
Temporary Maintenance has begun!
...What?
My eyes flew open, even though I hadn’t meant to open them.
But the System’s voice in my ears hadn’t changed.
Neither had the dozens of error messages floating in the air.
Confusion seized me.
*Logout rejected?
Why on earth?*
This had never happened before.
No—it had, but only when I was in the middle of an important Quest.
Even then, it hadn’t happened like this.
*System error?
Temporary Maintenance?*
An update, sure.
But I’d never heard of anything like this.
An error in the System, which had always been absolute?
How could that be possible?
“What the...!”
A groan escaped me.
I bit down hard and shouted over and over in my mind.
*Logout!
Logout!*
But nothing changed.
Nothing at all.
The holographic windows that poured out with every command showed only the words “System error.” Faced with this unbelievable reality, all I could do was stare blankly and take it in.
Actually, if I had to name one more thing I could do, it was let the person whose presence had drawn close to the door know that he was an unwelcome guest before he entered my room.

Anyway, I’m busy.”

Even on this, we’re of one mind.”
The next moment, the unwelcome guest opened the door without hesitation.

chapters.title: Chapter 995
paragraphs: Some conversations don’t need many words.
Especially when the matter is urgent.
That was true of my conversation with Jin Wikyung, who’d come to my room out of the blue. It lasted less than fifteen minutes.
But what he told me weighed as heavily as a massive boulder. As soon as he left, I called everyone together—the people who could help me bear that weight.
Rattle.
“Well, I’ll be damned. Live long enough and you see everything. Who’d have thought martial-world lowlifes like us would ever lay eyes on the Marquis of Shangshan?”
Namho tossed out the silly joke the moment the door opened, and I couldn’t help laughing.
For two reasons.
First, seeing Namho again—or rather, seeing all of them—felt good. Comfortable, too, as though it had been ages since we’d met.
Second, because Namho was sitting astride Taishan’s shoulders as though that were the most natural thing in the world. It was ridiculous.
“What are you doing?”
“What does it look like? Sitting.”
“I can see that. Why are you sitting *there*?”
“Easy. It’s incredibly comfortable. This fellow’s a real find.”
Namho smiled with the satisfaction of an inventor who’d made a world-changing discovery, then patted the top of Taishan’s head.
“What are you waiting for? Get inside.”
Taishan stood blankly in the doorway. He glanced off into the distance before answering.
“Taishan. Feet won’t move. Must be hungry.”
“What the hell are you talking about? The jerky you stuffed into your mouth barely fifteen minutes ago amounted to a whole calf.”
Apparently, the ride was pay-as-you-go.
And the mileage was terrible.
“Don’t remember. Hungry.”
“You bottomless pit...”
With a deep sigh, Namho pulled a piece of taffy from his sleeve and waved it in front of Taishan’s eyes.
“There. Will you move now?”
In that instant, Taishan’s eyes narrowed to razor-sharp slits.
“Just one?”
“Damn it. I’ll give you another as soon as we get back.”
“Three.”
“You little bandit. Not a chance. Two. That’s my final offer, so think carefully.”
Taishan’s resolve was beginning to waver when a voice sounded from behind his enormous body, ending the negotiations.
“Move. Now. Or I’ll personally stab each of you twice.”
“What, two stabs each aren’t enough? Should I make it three?”
Her voice was low and calm, which somehow made the warning more dangerous. Taishan swallowed hard and hurried into the room.
He even snatched the taffy Namho had been waving in front of him.
With the doorway finally clear, Ju Hwaran—the one who’d put an end to the rush-hour jam—strode toward me. She called out in a voice suddenly thick with emotion, as though nothing had happened.
“Young Master Jin! No, Benefactor! No, Pavilion Master!”
I was pretty sure I’d asked her several times to pick one.
It was funny, but her sudden change of attitude caught me off guard. While I floundered, her eyes filled with tears.
“I’m sorry I arrived so late during the last battle. You must’ve had such a hard time.”
Over Ju Hwaran’s shoulder, Sama Pyo stood like an invisible man and muttered to himself.
“I’d guess the enemies had a harder time.”
Song Ilseom, arms crossed and his willow-leaf saber tucked against his chest as always, nodded.
“Judging by the aftermath, he was a monster. The enemies were smashed to pieces.”
Jaw clenched, Ju Hwaran ignored the voices behind her and continued.
“Were you hurt? Are you all right now?”
Sama Pyo and Song Ilseom at least had some sense. They slipped away at the right moment instead of barging in like Hyuk Mujin.
“Come on, Young Lady Ju. Why ask how someone’s feeling when he went through Bone Transformation just the other day—”
A chill settled over the room.

I didn’t know what expression Ju Hwaran had on her face as she slowly turned around, but I saw terror spread across Hyuk Mujin’s face as his voice trailed off. I decided I’d go on living without ever finding out.

“Mujin, shut your blabbering mouth. Young Lady Ju, I’m fine. Completely fine, so please don’t worry. And Taishan, I have something important to say, so swallow that taffy before we start—oh, you’ve finished it already. Did you chew it, or drink it?”
With Taishan’s magic trick over—and me wondering whether taffy might actually be a liquid—I’d finally sorted out the traffic. Namho gave me an uneasy look.
“Something important, huh? For some reason, I already have a very bad feeling about this... Am I just being an old worrywart?”
“If only that were all.”
I wasn’t the one who said it.
The last guest, Jeok Cheongang, strode into the room and gave me a nod.
“Tell them what’s happening beyond Shanxi Province.”
His grave eyes told me he’d heard the same news I had.
I looked silently from one face to the next in the now-crowded room. At last, I spoke.
“Something troubling is happening in the west.”
“The west? Where in the west...?”
As expected, Namho was the first to react. His brow furrowed as he spoke, then his narrow eyes widened.
“Y-you don’t mean...?”
“Yes. The place you’re thinking of.”
I nodded, then spoke in a heavy voice.
The far western edge, the birthplace of the Heavenly Demon Divine Cult—called the Demonic Cult in the Central Plains—and now the home base of Dark Heaven. That accursed land.
“Xinjiang.”
A massive shock swept through the room like an invisible wave.
When did Murim—that other world within the world—and the martial artists who lived in it first come into being?
No one knew for sure.

Oral traditions passed down through the generations, along with the few surviving lines in records from the distant past, led many to claim that Shaolin Temple in Henan had begun Murim’s long history. In time, that became the accepted account.
Jeok Cheongang had told me something different while I was enduring grueling training on Mount Jiuhua.
“History is shaped and pieced together. People believe what they want to believe—whatever suits them.”

Back then, Jeok Cheongang had been suffering from the infirmities of old age, and he’d begun reminiscing more often. Or rather, I’d half-begged him to. I thought I’d read somewhere that recalling and revisiting old memories whenever he had time might slow the illness’s progression.
And among Jeok Cheongang’s vast store of knowledge were secret histories of Murim that few people knew.

“Light and darkness go hand in hand. The idea that martial arts were born in Shaolin, packed with fellows trying to become Buddhas, is absurd enough. But did you think no one would try to use such power for evil?”
“Are you saying...?”

“That’s right. According to records left by our sect’s forebears, the Demonic Cult came into being that way, too. No one knows exactly when, but it was probably around the same time as Shaolin Temple.”
Murim could only have become a mountain of sabers and a forest of swords because the age itself was so chaotic.
The Shaolin warrior monks learned martial arts to protect. Others, on encountering that astonishing power, learned martial arts to conquer the world.

“People of every stripe must’ve gathered from all directions, in droves. They used martial arts to wield such mysterious power that they hardly seemed human. Just imagine how astonished everyone must’ve been.”
There must have been only a few dozen of them at first.
The world around them was dark even in daylight. Having encountered a power like a great light, they soon became followers and spread in every direction.
They told others what they’d seen with their own eyes. When people refused to believe them, they took hold of their sleeves and led them to him.
To the man with that unbelievable power. To the leader who would protect them in this wretched age of chaos.
The followers grew to hundreds, then thousands, and finally a hundred thousand. Their leader declared himself the Cult Leader and a divine man sent by Heaven.
“That was the beginning of the Heavenly Demon and the Demonic Cult.”
Jeok Cheongang had also said that they probably hadn’t called themselves the Heavenly Demon or the Demonic Cult from the very beginning.
What mattered was that the first Heavenly Demon never conquered the world. He and his followers settled instead in a desert on the western frontier.
Over nearly a thousand years, they sometimes turned their blades on one another. After several divisions and reunifications, they brought about the Great Faction War, a calamity of enormous scale.
Throughout those long years, the scorching desert ruled absolutely by Fiends became a Land of Ruin that even Murim of the Central Plains couldn’t hope to challenge.
And so it remained, even now that a new shadow called Dark Heaven had fallen across it.
But...
“Something unprecedented is happening in *that* Xinjiang?”
A long silence had followed my brief account. Namho’s question finally broke it, and I nodded.
“That’s what I heard.”
“Where did the information come from?”
“Where do you think?”
I pointed upward. Namho let out a weary breath.
“The Murim Alliance... No, the Hidden Shadow Pavilion.”
“I heard they lost more than thirty elite agents. After their first and last messenger eagle, all contact was lost.”
“Damn it. Then there’s no room for doubt. How many enemies are we looking at?”
“That...”
Even I couldn’t bring myself to answer right away. Namho groaned at the look on my face.
“I see. The Hundred Thousand Demonic Disciples all over again.”
“Maybe more than that. At least, that’s what the information I received suggests.”
More important, these enemies would be far stronger and more terrifying than the Demonic Cult’s followers had been fifty years ago.
The desert no longer belonged to the Demonic Cult. It belonged to Dark Heaven.
They weren’t merely the successors of the Demonic Cult under a different name. They were a new group of followers, ruled by a power incomparably stronger and more dangerous.
*Could that be why Logout was suddenly blocked?*
The thought crossed my mind, but I shook my head.
No. That wasn’t it.
The Quest hadn’t appeared yet, because I hadn’t made my choice.
Now was the moment to make it.
“From this moment on, we’re heading west.”
Ding.
An alert sounded, announcing a new Quest.
